productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I honestly cannot recommend this phone at ALL!!!! I have broken down into numerous issues below:First for the positives: There are so few and far between... The included phone case is actually nice and works well, although is a fingerprint magnet. The screen can get nice and bright, and does have some decent clarity to it. The speakers are pretty good for as cheap as the device is. Honestly thats about it, now for the negatives...Performance: To say this thing is a potato would be an understatement. The UI is laggy and slow at the very least, sometimes crashing multiple times performing simple tasks. Asking it to the change the background on the home screen would cause a crash, accessing settings would cause a crash, and simply restarting the phone would cause it to be so laggy for up to 5 minutes before it would respond properly. Signal is not the greatest, very spotty at times and would go from 5 bars to none for no reason randomly.UI (Operating System): Crashes all the time, laggy, and contains a ton (and I mean a ton) of bloatware. I finally had to disable Blu's "app store" completely, as everytime I would remove apps, more would suddenly and randomly get installed. I got to the point where almost everything except Spotify was either removed or disabled, and the UI still could not run properly.Battery: Battery while it seems large, actually does not perform as well as similar sized batteries. After a full charge, the battery was already down to 72% within 30 minutes just from using Spotify, even after removing all the bloatware. Charging is not great, even hooked up to a PD charger (capable of 120watts), would take over half an hour to even gain 5%.Memory: While internal memory did seem okay, I did decide to opt into an MicroSD card, so that I could download songs via Spotify, that was a HUGE mistake. It would work, but upon rebooting the phone, or heck even walking away for 10 minutes, the SD would dismount or something and completely wipe the card. It actually destroyed 2 MicroSD cards, due to being corrupted so bad that even a computer could not get them to reformat. Also, as a side note, for some reason everytime the screen would switch off due to inactivity, the downloads would stop, weird i know!Overall: Destroys SD Cards, slow and laggy performance, slow charging, weak battery, slow download, spotty network at best. Does have Okay speakers and screen, but performance can't correct for that.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A good phone for the price but you must disable some apps
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's about as cheap a price as you can pay for an unlocked new smart phone, so you have to adjust your expectations for that. Given the price this phone performs excellently. Screen, battery life, camera,  and performance is all adequate. You probably won't be wanting to use the pictures the camera takes but it's perfectly acceptable for video calls. Yes there's frequent small lags on a phone this low end. I've used many low end androids over the years and they all have that issue. I don't expect to use this phone for more than a few months max, and it is a perfect fit for the short time I need it for. Again, don't expect to be wowd by anything for the price point, but it's all functionalFor the price I was almost willing to give it 5stars as the best unlocked, no carrier required phone for this price I've ever used. However it comes with some bloat ware apps that required downloading and system apps that I had to forcibly disable. That's why it's only getting 4 stars.A phone with such low powered performance and low storage shouldn't have to be pruned by the end user. Forced disabling of some apps will improve performance though so if you get this phone I suggest you disable these apps in your app settings immediately:AppServices, Google Partner Setup, Google Wi-fi Provisioner, Headlines, news., Private Compute Services.And uninstall any preloaded apps or apps that were forced to install before you were able to disable the above.Some above are disguised by name as necessary but they are just bloat ware.I'd suggest this phone for anyone wanting an android phone to hold them over until they get a proper phone. Or for any reason you'd want to quickly get a cheap burner phone for a few months. Well worth the 60USD price tag

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer Panasonic KX-TGD833M
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Panasonic KX-TGD833M 
Cordless Home Phone System with Easy Call Block 
Make working from home easier and stress-free by stopping nuisance calls in 1 step. Expandable to 6 handsets, the KX-TGD833M is equipped with Smart Call Block and other scam protection measures, 2-way recording, and features for day-to-day convenience. 
Automated Call Block + One-Touch Call Block 
Talk to people, not computers. Automated Call Block stops robocallers from getting through by prompting callers to press “1” to connect their call. Plus, you can easily block other unwanted callers (up to 1000 numbers) with the touch the Call Block button 
One-Ring Scam Alert 
Protect yourself from one-ring scams in the simplest way possible! When you return a one-ring call, KX-TGD833M first displays a confirmation screen to prevent nuisance callers. 
2-Way Recording 
Incredibly convenient 2-Way Recording ensures you will never miss important details in a call. Record your telephone conversations and replay later. Plus, the announcement of “Start Recording” at the beginning of the call effectively deters suspicious callers. 
Digital Answering System 
Missed a call? Get message notifications even if you're away from home, or retrieve messages easily from the handset; up to 17 minutes of record time. 
Hands-Free Functions 
Answer and talk on the phone without pain or fatigue in your hand or neck when you use your handset hands-free; set up as a home intercom system. 
Long Battery Life with Alert 
Up to 10 hours talk time & 5 days of standby on handset (in eco mode) and audible alerts and visual icons make sure you know when it's time to charge. 
Caller ID and Phonebook 
50-item Caller ID lets you check who's calling before picking up; make outgoing calls without having to dial manually using a 100-number phonebook. 
Bilingual Talking Caller ID 
Caller ID displays and announces in English or Spanish so you can know who is calling, even when you’re across the room (add'l phone service may be required). 
See and Dial Clearly 
Bright, large display on handset units makes it easy to see who's calling. And, a backlit keypad makes it easy to dial even in low-light situations.

Fantastic! If I'm not mistaken I bought this at a fraction of the cost because it probably was purchased by someone else who returned it and Amazon was offering it for about $50 something dollars. Well I'd never know because it was in its original packaging and it's brand new. I am so happy to be able to buy a corded/cordless home phone system and at such a good price. It's a Panasonic and my last system was too but it was totally cordless and it lasted me for about 10+ years. So I find this brand to be tried true and trustworthy. I am so happy with this purchase. I'd encourage people to keep a stationery phone in your place of residence. If your cell gets lost or stop working there's always your trusty land line.

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer KX-TGF975B
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
KX-TGF975B 
Cordless Home Phone with Advanced Call Block and Link2Cell 
Our most advanced call blocking phone to help stop nuisance calls before they happen, with 14,000 numbers pre-blocked and 1-step call block button for an additional 2K numbers, and Bluetooth cell pairing to make and receive mobile calls through your cordless handset. Expandable to 6 handsets. 
14,000 Pre-Blocked Numbers 
TGF975B helps block calls before they happen, with 14,000 pre-installed call block numbers as a robust line of defense against nuisance calls to keep your work and home life free from interruption. 
*Robocall database is supplied from YouMail Inc. 
A Landline Phone that Pairs with Your Cell Phone 
Pair up to 2 cell phones via Bluetooth with the base unit to make and receive mobile calls anywhere in the home through your cordless handset. The handsets alert you when your cell phone receives incoming calls and texts and allow you to make and receive mobile phone calls with landline clarity. 
Automated Call Block + One-Touch Call Block 
Talk to people, not computers. Automated Call Block stops robocallers from getting through by prompting callers to press “1” to connect their call. Plus, you can easily block other unwanted callers (up to 2000 numbers) with the touch the Call Block button. 
Bilingual Talking Caller ID 
Caller ID displays and announces in English or Spanish so you can know who's calling, even when you’re across the room (add'l phone service required). 
Long Battery Life with Alert 
Up to 10 hours talk time & 5 days of standby on handset (in eco mode) and audible alerts and visual icons make sure you know when it's time to charge. 
Answer Using Voice Command 
Answer and talk on the phone hands-free for incredible convenience that helps avoid pain or fatigue in your hand and neck. 
Digital Answering System 
Missed a call? Get message notifications even if you're away from home, or retrieve messages easily from the handset; up to 18 minutes of record time. 
One-Ring Scam Alert 
Protect yourself from one-ring scams in the simplest way possible! When you return a one-ring call, KX-TGF975B first displays a confirmation screen to prevent nuisance callers. 
2-Way Recording 
Incredibly convenient 2-Way Recording ensures you will never miss important details in a call. Record your telephone conversations and replay later. Plus, the announcement of “Start Recording” at the beginning of the call effectively deters suspicious callers.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent Replacement for My 17-Year-Old Panasonic Phones
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently replaced my 17-year-old Panasonic cordless phone system with the Panasonic KX-TGF975B, and I couldn't be happier with my purchase.The setup was straightforward, and the sound quality is excellent—clearer than my old phones ever were. I especially like having five handsets, which makes it easy to have a phone wherever I need one in the house.One of my favorite features is the advanced call blocking. With so many spam and robocalls these days, it's great to have a phone that helps filter out unwanted calls. The answering machine, Bluetooth Link2Cell feature, and scam alert functions are all thoughtful additions that make this system feel modern and convenient.After using Panasonic cordless phones for 17 years, I had high expectations, and this new system has exceeded them. If you're looking to replace an older cordless phone system or simply want a dependable home phone with excellent features, I highly recommend this model.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The landline phone system we had in our home worked fine however the problem was that we were constantly bombarded each day with Robo Calls  and all kinds advertising and junk spam phone call that were just never ending and very annoying to say the least.  I did quite a bit of research on Amazon on the new generation of phones that included anti spam technology and ultimately decided up this Panasonic phone system after going through all the product reviews.  I also liked the fact that it was made by Panasonic. The phone system I was replacing was also Panasonic and had served us well for many years so I have faith in the brand.  Setup and installation of the system was straight forward and easy enough and within 30 minutes I had the system up and running and set up.  I did have to read the instructions in order to set up my preferred preferences (voice message, ring volume, spam settings, etc) but I found the instructions very clear and easy to follow.  This phone allows  you to sync it with your cellular phones, which is a really nice option,  but I have no interest in this feature at the present time so I didn't bother with that, however I did read the instructions on how to do it and it didn't appear to be to complicated.  I may utilize the cell phone feature later.. I found the system to be visually attractive and of quality construction and the best part of all is that from the minute I activated the system the spam phone calls  immediately stopped.  It was like a miracle  We would receive no less that a dozen such annoying spam phone calls each day, sometimes two dozen. It's been 2 days now and we have not received even 1 such annoying call.  My wife and I are thrilled to say the least and if a spam call does slip through somehow all we have to do is simply press the "Block" call button and the phone and that number will never be able to call us again.  The system comes pre-programmed with an internal list of known spam callers and you can add your own numbers to that list if you need to simply by hitting the "Block" button.  Doesn't get any easier than that.  This is really a great system, I love it.  Its  spam blocking technology really works well and the amount of other features that the phone has is amazing.  If you're looking to replace your older phone system in order to avoid those annoying spam calls just order this system.... you will be very happy you did.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Flaw in the answering machine's LEDs (Model KX-TGF975B)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the Panasonic Cordless Phone System (Model KX-TGF975B) last fall, having always trusted Panasonic phones in the past. Unfortunately, after just a few days, both the answer on/off LED and the message indicator light stayed constantly lit, even when the answering machine was off and no messages were recorded.I initiated a warranty claim through Panasonics website right after Christmas, sending the 1st defective unit back (at my expense). The Warranty claims center sent me a second unit. Unfortunately, the same problem occurred a few days after I starting using the unit.So, I sent back a this 2nd unit (I had them send me a shipping label) and, wouldn't you know it, the same problem existed on this 3rd unit.I, again, emailed their Warranty claim center asking them to please test any unit they send to me before sending it so that we are sure that it works and requested another shipping label. They responded,"Hello,Please call technical support on this at 1 800 *** 7262 as these units you received are perfectly working items.ThanksThank you,Panasonic Consumer Product Support".Well, this was quite rude and it insinuated that I was doing something to break the unit to somehow make two led lights stay on. I don't even know how I would go about doing that. I made a video of the problem and called the number. The technician I spoke with said they weren't setup to test or repair the phones. He gave me a number to call Panasonic Support directly (apparently they were just a Florida-based warranty facilitators). No apology for the rudeness.I called Panasonic and spoke to two people. The second person said that they couldn't help but to call 1 800 *** 7262 for help. That was the company in Florida who had just given me Panasonic's support number!  Good grief.So, I sent back the 3rd unit (at my expense) and two weeks later received a 4th unit (it's now the end of February 2026). Again, same problem.This is a a $200 phone system that can't get the most basic indicators working correctly and chooses to use a warranty company that doesn't fix or even test or acknowledge issues with their devices. The warranty service was fast but completely ineffective.I've attached a video showing the Answer On/Off light staying on. The message light (triangle under the play button) isn't on before this video was recorded but comes on permanently within hours/days of the first light staying on.It's a shame that I cannot recommend this phone system as I've used Panasonic phones my entire adult life. It’s far too expensive to have this unfixable inherent design flaw. I’ve attached videos so you can see for yourself. Save your money and look elsewhere.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I would like to give this phone a "3+" star rating if I could.  The phone itself has many nice features included but it also has some "issues" you will have to deal with.  It is easy to set up and looks good on a desk in an office.Be aware that the manual that comes with it IS NOT complete.  It does not offer all the information you need about the phone.  If you want the REAL instruction/set-up manual go to the Panasonic help site and they will give you a free extensive instruction manual.  This is the complete manual that really is helpful.The screens are bright and easy to see as well as the numbers.  The buttons all "work" well with soft touch features.One BIG PROBLEM is that the phone WILL ring out of sequence with your other phones you have in your home.  I did ALL of the troubleshooting offered by Panasonic to no avail to correct this problem.  Also, I contacted my telephone service provider and they told me that some phones like these have this issue and really nothing could be done to correct it (the phone company did check all my service and lines and found everything in working order on their "end").The speaker on the base unit works well but voices sound sort on "tin-like" and there is no way to adjust the tone of the speaker; so this is another issue you might just have to live with.  I did call friends and ask them how I sounded from my end and they all told me I sounded fine.If you can "live with" the out of sequence ringing this phone should work well for you.  I decided to keep the phone because of the other features and because I have purchased Panasonic phones for many years and they overall work quite well.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very nice phone with lots of features
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this 5 handset phone to replace a similar, but very old, Panasonic 5 handset phone.  I was happy with the old phone, but some of the old handsets started to fail (no screen or keytone) and could not be remedied with new batteries or other troubleshooting steps.  So far, I'm very happy with this replacement.It was easy to install and setup.  Of course, the 99 page manual is a bit daunting, but it is actually comprehensive and understandable.  Keep it in a safe place since you may need to refer to it.Another reviewer mentioned they didn't like the wall mount.  It does stick out a bit more than my old phone, but it's fine.  I don't even notice the difference at this point.One initial oddity was that when an incoming call came in, I could hear a ring in the bedroom, but not elsewhere.  The Panasonic phones rang on the second ring.  Turns out that is a built in feature.  It's supposed to delay on the first ring in order to screen "one ring" calls.  It was an old conventional landline phone that rang on the first ring.  I turned off the first ring block so all phones now ring on the first ring.  It wasn't a big deal, just an oddity.I can't say for sure whether the 14,000 call block feature actually works.  But I don't get many robocalls anyway.  Some calls are identified by my provider as "spam risk", but I never answer those calls.  I may start adding them to the "call block" feature, although that may get tedious.One annoyance:  When listening to a recorded message on a handset (as opposed to the base unit), there is no "erase" option like on my old handsets.  When the message is playing you have to hit "pause" and then "menu."  That makes no sense.  Fortunately, there is a key shortcut - *4 - you can hit to quickly erase the message.I have not used the cell-link feature.  I'm not sure I see a need to answer my cell using a handset.  However, I may try it out at a later time.Overall, I'm very happy with this Panasonic phone system and hope it lasts as long as my prior Panasonic phone.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Ottimo equilibrio tra prezzo e prestazioni
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ho acquistato questo Samsung Galaxy A16 4G LTE con un obiettivo molto semplice: trovare uno smartphone che fosse concreto, affidabile nell’uso quotidiano e, soprattutto, con un rapporto qualità prezzo convincente. Dopo averlo provato per un po’, posso dire che la sensazione generale è stata proprio quella di aver fatto una scelta sensata. Non cercavo un telefono da far “notare”, ma un dispositivo che mi accompagnasse nelle attività di tutti i giorni senza darmi la percezione di aver speso più del necessario rispetto a quello che offre.La prima impressione è stata positiva già dal momento in cui ho iniziato a usarlo. Si capisce subito che si tratta di un prodotto pensato per chi vuole qualcosa di pratico, senza complicazioni inutili. Il fatto che sia un dual SIM, per me, è stato un elemento utile perché aggiunge flessibilità nella gestione delle due linee. Anche la presenza di 4GB di RAM e 128GB di memoria mi è sembrata una combinazione equilibrata per questa fascia, soprattutto se si cerca un telefono essenziale ma con un margine di utilizzo abbastanza tranquillo nella vita di tutti i giorni.Quello che mi ha convinto di più, però, è l’insieme. Non ho avuto la sensazione di trovarmi davanti a un prodotto costruito al risparmio in modo evidente, ma a un modello che cerca un buon compromesso tra dotazione e spesa. In questa fascia, per me, conta molto che il telefono risulti coerente con quello che promette, e in questo caso la sensazione è stata quella giusta. Non ho avuto aspettative irrealistiche, e proprio per questo sono riuscito ad apprezzarlo di più: fa quello che deve fare, in modo semplice e diretto, senza far rimpiangere scelte più costose se l’uso richiesto è quello normale di un utente non troppo esigente.Anche esteticamente, nella versione nera, mi è sembrato sobrio e adatto a chi preferisce un dispositivo discreto. Non è un telefono che punta a stupire, ma a essere utilizzato con naturalezza. Questo per me è un punto a favore, perché spesso si tende a cercare caratteristiche spettacolari che poi, nell’uso reale, non incidono davvero quanto un equilibrio generale ben riuscito. Invece qui ho avuto l’impressione di un modello pensato con un criterio pratico, e questo lo rende facile da consigliare a chi vuole un acquisto ragionato.Naturalmente, quando si sceglie un prodotto di questo tipo, bisogna anche essere onesti su ciò che ci si aspetta. Io non lo vedo come la scelta per chi cerca il massimo in assoluto sotto ogni aspetto, ma come una soluzione molto valida per chi dà priorità alla convenienza concreta. È proprio in questo senso che mi ha soddisfatto: non promette più di quello che può offrire, e anzi riesce a trasmettere una sensazione di ordine e coerenza che, per me, vale molto più di tante promesse generiche.Un altro elemento che ho apprezzato è la semplicità con cui entra nella routine quotidiana. Quando un telefono non complica le cose, il suo valore cresce, soprattutto per chi desidera usarlo senza doverci pensare troppo. In questo caso, la dotazione generale mi è sembrata ben calibrata per un utilizzo normale, e la memoria interna da 128GB dà una base interessante per chi ha bisogno di spazio senza voler salire su modelli più impegnativi. Anche qui, il punto non è stupire, ma risultare utile in modo concreto.In definitiva, per me questo Samsung Galaxy A16 4G LTE merita pienamente il voto massimo perché rappresenta bene l’idea di miglior rapporto qualità prezzo. Non lo dico in modo superficiale: lo dico perché, per quello che offre e per come si presenta nell’uso quotidiano, mi ha dato esattamente la sensazione che cercavo. È uno smartphone che consiglierei a chi vuole un cellulare affidabile, essenziale e ben bilanciato, senza inseguire il superfluo. Se l’obiettivo è fare una scelta intelligente, mi sembra davvero centrato.
Ich habe 89€ bezahlt und das Handy ist echt Klasse!Hat alles was man braucht und ein echtes Schnäppchen!

aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Panasonic KX-TGD864W 
Cordless Home Phone System with Link2Cell & Easy Call Block 
Make your experience of cell and landline calls more clear and free of interruption. Expandable to 6 handsets, the KX-TGD864W pairs with your cell phone to increase call clarity and range, with Smart Call Block and other scam protection measures to stop nuisance calls. 
Link2Cell Technology 
A Landline Phone that Pairs with Your Cell Phone 
Pair up to 2 cell phones via Bluetooth with the base unit to make and receive mobile calls anywhere in the home through your cordless handset. The handsets alert you when your cell phone receives incoming calls and texts and allow you to make and receive mobile phone calls with landline clarity. 
Automated Call Block + One-Touch Call Block 
Talk to people, not computers. Automated Call Block stops robocallers from getting through by prompting callers to press “1” to connect their call. Plus, you can easily block other unwanted callers (up to 1000 numbers) with the touch the Call Block button 
One-Ring Scam Alert 
Protect yourself from one-ring scams in the simplest way possible! When you return a one-ring call, KX-TGD86X first displays a confirmation screen to prevent nuisance callers. 
Digital Answering System 
Never miss a message with the answering system with 18 minutes of record time; easy-to-read message counter lets you know when messages are waiting. 
See and Dial Clearly 
Bright, large display on handset units makes it easy to see who's calling, and a backlit keypad makes it easy to dial even in low-light situations. 
Hands-Free Functions 
Answer and talk on the phone without pain or fatigue in your hand or neck when you use your handset hands-free; set up as a home intercom system 
Long Battery Life with Alert 
Up to 10 hours talk time & 5 days of standby on handset (in eco mode) and audible alerts and visual icons make sure you know when it's time to charge. 
2-Way Recording 
Incredibly convenient 2-Way Recording ensures you will never miss important detailsin a call. Record your telephone conversations and replay later. Plus, the announcement of “Start Recording” at the beginning of the call effectively deters suspicious callers. 
Bilingual Talking Caller ID 
Caller ID displays and announces in English or Spanish so you can know who's calling, even when you’re across the room (add'l phone service required).

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great phone...but compared to what?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Tldr: Good phone for this price, noticeably better than older A13 and I wish more people would include context to their reviews. Glad I bought mine.I'm leaving a long and detailed review because I got tired of reading through reviews that seemed contradictory, or said something was "bad" but without any context. If I made a poor choice buying a phone I'd likely be stuck with it for some years. I'm hoping this helps others like myself who are reading the reviews.Ok, so the most important context is what phone I'm coming from over to the A17 5g. My old phone was Samsung A13 5g. My opinions of the new phone will be largely based on how they compare to the previous phone I used. So it's budget phone to budget phone, with the A17 having approximately 3-4ish years newer tech (or same tech but cheaper.) Both phones are being used on metro PCS (T mobile) network.So I've now had the A17 for exactly one week. I primarily use my phone for android auto, text, checking email, web browser, occasional YouTube and maybe once per week on some games. I don't use it for heavy loads like massive file transfers or rendering video. It's fairly light use overall.So far, the things I've been most pleased with are the screen and software/system layout. The screen has decent color and brightness and is MUCH better than the A13. Both screens claim to run at 90hz but the change from the old 270 PPI (I believe stands for pixel per inch or some equivalent) to 385 PPI feels massive. Much cleaner image from text to images. The change from LCD to AMOLED gives much better contrast with deeper colors. The software and system layout are a bit harder to describe in detail. It's more of a personal/ascetic preference. Things look and feel a lot cleaner. There are added optional features like side slide tabs to house shortcuts for certain apps. Another feature is top down swipe from the right for system shortcuts and from the left for notification, so they are smashed together.Another improvement, though less so than the screen and software changes, is in the speed and responsiveness of the phone. This one also needs to be put in context a bit. I'm sure some would complain about it while coming from a more expensive and technologically superior phone. I have my own bias, as I'm coming from an inferior phone which had over 3 years of use (slowing it down over time.) I also use it for mostly light tasks. That being said, I am pleased that the phone is noticeably more responsive than my old one. Most of the lagging happens on start up (goes away after a few mins while the phone is connecting a bunch of apps and putting out/requesting info like date/time/location.) When I booted it for the first time, that was the worst lag I had. It will also slow down if you have several apps running at the same time.  I feel like that's obvious, but some people genuinely don't know that if you hit the home button to leave an app, you need to bring up multi view and actually swipe the box away to close it fully. If you never close apps and never restart your phone on occasion it WILL slow way down. While using the phone for max 1 or 2 things at time it runs perfectly fine, and is better than the A13.Battery life is good. I went from appx. 5000mAh to 5000mAh phones, so besides the slight degradation in the old phones battery life it should be the same. 5000mAh for my uses feels excellent overall. It can go for a full 2 days without charging. Charging speed itself seems improved, but that's never mattered too much for me so I can't comment much. Seems fine though, roughly 1.5h charge from mostly dead to full. That's using a 25w fast charger block and appropriate USB c cable. I didn't use the cable that came with the phone so I can't comment. It didn't come with a charger block, by design. Your mileage on charge speed will vary based on what you're using to charge the phone with. The phone can't charge at full speed if you're using a 5w charger from 15 years ago.I don't have much to say about the camera. I rarely take photos and when I do it's usually quick snap shots of paper instructions or to share location. I believe (though I'm not sure) the A13 was also 50mp front camera but either the the other 2 lenses have been upgraded or they improved the camera software, because pictures do look a bit cleaner. It's not night and day or anything, but it looks better to my eye. Camera is also faster to adjust light and contrast when first focusing on a object, as compared to the old A13.Build quality seems a little improved. They are both budget phones and how build quality "feels" is inherently subjective but to me it does seem a little better.A quick note on activating this new phone...this may only be an issue I personally had, but in case this helps someone else I'd like to include it. I had a bit of trouble switching my physical SIM card out of my old phone and into the new. The metro app was telling me the phone wouldn't be compatible unless I changed phone plans (which is BS.) I had to call customer service and they opted to use the eSiM feature, rather than swapping the physical Sim. I noticed they also used the new phones 2nd SIM number to activate it, while i had tried using first. If you're having trouble perhaps check the phones info from the settings menu, and then try eSIM activation using the 2nd address. It worked fine for me after this.Samsung has a quick transfer feature if your previous phone was a Samsung. It basically copies over everything from your old phone, including apps, pictures, contacts and even text message history ect. It took 3 or 4 attempts (it didn't want to connect and dropped the connection once at 30% complete.) Luckily if it disconnects part way through, it will pick up where it left off, without needing to restart. Once it finally had a stable connection it took me about 6 minutes, it will vary based on how much stuff you have to move over. You need to download an app to do the transfer, but it will prompt you and take you to it's link.Summery: I find it pretty impressive how nice this phone feels both compared to its older model and for its price point in general. I found it frustrating that people would say this part or that was crap or great, but without giving any context to what they based that opinion off of. In my opinion, based on how cheap this phone is and compared to its older model (A13) this is an awesome phone so far, being one week in. Screen is a big improvement, system software and layout is better (IMO) and they seem to be making incremental improvements to things like the camera and overall build. For this price point I find it really impressive what you actually get. If you're coming from an older mid range phone I expect it will either be inferior or about the same. If you're coming from another phone in the 200 range it should be decent to good. For less than 200 and for what I use it for though, I'm very happy I bought this phone.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this to replace a Samsung A50 that was purchased in October 2019. Yes, 2019! That's before the world changed forever due to a pandemic. And that alone should tell you how infrequently I change phones and what my priorities in life are. I'm a simple woman with simple needs.There wasn't anything really wrong with my old phone but t unfortunately I cracked the screen and it was almost as much to fix it as it was to get a new one. So since it was practically a dinosaur I chose to "upgrade" and decided to take the chance on getting this model after doing a lot of research. I didn't want to spend a lot of money because I mainly use my phone for basic tasks, talking, texting, etc. I don't do any gaming, heavy streaming or lots of downloading. At most I'll watch a YT video or scroll sparingly on SM if time permits.It arrived quickly and came unlocked as described. That's about it for positive feedback. It was really surprising to me that this phone didn't perform nearly as well as it's almost 7 year old predecessor. Let's start with the fact that it took over 4 hours to do a transfer at the mobile store. Then I learned I really didn't have enough storage so a lot of my texts didn't transfer over. The next thing is I keep running out of space and have to keep deleting photos & videos. Now keep in mind these are the same photos from my old A50. I also have almost the same specs on this phone as there is on the A50 so I don't understand why this is happening.Yes, I know things change but I'm not a fan of the new texting features. They're so annoying, especially auto-correct and the "typing" bubble like the iPhone. And I don't find this to be very intuitive so I have trouble changing certain features easily. I have to dig and dig to find what I need.The UI (?) updates are constant and very annoying. Internet pages or tabs will close or switch for no reason and the phone is also laggy as heck. For example, sometimes it takes at least 4-7 seconds to capture a screenshot. Or at times there's a long delay to move from one part of an Internet page to another. What's crazy is I'm not the type of user who requires everything on my phone to move at the speed of light. I can accept a delay here or there but it's a constant waiting game with this phone. And don't get me started on how terrible the camera is. I absolutely despise every picture this camera takes and selfie are the worst! They have everyone looking haggard as heck, no matter what the setting. My A50 camera was 1000x better than this and I could always find a way to take a flattering photo.When I initially read all the negative reviews (and I mean ALL) I incorrectly assumed some of complaints were from folks who were used to swapping out their $2K phones every year. They had high standards and this is a low budget phone so they were disappointed. I get it. It's hard to enjoy beer when you have champagne tastes. But I was quite mistaken. A lot of the complaints are very valid and quite accurate.If you're looking for quality on a budget this ain't it. Trust me. This phone is probably best for a 10-year old child. Take it from someone with super low standards and who kept their own phone for an actual child's formative years. I'll keep it because I don't want to spend more money right now but do yourself a favor and keep your expectations low. If you need a high performance phone look elsewhere. I wish I did.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice Phone for Money, but Not Necessarily for Seniors
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was impressed with this phone on unpacking, and liked the compact handset and functionality. I had purchased it for my mother who has dementia and is hearing impaired. She had been trying out one of the picture phones, but the sound was totally deficient considering these are made for the elderly (check this feature out carefully if you are buying one). I thought this Panasonic phone would be simple enough to use and provide the decibel level we were missing with the picture phone.The interesting thing I learned in trying to teach her how to use this phone is that we basically need to relearn how to use a cordless landline phone, as many of us haven’t used one in over 20 years now. Most elderly innately understand the original corded handset that you hold to your ear and replace in the base to disconnect. Where the cordless landline is more similar to a cell phone (which my mom had been using for the past 15 years or so), there are some key differences that are critical to the proper usage of this phone. Primarily, the phone line must be disconnected at the end of the call. That requires the user to tap the OFF button or replace the handset in the base. One party can disconnect a call on a cell phone, a landline requires both to disconnect. This can be dangerous for seniors who fail to end the call properly, and leave the line open.  You can’t text them and tell them it’s off the hook either!  Secondly, placing a call requires two steps as opposed to one. Even the “Favorites” button (which ideally would be labeled) covers ALL “favorites”, so requires multiple button presses to reach the desired party. I was the only Favorite designated on my mom’s phone, but it still required two taps to make the connection.  As an aside, even though I advised my mom that there were essentially only three buttons she needed to know, the busy display and sheer number of buttons and labels was likely overwhelming to her.Our tests with the Boost feature didn’t seem to be too successful, as the only step we took that made the calls clear enough for her was using the speaker phone. I personally would have labeled the speaker phone “Speaker” rather than “Sp Phone”, as I think the former is more recognizable terminology.  I also think the speaker should be a major button, not a minor one in terms of size as it is so commonly used.  Likewise, I think “END” would be clearer than “OFF”, but these are just my opinions.Because I did not get to utilize many of the other features, I withheld a star from my rating, but that does not indicate any disappointment with the phone’s performance. If I had a landline, I would love this phone and even debated keeping it for myself.  I think it is well-designed and while not necessarily configured intuitively, it still packs a lot of functionality into one compact phone. The ability to purchase it with multiple handsets is a big plus.  In summary, my only issue with the phone was its potential unsuitability for a senior, particularly one with hearing or cognitive impairment. Otherwise, it’s a good phone for the money.Footnote - Panasonic gets extra points for including a diagram on the top flap of the outer box on how to repack the phone. This packaging was an engineering feat on its own, and repacking it in the same configuration would have been impossible without the diagram!

It’s a shame more isn’t done to lock this down.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Many eye saving features.  Best phone I have had.  No bloatware.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am very impressed with this phone.  Unlike many other brands this phone has no bloatware no games no unwanted apps included with it. I love the map I love the matt and semi shielding from off center viewing is great.  Although not really paperwhite, two screen modes mimic this well.  A slide switch is provided on the side where you can alternate between screens. Their are 4 different screens available and you can alternate between the normal color screen and either of a muted color, B&W, or a limited function BW version for long reading sessions.As it came it was set up with gesture mode which I did not like.  Easy to change into the familiar 3 button mode in settings.You can also activate a small grey handle on a side to pull out useful stuff on top of apps, like a note taker, or several other productivity enhancementsThe pull-down menu from the top is greatly enhanced from that on my previous pixel or Samsung phone. It gives you information such as status of connections on the top line followed by a plethora of buttons that you can customize the order of. Very helpful.I have had no issues with the speed of this phone, or any of its functions. It is a pleasure to use, and I love the eye strain reducing features. For under $200 I highly doubt this could be beat by anyone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A GREAT VALUE PHONE PACKED WITH INNOVATIVE FEATURES BUT ONE BAD APPLE RUINED IT
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So let me start by saying this. I bought 2 of these on seperate times. One in April of 2026 and then recently in June of 2026. So the first one I bought I loved it. Great phone love the paper like screen features of the phone.  For a $200 budget phone it was so good that I actually started using this phone as my main phone instead of my Motorola Razr+. Great size, great features, and you can actually make the screen like paper. As for the features and specs just look at the product description on Amazon. Great phone great camera. Now for the reason I returned this 1st phone. Unfortunately I switched carriers from T-Mobile to Spectrum a week after I bought this phone.  And this phone is not compatible Spectrum. So I ended up returning it.  Now like I said I love the phone so much that even after Spectrum gave me a new phone a Samsung S25 FE I was not happy with the phone. So I ordered another TCL 60 Nxtpaper.  So I used the TCL as the main phone and stopped using the S25 FE. So after about 3 weeks into using the phone as a daily use. One night I decided to transfer my pics that I took with the phone and also to put some other pics into the phone. So here is the problem with this 2nd TCL phone. It won't file transfer when you connect to your laptop. When you transfer files to the SD card thru a USB cable it pauses and just stands there at 25% or whatever it stops at whatever percentage it decides to stop working. Same thing with transferring files thru USB cable to internal storage of the phone it gets worse not only does it stall at a certain percent it will disconnect itself from the  connection. The phone shuts down and the laptop will flicker and restart. And when that happens it won't read the phone or the connection so the laptop and the phone needs to restart. So after a couple of nights of this frustration. I decided to return the 2nd phone. I gave it 4 stars because the phone is a good phone great features and value priced.  One star off for one bad apple in a bunch.  Great phone overall.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Ottimo equilibrio tra prezzo e prestazioni
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ho acquistato questo Samsung Galaxy A16 4G LTE con un obiettivo molto semplice: trovare uno smartphone che fosse concreto, affidabile nell’uso quotidiano e, soprattutto, con un rapporto qualità prezzo convincente. Dopo averlo provato per un po’, posso dire che la sensazione generale è stata proprio quella di aver fatto una scelta sensata. Non cercavo un telefono da far “notare”, ma un dispositivo che mi accompagnasse nelle attività di tutti i giorni senza darmi la percezione di aver speso più del necessario rispetto a quello che offre.La prima impressione è stata positiva già dal momento in cui ho iniziato a usarlo. Si capisce subito che si tratta di un prodotto pensato per chi vuole qualcosa di pratico, senza complicazioni inutili. Il fatto che sia un dual SIM, per me, è stato un elemento utile perché aggiunge flessibilità nella gestione delle due linee. Anche la presenza di 4GB di RAM e 128GB di memoria mi è sembrata una combinazione equilibrata per questa fascia, soprattutto se si cerca un telefono essenziale ma con un margine di utilizzo abbastanza tranquillo nella vita di tutti i giorni.Quello che mi ha convinto di più, però, è l’insieme. Non ho avuto la sensazione di trovarmi davanti a un prodotto costruito al risparmio in modo evidente, ma a un modello che cerca un buon compromesso tra dotazione e spesa. In questa fascia, per me, conta molto che il telefono risulti coerente con quello che promette, e in questo caso la sensazione è stata quella giusta. Non ho avuto aspettative irrealistiche, e proprio per questo sono riuscito ad apprezzarlo di più: fa quello che deve fare, in modo semplice e diretto, senza far rimpiangere scelte più costose se l’uso richiesto è quello normale di un utente non troppo esigente.Anche esteticamente, nella versione nera, mi è sembrato sobrio e adatto a chi preferisce un dispositivo discreto. Non è un telefono che punta a stupire, ma a essere utilizzato con naturalezza. Questo per me è un punto a favore, perché spesso si tende a cercare caratteristiche spettacolari che poi, nell’uso reale, non incidono davvero quanto un equilibrio generale ben riuscito. Invece qui ho avuto l’impressione di un modello pensato con un criterio pratico, e questo lo rende facile da consigliare a chi vuole un acquisto ragionato.Naturalmente, quando si sceglie un prodotto di questo tipo, bisogna anche essere onesti su ciò che ci si aspetta. Io non lo vedo come la scelta per chi cerca il massimo in assoluto sotto ogni aspetto, ma come una soluzione molto valida per chi dà priorità alla convenienza concreta. È proprio in questo senso che mi ha soddisfatto: non promette più di quello che può offrire, e anzi riesce a trasmettere una sensazione di ordine e coerenza che, per me, vale molto più di tante promesse generiche.Un altro elemento che ho apprezzato è la semplicità con cui entra nella routine quotidiana. Quando un telefono non complica le cose, il suo valore cresce, soprattutto per chi desidera usarlo senza doverci pensare troppo. In questo caso, la dotazione generale mi è sembrata ben calibrata per un utilizzo normale, e la memoria interna da 128GB dà una base interessante per chi ha bisogno di spazio senza voler salire su modelli più impegnativi. Anche qui, il punto non è stupire, ma risultare utile in modo concreto.In definitiva, per me questo Samsung Galaxy A16 4G LTE merita pienamente il voto massimo perché rappresenta bene l’idea di miglior rapporto qualità prezzo. Non lo dico in modo superficiale: lo dico perché, per quello che offre e per come si presenta nell’uso quotidiano, mi ha dato esattamente la sensazione che cercavo. È uno smartphone che consiglierei a chi vuole un cellulare affidabile, essenziale e ben bilanciato, senza inseguire il superfluo. Se l’obiettivo è fare una scelta intelligente, mi sembra davvero centrato.
Ich habe 89€ bezahlt und das Handy ist echt Klasse!Hat alles was man braucht und ein echtes Schnäppchen!

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer Panasonic KX-TGD832M
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Panasonic KX-TGD832M 
Cordless Home Phone System with Easy Call Block 
Make working from home easier and stress-free by stopping nuisance calls in 1 step. Expandable to 6 handsets, the KX-TGD832M is equipped with Smart Call Block and other scam protection measures, 2-way recording, and features for day-to-day convenience. 
Automated Call Block + One-Touch Call Block 
Talk to people, not computers. Automated Call Block stops robocallers from getting through by prompting callers to press “1” to connect their call. Plus, you can easily block other unwanted callers (up to 1000 numbers) with the touch the Call Block button 
One-Ring Scam Alert 
Protect yourself from one-ring scams in the simplest way possible! When you return a one-ring call, KX-TGD830 first displays a confirmation screen to prevent nuisance callers. 
2-Way Recording 
Incredibly convenient 2-Way Recording ensures you will never miss important details in a call. Record your telephone conversations and replay later. Plus, the announcement of “Start Recording” at the beginning of the call effectively deters suspicious callers. 
Digital Answering System 
Missed a call? Get message notifications even if you're away from home, or retrieve messages easily from the handset; up to 17 minutes of record time. 
Hands-Free Functions 
Answer and talk on the phone without pain or fatigue in your hand or neck when you use your handset hands-free; set up as a home intercom system. 
Long Battery Life with Alert 
Up to 10 hours talk time & 5 days of standby on handset (in eco mode) and audible alerts and visual icons make sure you know when it's time to charge. 
Caller ID and Phonebook 
50-item Caller ID lets you check who's calling before picking up; make outgoing calls without having to dial manually using a 100-number phonebook. 
Bilingual Talking Caller ID 
Caller ID displays and announces in English or Spanish so you can know who is calling, even when you’re across the room (add'l phone service may be required). 
See and Dial Clearly 
Bright, large display on handset units makes it easy to see who's calling. And, a backlit keypad makes it easy to dial even in low-light situations.

A light on the top of the handset flashes when the phone rings, signaling an incoming call. With the ringers muted, this visual indicator can let you know the calls in silence. Also helpful for those who are hearing impaired. 
Audio Assist button instantly increases incoming call's volume and enhances sound frequencies to make speech easier to understand. It is easy to use, just one press on the Audio Assist button on handset. Press again to turn off. 
2" backlit display on handset with high contrast text makes it easy to read incoming caller ID or call history records. Plus, the lighted handset keypad allows for easy dialing in low light conditions. 
With the full-duplex speakerphone on the handset, this phone set not only lets you speak hands-free but also allows both ends to speak and be heard at the same time. Enjoy conversations that are more true to life. 
Stay informed even when you are away from home. All calls are routed to the built-in digital answering machine when necessary, recording key messages for you. 
Screening calls has never been easier. The handset announces the name of the caller, so you don't have to scramble for the handset to see who's calling. 
Experience the best in long-range coverage and clarity, provided by a unique antenna design and advances in noise-filtering technology. 
What's a Smart Call Blocker? 
A simple one-time setup to filter unwanted calls while letting trusted ones through. 
Quick Setup to let the system working for you 
Set Directory - for your family so their calls will go through without the screening. 1. Press MENU on handset. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Directory, then Select. 3. Press Select again to choose Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then Select. 
Set Allow list - so their calls do not get through the screening. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow list, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter telephone number, then Select. 5. Enter name, then Select. 
Set Block List - to prevent their calls from ringing through. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Block list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then press Select. 
Set Star name list for your trusted organizations - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Star name list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the name (up to 15 characters), then press Select. 
Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have never WANTED to leave a review for anything but in this instance, I had to. I followed the instructions for set-up, followed instructions for blocking. There are levels to the blocking: you choose what works for you. Then I added family and friends numbers to the directory. It worked like a charm!!! Only calls from numbers in the directory are coming through! I love it! No more spam calls, no more unavailable calls, no more private calls!Now when I checked the phones, I did see the blocked calls in the call history, but they were silenced and did not bother my relative.I asked for three days straight if they had gotten any spam calls........NO!!!So if you are looking for a way to block those unwanted calls, I totally believe in these phones.Yes, I read the comments. Even with the negative comments, I was willing to take th chance and I'm glad I did. Money well spent!!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: With caller ID, call blocking works great
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the AT&T BL102-4 cordless phone set from the Amazon Warehouse (like-new used in original packaging)  when our family switched from a traditional landline setup to a VOIP landline with our local cable provider.  We previously had been using a cordless system from another brand with our phone company's service and the call quality was never good - often lots of crackle on the line, making callers hard to hear.  I wasn't sure if it was the phones, the service, or the cords, so I replaced all of them and started anew.The build quality of this AT&T phone system was a little less substantial than I expected, but the phones do their job and call quality is good.  The handsets and the base feel kind of cheap, but this is an under-one hundred dollar phone system so I guess that's to be expected.  It works well though, and the features are good.The only feature I miss is Bluetooth.  If this system had it  I could pair it with my cell phone, but other than that, it's not missing anything.----------------------------------➡️  SETUP & USE:I put the batteries in the phones and charged them as I went to the included user manual to try and figure out how to set it up.  The manual is a bit overwhelming, but if you read it carefully and go step by step, you can figure it out.Some features on the phone duplicate those offered by my cable company, so I did need to figure out which ones to set up and which ones to leave off on the phone.  For example, my cable provider offers voicemail, and thus using the answering machine feature of this phone system isn't something that I do.Once I set up things like the number of rings before the calls were answered, I started adding numbers into my phone's contacts.  Doing this let these callers come right through, and helped with call blocking.  I set it up so that callers I didn't recognize would have to press the pound button on their phones to get through.  This eliminates robocalls, but real-live telemarketers can still get through.---------------------------------------➡️ CALL BLOCKING FEATURE:Call blocking only works if your phone service provider has caller-ID enabled for your account.It works like this...When a call comes through that you have not put on your call block list already, or that your provider has not filtered, you get an audio announcement of the number and associated caller name.  You can disable the audio announcement if desired.You can then decide if you want to answer or block the call.  If you wish to block it, you press the call block button on the handset which is in the lower right corner.  That stops the call from coming through and the ringing stops on the phone.Call blocking has been a life-changing feature for us.  The combination of our cable provider phone service and this phone has eliminated 98% of our telemarketing calls and all of the robocalls.  We no longer have to unplug our phones to get some sleep, and the calls we do get are nice and clear.------------------------------------------The top 3 reasons I purchased this phone system...1. I got a heck of a deal through the Amazon Warehouse during Prime Day (an additional 20% off the warehouse price), making it under seventy for me.2.  The call blocking feature to eliminate robocalls and telemarketers.3.  The ability to increase the volume easily on the handset, for my hard-of-hearing husband.-----------------------------------------------This phone system works with both traditional phone service providers and VOIP cable company phone services.  It comes with four handsets and has a built-in answering machine along with the call blocking feature that works with the caller ID provided by your phone service provider.The handsets are lightweight, have big numbers that are easy to see along with the LCD display.  The caller ID announce feature is a nice addition and most of the time it's easy to understand.🎯 I think this phone system is a good one for those who want to eliminate robocalls and telemarketing calls from their life.  I also think it's a good choice for those who are impaired visually or have hearing loss.===========================================

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this due to what seemed like pretty awesome and aggressive call Blocker features and the large screen.  I've always bought panasonic but this phone was far more "advanced".  I just set it up and I really dislike how complicated this is.  All phones I've had, for decades, had intuitive set up and I chalked my difficulty up to maybe just not being used to.this brand.  I spent 45 minutes scrolling , hitting buttons, not finding a simple "erase" or "space" anywhere to enter numbers then having the phone save stuff I have to go retype and erase.  I didn't use the manual, having zero problem, ever, setting up a phone, and if you lose the manual good luck setting this up or trying to do "a" thing.  I liked the smart call block  which instructs callers that you're screening calls and to say their name  then press pound to be rung thru.  The manual clearly states that this can block calls you want to have and so don't use it.  Which isn't helpful.  Doctors and others call from private cell phones now and many work from home and aren't using caller-ID branded company phones so its also impractical to block everyone but who is in your phone directory  (another option).  If you want to do this, you cant import or choose the numbers you've added to your directory- you have to retype all the names and numbers,  one by one, again, to your " allow list" .  Many i have in my directory still say "unavailable" above the number which isn't helpful if you have the caller ID speak who is calling so you can go pick it up or let it go to voice mail. A few options you can set up, like allowing everyone in your Directory through didn't work.  I also looked for extra batteries, just in case, and in putting the phone name, I find none listed.  I guess you have to look at the 300 batteries being sold to find the compatible ones but ATT ought to make this easier.  While the screen is large, my smaller one had thicker text and I find this readout spidery and not too easy to read.  Perhaps I'll get used to it but I find this overly complicated, the spoken set up instructions pretty much tell you to read the manual, and alas, it has shrill, annoying ringer tones.  The voice announcer is really weird, pronouncing things slowly and with strange inflection..  Wouldn't buy again and would return if I didn't need a phone this second.  Way too complicated, even.for the easy stuff.UPDATE: I have tried my best to adjust to this phone and persevere.  after months and re-re-reading everything and multiple resets and endless tweaking this phone is a nightmare.  if I leave it on " block everyone but people in my directory" then its fine.  but not practical.  i had it on "block unknown calls" which then started giving me spam numbers calling but without any ID to it.  my best friend continually rings thru as "unknown caller" tho she's in my allow list and directory,  yet the talking ID will announce her name.  many, many times I'll answer the phone and it goes to one, constant ring, like an alarm going off.  it won't answer and I can't turn this off! I have to yank the batteries out. the person calling gets dead air.  many times someone will call and hear me but I can't hear them.  I even called ATT who muddled thru the same instruction tome as I have. people in directory show up as "unknown caller" in spite of being allowed. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I give it 5 stars!!  (I don’t know what the “Lock Feature” is, but just gave that feature 5 stars too).  I had a Panasonic cordless that was several years old and still worked perfectly, but it only allowed me to block 30 numbers at a time, which, with the increase in spam callers, caused me to have to constantly have to go into the block list and remove older numbers to make room for the more recent ones.  WELL… this one lets you block 1000 numbers!!!  (Hopefully that will be enough for a while).  Also, my Panasonic cordless would announce “you’ve got a call from…” and then state about the first 5 numbers, so I was still hearing it ring, tho I know from the area code not to pick it up.  With this AT&T cordless, if the spam callers hang up after my greeting starts playing, I never even hear it ring once nor announced.  And if the number is on my block list, it won’t ring thru either.  I check the phone’s caller list daily and if I see new un-blocked spam calls listed I can easily put them on the block list.  It is also much easier to block calls actively coming in or even afterwards than it was on my older Panasonic.  I only have to push a cpl of buttons to put a number on the block list with the AT&T phone, while with my Panasonic, I had to go to the Menu, scroll down to find block list, erase a number to make room for new number, go back to call list to see new spam number, edit it down to 10 digits (minus the “1”), then save it.  It was a LOT of steps. So this AT&T phone makes it much simpler in way fewer steps to block numbers.  I no longer hear spam caller rings / announcements start in the early morning hours because most of them hang up w/o leaving a message. If they do leave a message - which I have not experienced yet since installing new phone about 4 days ago - I would be able to put them on the block list the same as if they hadn’t.  I have observed that spammers roll thru various exchanges to try to get to you by changing 1 digit in the number they are calling from at a time.  I am very diligent in checking every day for those numbers and block them immediately.  This is why the ability to block 1000 numbers is the MOST important new feature of this phone to me.  One thing that is different, which is not as good as the Panasonic, is setting Quiet Hours… those hours between midnight and whatever time in the morning you do not want the phone to ring at all from anyone.  On the Panasonic, there is a setting to enter the specific hours once that you want to be Quiet and it observes those hours day in and day out; however, with the new AT&T phone, you have to set them each night.  It’s an easy setting, but still so easy to forget to do that before bed every night.  So that is the one deficiency of this phone, and I am surprised AT&T didn’t catch that in their development of it.  But so far, I have remembered to set it nightly.  Even if I forget, I still LUV this phone because it blocks spam callers so perfectly, and that is the main reason I bought it!!  So, if you have a problem with lots of spam callers and want to stop them in their tracks, this is the phone for you!!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great phone...but compared to what?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Tldr: Good phone for this price, noticeably better than older A13 and I wish more people would include context to their reviews. Glad I bought mine.I'm leaving a long and detailed review because I got tired of reading through reviews that seemed contradictory, or said something was "bad" but without any context. If I made a poor choice buying a phone I'd likely be stuck with it for some years. I'm hoping this helps others like myself who are reading the reviews.Ok, so the most important context is what phone I'm coming from over to the A17 5g. My old phone was Samsung A13 5g. My opinions of the new phone will be largely based on how they compare to the previous phone I used. So it's budget phone to budget phone, with the A17 having approximately 3-4ish years newer tech (or same tech but cheaper.) Both phones are being used on metro PCS (T mobile) network.So I've now had the A17 for exactly one week. I primarily use my phone for android auto, text, checking email, web browser, occasional YouTube and maybe once per week on some games. I don't use it for heavy loads like massive file transfers or rendering video. It's fairly light use overall.So far, the things I've been most pleased with are the screen and software/system layout. The screen has decent color and brightness and is MUCH better than the A13. Both screens claim to run at 90hz but the change from the old 270 PPI (I believe stands for pixel per inch or some equivalent) to 385 PPI feels massive. Much cleaner image from text to images. The change from LCD to AMOLED gives much better contrast with deeper colors. The software and system layout are a bit harder to describe in detail. It's more of a personal/ascetic preference. Things look and feel a lot cleaner. There are added optional features like side slide tabs to house shortcuts for certain apps. Another feature is top down swipe from the right for system shortcuts and from the left for notification, so they are smashed together.Another improvement, though less so than the screen and software changes, is in the speed and responsiveness of the phone. This one also needs to be put in context a bit. I'm sure some would complain about it while coming from a more expensive and technologically superior phone. I have my own bias, as I'm coming from an inferior phone which had over 3 years of use (slowing it down over time.) I also use it for mostly light tasks. That being said, I am pleased that the phone is noticeably more responsive than my old one. Most of the lagging happens on start up (goes away after a few mins while the phone is connecting a bunch of apps and putting out/requesting info like date/time/location.) When I booted it for the first time, that was the worst lag I had. It will also slow down if you have several apps running at the same time.  I feel like that's obvious, but some people genuinely don't know that if you hit the home button to leave an app, you need to bring up multi view and actually swipe the box away to close it fully. If you never close apps and never restart your phone on occasion it WILL slow way down. While using the phone for max 1 or 2 things at time it runs perfectly fine, and is better than the A13.Battery life is good. I went from appx. 5000mAh to 5000mAh phones, so besides the slight degradation in the old phones battery life it should be the same. 5000mAh for my uses feels excellent overall. It can go for a full 2 days without charging. Charging speed itself seems improved, but that's never mattered too much for me so I can't comment much. Seems fine though, roughly 1.5h charge from mostly dead to full. That's using a 25w fast charger block and appropriate USB c cable. I didn't use the cable that came with the phone so I can't comment. It didn't come with a charger block, by design. Your mileage on charge speed will vary based on what you're using to charge the phone with. The phone can't charge at full speed if you're using a 5w charger from 15 years ago.I don't have much to say about the camera. I rarely take photos and when I do it's usually quick snap shots of paper instructions or to share location. I believe (though I'm not sure) the A13 was also 50mp front camera but either the the other 2 lenses have been upgraded or they improved the camera software, because pictures do look a bit cleaner. It's not night and day or anything, but it looks better to my eye. Camera is also faster to adjust light and contrast when first focusing on a object, as compared to the old A13.Build quality seems a little improved. They are both budget phones and how build quality "feels" is inherently subjective but to me it does seem a little better.A quick note on activating this new phone...this may only be an issue I personally had, but in case this helps someone else I'd like to include it. I had a bit of trouble switching my physical SIM card out of my old phone and into the new. The metro app was telling me the phone wouldn't be compatible unless I changed phone plans (which is BS.) I had to call customer service and they opted to use the eSiM feature, rather than swapping the physical Sim. I noticed they also used the new phones 2nd SIM number to activate it, while i had tried using first. If you're having trouble perhaps check the phones info from the settings menu, and then try eSIM activation using the 2nd address. It worked fine for me after this.Samsung has a quick transfer feature if your previous phone was a Samsung. It basically copies over everything from your old phone, including apps, pictures, contacts and even text message history ect. It took 3 or 4 attempts (it didn't want to connect and dropped the connection once at 30% complete.) Luckily if it disconnects part way through, it will pick up where it left off, without needing to restart. Once it finally had a stable connection it took me about 6 minutes, it will vary based on how much stuff you have to move over. You need to download an app to do the transfer, but it will prompt you and take you to it's link.Summery: I find it pretty impressive how nice this phone feels both compared to its older model and for its price point in general. I found it frustrating that people would say this part or that was crap or great, but without giving any context to what they based that opinion off of. In my opinion, based on how cheap this phone is and compared to its older model (A13) this is an awesome phone so far, being one week in. Screen is a big improvement, system software and layout is better (IMO) and they seem to be making incremental improvements to things like the camera and overall build. For this price point I find it really impressive what you actually get. If you're coming from an older mid range phone I expect it will either be inferior or about the same. If you're coming from another phone in the 200 range it should be decent to good. For less than 200 and for what I use it for though, I'm very happy I bought this phone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Features and Value, But Smart Switch Had Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: While the phone setup had a major hiccup, the overall experience has been excellent.The Setup Headache (Data Transfer)Setting up the phone and transferring data from the old device was a bit confusing and frustrating. The transfer app kept insisting on an update, but the download would just sit on "pending" forever and never actually progress. After wasting some time waiting, we finally aborted the automated transfer and did everything manually. If you run into the same issue, saving yourself the headache and going the manual route from the start might be faster.The Good Stuff: Features & PerformanceOnce the manual setup was done, the actual user experience has been fantastic. For the price, this phone is packed with incredible value and high-end features:Built-in AI Assistants: Having both the Gemini app and Microsoft Copilot ready to go right out of the box is incredibly convenient for quick searches, drafting, and productivity.Smart Camera Features: The hand recognition for selfies is a game-changer. You just show your palm to the camera, and it triggers the timer—no more awkward stretching to hit the shutter button.Excellent Value: Despite the initial software download glitch during setup, the phone itself offers a ton of modern functionality that makes it very worth the money.The VerdictThe phone itself is a 5-star device for features and value, but I'm knocking off one star due to the frustrating data transfer glitch. If you don't mind a little manual setup, it is a fantastic, feature-rich phone that won't break the bank!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this to replace a Samsung A50 that was purchased in October 2019. Yes, 2019! That's before the world changed forever due to a pandemic. And that alone should tell you how infrequently I change phones and what my priorities in life are. I'm a simple woman with simple needs.There wasn't anything really wrong with my old phone but t unfortunately I cracked the screen and it was almost as much to fix it as it was to get a new one. So since it was practically a dinosaur I chose to "upgrade" and decided to take the chance on getting this model after doing a lot of research. I didn't want to spend a lot of money because I mainly use my phone for basic tasks, talking, texting, etc. I don't do any gaming, heavy streaming or lots of downloading. At most I'll watch a YT video or scroll sparingly on SM if time permits.It arrived quickly and came unlocked as described. That's about it for positive feedback. It was really surprising to me that this phone didn't perform nearly as well as it's almost 7 year old predecessor. Let's start with the fact that it took over 4 hours to do a transfer at the mobile store. Then I learned I really didn't have enough storage so a lot of my texts didn't transfer over. The next thing is I keep running out of space and have to keep deleting photos & videos. Now keep in mind these are the same photos from my old A50. I also have almost the same specs on this phone as there is on the A50 so I don't understand why this is happening.Yes, I know things change but I'm not a fan of the new texting features. They're so annoying, especially auto-correct and the "typing" bubble like the iPhone. And I don't find this to be very intuitive so I have trouble changing certain features easily. I have to dig and dig to find what I need.The UI (?) updates are constant and very annoying. Internet pages or tabs will close or switch for no reason and the phone is also laggy as heck. For example, sometimes it takes at least 4-7 seconds to capture a screenshot. Or at times there's a long delay to move from one part of an Internet page to another. What's crazy is I'm not the type of user who requires everything on my phone to move at the speed of light. I can accept a delay here or there but it's a constant waiting game with this phone. And don't get me started on how terrible the camera is. I absolutely despise every picture this camera takes and selfie are the worst! They have everyone looking haggard as heck, no matter what the setting. My A50 camera was 1000x better than this and I could always find a way to take a flattering photo.When I initially read all the negative reviews (and I mean ALL) I incorrectly assumed some of complaints were from folks who were used to swapping out their $2K phones every year. They had high standards and this is a low budget phone so they were disappointed. I get it. It's hard to enjoy beer when you have champagne tastes. But I was quite mistaken. A lot of the complaints are very valid and quite accurate.If you're looking for quality on a budget this ain't it. Trust me. This phone is probably best for a 10-year old child. Take it from someone with super low standards and who kept their own phone for an actual child's formative years. I'll keep it because I don't want to spend more money right now but do yourself a favor and keep your expectations low. If you need a high performance phone look elsewhere. I wish I did.
