productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Wonderful upgrade from the S21 Ultra! Display is good straight-on and up to 30% off-axis.Wonderful upgrade from the S21 Ultra! Display is good straight-on and up to 30% off-axis.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: SUMMARY: BUY IT! The S26 Ultra is an excellent phone with a solid set of features. My S21 Ultra's OneUI/Android OS updates ended in January.• The S26 Ultra display looks great, better than the S21 Ultra, if viewed straight-on and up to maybe 30% off-axis with the privacy display off. I use my phone like this most of the time and have no need for the "privacy" feature, so a win. Farther off-axis though, or with the privacy display "on", the nicest thing I can say is "it will do the job until the S27 Ultra is released with hopefully Privacy Display V2.0". The display defaults to midway FHD+ resolution for a tiny battery savings, like the S21U did, so bump it up to QHD+ in Settings->Display->Screen Resolution to fully enjoy.• The display's dithered (Frame Rate Control) 8-bit (16.7 million colors) to simulate 10-bit looks OK visually. The S21U used the same, and so likely does iPhone 17. I'm hoping for a true 10-bit display (1.07 billion colors & no visual artifacts) in the S27 or S28 Ultra with a much higher-than-existing 480 Hz PWM display-dimming frequency to reduce eye strain, 3500 nits of max brightness (vs 2600 in the S26U), and at least a 7000 mAh silicon-carbon battery - all 4 things as in current Oppo & Xiaomi phones. :/• The 25 watt wireless charging works so well that I can see I won't be using a wired charger much. Same 25W rate as my wired S21U charging, but the S26U battery fills faster at 25W for some reason. The wireless charger puck’s magnet ring strongly locks right onto my Otterbox Defender Pro XT case's (Amazon B0GD2KS743) opposite-pole magnet ring. The Samsung 25W wireless charger kit is labeled "Magnet Wireless Charger | 45W Power Adapter", a 25 watt wireless puck AND a 45 watt charger in the same box (EP-P2900TBEGUS, Amazon B0FXHJTGNN). The puck requires the 45W charger (EP-T4511NBEGUS by itself, Amazon B0DQFJKP4B), its info says, even though it puts out just the 25W of charging power. You can unplug the 25W wireless charging puck from the 45W adapter it comes with (USB-C), then use the wired charging cable in the S26U box to get a full 45W charging rate, about 2x as fast (real-world tested) as 25W! 2 charging rates in one box. The 15 watt wireless charging on the S21U was nearly useless with no magnets for coil alignment.•  The S26U display shows: “Super fast wireless charging” for 25W from the puck; "Super fast charging" for the S21U's 25W wired adapter; “Super fast charging 2.0” for 45W wired charging; & “Super fast charging 3.0” for a wired connection with the 60W wall charger. I’m finding the Samsung 60W (EP-T6010NBEGUS, Amazon B0GXGMCQYJ) & 45W wired chargers are charging at nearly the same rate if the battery is already mostly full. Seems the 60W rate would only happen for a while if the battery is very low and not too warm, since the charging rate is also thermally limited. The 25W wireless & 45W wired cable S26U charging is really all many people would likely need, unless their battery gets full-cycled (mostly discharged) often, then the 60W would help. The 60W adapter is heavy! Best to use it in a fairly tight-fitting wall socket.• The S26U uses higher 15 Volt and 20 volt charging voltages than some past phones, such that it only needs 3 amps vs 5 amps of current, resulting in requiring less bulky (than 5A) 3A charging cables. 5 amp cables will still work perfectly, passing only 3A, just less flexible. S26U 25W (S21U charger) = 2.77A*9V; 45W = 3A*15V; 60W = 3A*20V. Some older phones used 45W = 5A*9V. Their “45W” wall adapter wouldn’t give 45W S26U charging if they can't produce 15V. The Samsung S26U 3A charging cords have nice rubber strain reliefs at the ends. They can transfer data too at a very reduced USB 2.0 480 Mbps rate with their one half-duplex data wire pair: 3ft 3A = EP-DA705BBEGWW (Amazon B07T99CGDF); 6ft 3A = EP-DX310JBEGU (Amazon B09QQKPPJK). A USB 3.2 rated 5/10/20 Gbps USB-C cable with 4 more full-duplex data wire pairs & an E-Marker chip is needed for the S26U's port's full speed 5 Gbps data transfers [Amazon B0DZP2S6F9 & B0D4PRVVR7].• The 45 watt USB-C port on the Samsung EP-L5300 (Amazon B089RD7F71) car charger works for the S26U with the Samsung 25W wireless puck (puck w/o adapter EP-P2900BBEGUS [Amazon B0FXHJQJ81]) AND with wired 45W wired charging (tested!). Plus it has a 15W USB-A port for something else.• The S26U's 5000 mAh lithium battery is lasting much longer for a given time period than the same in the S21U, even though small by today's standards, likely thanks to the higher efficiency of the 3nm Snapdragon SoC CPU and Adreno 840 GPU vs 5nm in the S21U. The charging battery-life-extender “stop %” setting in the S26U is adjustable from 80–100%, vs. fixed at 80% or 100% in the S21U. Mine is set at 90% now. I can go to bed with 90% showing on the S26U, then wake up with 81% - and that is with the two cell carriers running (see below). Awesome!• App start-up & switching between apps is much faster and smoother on the S26U than the S21U, given the 2X faster performance SoC CPU. App & OS updates (and phone restarts) go fast! The S26U has UFS V4.0 storage vs. the rumored latest V4.1 (higher efficiency), but no loss since they both transfer data at the same speed. The 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro SoC expected in the S27 Ultra is slated for UFS V5.0, twice the bandwidth of V4.0, and for LPDDR6 memory which will also used by the new Adreno 850 GPU & its 50% wider memory bus. Will be a beast! The S26U's Adreno 840 GPU is 3x as fast as the S21U's Adreno 660 and has hardware ray tracing, while consuming much less power.• The dual SIM radios in the S26U work well! I'm now running Cricket (AT&T towers) on physical SIM IMEI1 and Spectrum Mobile (Verizon towers) on eSIM IMEI2. The S26U is fully set up for switching the call, messages, and data independently between carriers, sim1 and sim2 in the quick panel. The upper left of the lock screen shows "cricket * Spectrum" for carriers, and the signal strength bar adds a new row of dots underneath to show the signal strength of the other carrier too, plus showing both strength bars when the quick panel is pulled down. If you travel to different parts of town where one carrier’s signal is much weaker, and/or has a “full tower load” signal drop-out, and/or only one carrier has 5G mmWave antennas in an area ("5G+" display), and/or you want to use your data quota on a specific carrier, this is great. Two chances at getting a good connection. I've found that certain carriers (Total Wireless) won't sell a second line eSIM unless they also have the physical SIM on line 1, so they couldn't be used for different dual carriers. Given an IMEI2 number, a carrier will know who the carrier for IMEI1 is.• Better weight/size distribution. Only 1 oz less (9 oz vs 10 oz), with cases, than the S21U, but the S26U literally feels 25% lighter being slightly larger. Kind of a magic trick!• The Wi-Fi 7 works well as does the 6 GHz band. In my TP Link BE 550 Pro router/AP (from Amazon! B0DM6RF34J) I had to change the 6 GHz bandwidth from the default 160 MHz to "mixed 160/320 MHz" (or just 320 MHz) to have that band show as Wi-Fi 7 on the S26U vs Wi-Fi 6E (symbols for both on the display). I've read that iPhones don't even have a 320 MHz bandwidth option on 6 GHz, so those users are apparently left with 6E on 6 GHz. The bandwidth setting in your router on the 5 GHz band might have to be lowered to 80 MHz max (20/40/80) from 160 MHz if you are experiencing lag. I haven't seen it, but a bug there with some routers from reports. The S21U was officially the world's first smartphone to support 6 GHz 6E Wi-Fi when it came out! I had mine talking to a wired ARRIS 6E AP blade, but the S21U's 6 GHz radio died after the second year. :(• The S26U Wi-Fi switches between SSIDs VERY well, automatically, based on signal strength, when walking around a spread-out house with different wired Wi-Fi AP’s, as is my case. The S21U usually didn’t, requiring frequent manual SSID changes walking around. I’ve noticed the S26U even turns the Wi-Fi back on when I get home (SSID recognition), after I’ve turned it off while gone in the car.• The "3D" fingerprint reader on the S26U works very well! Nearly every time. That is without even turning on the new "improve accuracy" additional 10x scan option, too. The "0D" (lol) fingerprint reader on the S21U was useless, at least with my worn and scarred fingerprint. I gave up early-on with the S21U reader and used PIN codes ever since. The “Samsung Pass” app is usable now with its required fingerprint bio-ID.• I've shot some 4K and 8K video and it looks fantastic! Samsung's new APV encoding standard, a modern competitor to the older Apple Pro Res, is good with claimed 10% better storage efficiency. The phone will record 4:2:2 internally, supports Log recording, and can record to external SSD storage on USB via the port (there is a video setting to enable it). 4K60fps APV 422HQ generates 12GB/min; 422LQ = 6GB/min. Hoping for a full 1" camera sensor on the S27 Ultra! I love Samsung's change to natural "true/accurate" colors with the S26U cam vs. the processed "happy bright" colors of past Samsung phone cams. The S25 Ultra doesn't have APV, or the amazing new video Horizon Lock feature, so right there along with true color are 3 good reasons to get the S26U if you are a video fan.• The low light camera ability of the f/1.4 wider-aperture S26U main cam (vs. S25U's f/1.7) is also quite good. I wind up with a *lot* of low light situations where I need to take photos. Couldn't do it with the S21U much of the time. I would have to use my large Lumix GH7 & GH5 MFT cameras with a fast lens. Hoping for the rumored return (from the S10!) to a variable-aperture main cam on the S27, matching similar iPhone 18 rumors.• Be sure to download & install the Samsung "Good Lock" and "Camera Assistant" apps from the Samsung Store! The "Good Lock" app has all sorts of useful camera customization options with even more being added by the upcoming One UI 9.0 phone OS. Then go to "advanced resolution options" and enable "24MP" photo mode (adds to the existing modes), which is a very useful point-and-shoot AI processing of multi-frame stacked images using various cams: ultrawide cam for 0.6-0.9x; main cam for 1x-1.9x; and telephoto for 5x-9.9x. The 3x cam doesn't participate in the fun and is rumored to be gone in the S27 Ultra. Excellent 40% resolution improvement over 12MP, with noise reduction and reasonable file sizes. The S21U didn't have 24MP at all, while the S25U only has it in Expert Raw mode.• I've taken a *lot* of photos recently in 24MP mode ^^ and love it. Toggle-on "keep 24MP resolution" to keep it permanently in the camera's list between 12MP and 50MP. Note that while the 24MP shutter "snap" is instant, the phone then processes the photo in the background, once the camera is closed, for up to 30 seconds. Longer if several shots in a row. Shows up in the top status bar as "refining picture". If the image file is being transferred out to a PC using S26U's "Link to Windows" in Quick Panel and "Phone Link" on Windows 11 (the link uses both Wi-Fi & Bluetooth, check that BT is on), or a cable, close the cam and give it that time for the images to show up in the list. See my Windows 11 File Explorer photo that shows the Phone Link "Galaxy S26 Ultra" external device entry *above* "This PC", while a separate "Galaxy S26 Ultra" entry, if using a cable, shows up at the same time below "This PC" with the drive letter listings, acting like a drive. The latter cable connection is faster for photo & file transfer ofc, but the former Wi-Fi is not bad.• The S26U, like the S21U, can take *photos* in RAW mode (unprocessed sensor data) with the built-in Pro Mode (12 bit) or Expert Raw Mode (16 bit) added by the Samsung app for external processing on a PC/Mac with Lightroom, etc. The S26U isn't able to shoot *video* in true RAW mode though like the iPhone17 Pro Max can, but I don't view this as a problem at all. RAW video with its massive uncompressed files is really best shot with a dedicated camera like the Lumix GH7 that has a bigger sensor, lower noise, and large glass lenses to collect more light with less processing, IMHO.• The camera lenses do stick out in the back though, unlike the S21U where they were flat (and recessed with the S21U Otterbox Defender case). The S26U Otterbox Pro XT case mitigates that to some extent by having a plastic ring around the lens area that is slightly taller to help keep the lens from scraping on things when the phone is set down on its back. Lens protectors are a good idea (Amazon B0G7STMFKY).• The speakers/audio on the S26U can go a bit louder (and clearer) than the S21U, which was needed. Try this: while on a phone call in a noisy environment, pull down the quick panel and tap "Mic Mode", then select "Voice Focus". Does a good job of filtering out the background noise to let voice through. Hopefully the S27U will support 32-bit float audio recording, like the Lumix GH7 cam and iPhone 17 Pro Max support, for zero concern over recording levels! Samsung really needs to update their new APV codec to support 32-bit float audio, like Pro Res can – this is a big Samsung omission, IMHO. :/• The Bluetooth V6.0 in the S26U works better (stable, less lag, faster connect, longer range) than the S21U BT V5.2 with my car entertainment link (Lexus RX350) and PreSonus Eris 4.5BT desktop speakers. I can be 6 car-lengths away from a storage unit's BT entry gate (uses an app) now vs just 3 ft with the S21U. Unfortunately the S26U’s SoC chip doesn’t support the latest (Nov 2025) low-latency BT V6.2. Hoping for that in the S27U.• The S26U 5 Gbps USB 3.2 Gen 1 port, same as the S21U has, still supports DisplayPort Alt Mode & HDMI, using an adapter cable to an external monitor. Useful for Samsung Dex (PC-like environment independent from the phone's display) or screen mirroring. As with the S21U, Smart View in the quick panel is Samsung's version of (Wi-Fi Direct) Miracast. It works wonderfully, with a bit more lag vs. a cable, for phone screen mirroring through things like a Roku box, Amazon Fire Stick TV, or a smart TV. I use it a lot!• USB port/cable specs are a happy mess of evolved standards over the years. Use a USB 3.2 rated USB-C 5/10/20 Gbps "full featured" (22-wire) cable with an E-marker chip [Amazon B0DZP2S6F9 or B0D4PRVVR7] when connecting the S26U to things with 5/10/20 Gbps USB 3.2 USB-C ports like: an external NVMe SSD for storing video or a PC for file transfer. Originally 5 Gbps USB 3.0 "SuperSpeed" & 10 Gbps USB 3.1 "SuperSpeed+" links tried to verify/negotiate speed with "link training" which didn't work well in the real world. A modern cable's E-Marker chip eliminates the speed (and power) capability guesswork for speeds over USB 2.0. Otherwise, with just a USB 2.0 4-wire charging cable, a USB 3.2 port on each end will fall back to USB 2.0 speeds and Windows 11 File Explorer might show "external device failure" mid-way if transferring files/photos. Be sure to run Windows 10/11's Windows Update with: a USB 3.2 10/20 Gbps data cable in place from PC to the S26U, the S26U pull-down set for USB file transfer, and phone unlocked. A couple of new Samsung S26 high-speed drivers might show up (did for me). I’m hoping for a 10 Gbps USB 3.2 gen 2 port in the S27 Ultra, like the iPhone17 has, or even better 3.2 gen 2x2 20 Gbps for the higher res video out to NVMe SSDs.• The S26U adds Google Messaging via satellite connection to the emergency SOS satellite feature in the S25U, both only operational when no cell or Wi-Fi service exists. Spectrum Mobile does have satellite service via Skylo that comes included with the plans. I haven't been able to test since I always have cell & Wi-Fi signals around here. T-Mobile apparently offers S26U satellite via Starlink. The S26U allows up to 7 additional eSIMs to be stored & swapped out with the 2 active SIMs as needed. Future satellite-only monthly add-on plans could be added as a stored eSIMs. Maybe from Starlink or even Amazon's Leo 396-satellite network (Kuiper) & their ongoing Globalstar purchase (both currently geared toward Apple iPhone satellite).• Samsung is just now phasing out their wonderful messaging app in favor of Google messages due to universal (vs. carrier-specific) RCS. An alternative without RCS (typing, read indicators, & some other social media app stuff), but with the usual SMS and MMS, is Textra (free & paid versions). After install go to settings->apps->default apps->SMS app and set to Textra (Gmsgs still there, just not default). Samsung also recently, via an update, reduced the max number of email accounts that can be set to IMAP immediate-receive (push) in their Samsung email app. If you have many email accounts, like I do, and the app is suddenly crashing on startup, change a few to 15 minute (fetch) receive. Same with Thunderbird - defaults to just 10 email accounts as push. Be sure to go into battery settings for ANY of your messaging, email, and social media apps and change from "optimized" to "unrestricted". Otherwise the phone OS will randomly cut off their battery access when it thinks they are idle, delaying incoming messages.• The Samsung Smart Switch transfer app - the default that comes up when you power up the S26U - from the S21U took about 45 minutes to transfer 72GB of apps and data using the USB 2.0 charging cable in the S26U box. The S26U had 69% battery out of the box, then the 45 transfer took it down to 55%. Keep in mind the SSS app completely re-installs the latest version of the phone’s apps from Google Play & Samsung Store, not just copying them over, then re-loads their data. Works extremely well! ZERO problem with the transfer, but of course passwords have to be re-entered everywhere since they are phone-specific encrypted. Any discontinued apps (I had one) or side-loaded apps have to be handled later, manually.• Can't comment about the AI/Bixby and stylus. I don't use either (well, except for 24MP mode & Horizon Lock in the camera which use AI ^^), maybe in the future. The S26U has a 40% faster NPU than the S25U, if you do use the phone’s AI. Remember that Claude & ChatGPT AI do all their computes in the cloud, at data centers. They don’t use a phone’s (or PC’s) NPU at all, at least currently.* The upcoming new One UI V9.0/Android 17 OS release with some useful updates is now in beta test for the S26U! Release expected in late August. The S26U gets a full seven years of operating system updates, through 2033, making this phone a solid value to keep or trade in years to come. I may trade in for the future S27U or S28U if my hoped-for true 10-bit display & 7000+ mAh battery happen. :)• And *great work* Amazon in getting the pre-ordered phone to me right on the promised March 11 release date! Updated 7/22/26.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: We've been with Samsung since the S4 and though we were talked into something different by a salesperson, we returned after a couple months haven't veered since.Of all the iterations of the phone,  this one is my favorite.The best features are found in the camera and on-board editing tools and ai. It's an editing studio on the go.  When everyone takes group photos and you all use your phones to capture the same perspective, yours is the photo people will use for its crisp results. You can even drop logos on your photos with the sticker editing tool.App navigation and page transitions are smooth and not chonky like the other popular competitor.It offers so much better customization that I can't do on my work appointed competitor phone.Video stabilization is neat. Having it track the horizon line is a nice feature if you're a v-logger and need some stabilization that you'd get out of a gimble. It's not QUITE as good,  but if that guy with the famous Bigfoot footage from the 70s had this,  we would have a clean video of it... just saying.Size wise it's comparable to the last previous years releases. The screen size is a good size without feeling like I'm carrying a tablet.The phone being unlocked was an easy setup for moving from my old damaged phone to this one.  The condition of the phone was great and seemed brand new.The calls sound clear both in ear and speaker. Bluetooth also works great.Good value for the money.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast once bloatware rmv'd/disabled, privacy feature clever UPDATED 260803
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Not a my-choice purchase as old phone died... and wasn't crazy about how much more expensive new premier Samsung conventional smartphones were. But here we are... and there's good and bad imo.Good:- still has S-Pen (if dumbed-down from earlier phones)- *very* fast and responsive- privacy feature will prolly be on every smartphone soon- Smart Switch was so painless, wouldn't mind doing it again in 4y (have waited in carrier stores 8hrs to do the same thing once upon a time in smartphone history)- no options to make the battery life shorter, that it doesn't tell you about in no uncertain termsBad:- heavier than old phone, for almost the exact same screen size and phone thickness- dumbed-down S-Pen- privacy feature enabled, cuts screen resolution by a *lot*- still had data transfers not done, as classically-frustrating buying a new phone, just less so- so much bloatware (if you hate the attempted hegemony of AI like I do), that responsiveness is less than old phone before pruning it all offSo, other than the coup of the privacy screen (which certain things you can selectively hide), just a fast smartphone of the same resolution and slightly quicker response to inputs, as 5y ago. The flat real estate of the S26 screen is a throwback I love (means Corning glass protectors that actually work), but also mean state of the art's focused elsewhere, and that's AI like the rest of the multinational-profiteer-club universe it seems. But I'll take the better protectors and the privacy if that's what Samsung's offering, as iPhones are even more vintage-looking (and acting).So far no functional criticisms about the exp... but tbh, if there were, would be 2 stars just for spending so much on AI-fondling garbage s/w. So time will tell. Will update if such things appear. Four tentative stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ _---EDIT 21 JUL 26:Have had a chance to play with the best feature on the S26U, the privacy display.Good: having it On doesn't seem to affect battery life whatsoever. In fact, slightly extends it by disabling a portion of pixels not devoted to privacy angle (face-on to the screen). But only by a couple of minutes in my own testing.Bad: the privacy feature, even on Maximum setting, doesn't fully obscure the screen at angles typically seen by an over-shoulder voyeur -- your eyes must be >45 degrees from face-on, for screen display to be completely unreadable. Since your eyes are 2.36 - 2.56 inches / 60 - 65mm apart, one eye will see more than the other -- meaning when your brain combines the two, doesn't provide a perfect solution to voyeurism.Verdict: rather have it than not, esp when battery consumption's a wash (unlike many, many other features on this phone). Exposes voyeurs by preventing passing-glance views of what you're looking at; must be stationary a few secs to make out your screen details. Also can choose to only have certain features like password fields privacy-displayed, which is a game changer for those who want privacy but don't want their data compromised.---EDIT 03 AUG 26:Since the 21st of July, have been teaching myself the quite daunting new features in a Galaxy S Ultra phone, not present 5y ago -- and yep, AI was a large portion of the re-education.Did research, turned most off (at least those which one *can* be turned off). As in the prior posts, speed was slightly better but not obviously better, until this was done -- and then huge gains in response time for just about everything. The usual teething with apps that need permissions re-disciplined in a new phone, and getting Google to play nice with it (still can't get photos shot with Camera and stored in Gallery, to be sent to my Gmail inbox within an hour 😒But that's the only complaint, really -- with Camera and Gallery. Most everything else works smoothly and now very quickly. And the Play Store's updates are easily 5x faster -- which was a real chore on the old S22.Going to uprate to 5 -- could've become a travesty like the infamous Samsung exploding battery debacle, so am gald they've gone back to a flat screen and invested the savings into secure pixels -- which I've already found one moment where if not enabled, could've compromised my data. Five stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Definitely the very best Galaxy class smartphone experience I've ever had so far...
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have been a long-time buyer of Samsung Galaxy series of smartphones for decades. Over the years, I have experienced  mostly a good experience with some design flaws in the earlier models such as screen pixelation and poor battery utilization.  But for the most part my Samsung phones have lasted well over 3 years until I decide to upgrade and not because the phone has malfunctioned.I purchased the new Samsung Galaxy s26 Ultra to replace my 3 year old Samsung Galaxy s21 FE. I am really pleased with my s26 Ultra. This phone is lightening fast, snappy, and incredibly responsive--the user environment snaps smoothly in front of you so fast there is no time to see anything in between the transition except incredible speed.  The display is easy to see in direct sunlight . The biometrics--face and fingerprint unlock are accurate and function seamlessly--face unlock works really great even when I am walking outside in direct sunlight.My s26 Ultra is very comfortable holding it in my hand.  I purchased a premium $17 clear case that is perfect to protect it.  The s26 Ultra has a remarkable display that is so clear and realistic in color depth.  The battery utilization is by far the best user experience that I have ever had to date with a Galaxy series phone.  I can use my s26 Ultra all day--talk on the phone, use lots of apps, and still the battery meter hardly shows any battery loss and I can keep it unplugged for more than a 48 hours and it still has plenty of battery charge.The S-Pen is amazing.  The S-Pen is very nicely housed inside the phone same as it was for my previous Samsung series note phone that I owned several years ago. When using it to write "S notes" the user experience is fantastic--you can feel the pen against the screen that mimics the feeling like a real "pen to paper" experience with the strokes of the virtual pen having the same precision as a real pen.My s26 Ultra is running incredibly cool and does not get overheated. The CPU in this phone is fantastic.I was very fortunate in that I was going to buy the phone through my cellular carrier for about the same price as Amazon but it was only going to come with 256GB of storage and the color was limited to black, so I purchased my phone on Amazon and got a limited time deal that included 512GB of storage and I got to select the Sky Blue color from all the available colors that Samsung offers for this series. And Amazon let me spread the payments interest free for 5 months, so that was just perfect for my budget.Aesthetics of the phone are great too, I purchased my s26 Ultra in Sky Blue color and I love this color and the shape of the phone and design are very appealing too.I give the Samsung Galaxy s26 Ultra a well deserved 5 out of 5 stars.  Thank you Samsung and Amazon.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love my Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. I upgraded from the S24 Ultra, and for me, it was definitely worth it. The display is stunning, and I absolutely love the new Privacy Screen feature. I've also noticed improvements in the camera quality, and the battery life has been excellent.What I enjoy the most, however, is how much thinner and lighter it is than previous Ultra models. I used to dislike texting on my old phone because it felt bulky, but the S26 Ultra feels so premium and comfortable in my hand that using it is now a pleasure.Another feature I really appreciate is how easy it is to share photos and videos from my Android phone to an iPhone. It makes sharing with friends and family much more convenient.While I still think there's room for improvement with the camera and a few other features, overall, the S26 Ultra is a wonderful device, and I'm extremely happy with my upgrade.

If I keep it as long as I plan, the cost will be worth it for good battery life, a big bright screen, a fast processor, and good sound. I'd be sad to have a lower quality device that I use constantly.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My old V-Tech landline phone finally died. This V-Tech pair replacement has several improvements and only a few small downsides.The screen and buttons are substantially larger, making it much easier to read and use this phone. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Photo of wall mount is incredibly misleading.Photo of wall mount is incredibly misleading.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this set to replaced a Uniden setup that had literally fallen apart because the plastics disintegrated.  It all works well enough and has a few nice features like the intercom system and the fact that the handsets share entries in the address book without having to enter the same information multiple times.  Functionally, it's all fine, especially when considering the price.However, I did encounter one negative aspect, of which I thought potential buyers should be aware:Included in this set is a sort of "universal" wall-mount adapter that, when paired with this particular model, is a hilarious abomination of one-size-fits-all gone terribly awry.See the bottom photo on the left that depicts the phone mounted to the wall?  Yeah, the actual product isn't nearly so easy on the eyes.  I'm sure that configuration is possible with one model of this product but this isn't it.There are slots on the back of the main charging station marked "B" that correspond to the "B" posts on the mount and, when assembled, form a misshapen Frankenstein's monster of an eyesore (see photos).  According to the instructions that came packaged in the box, despite all appearances to the contrary, this is, in fact, correct.Yikes.I thought I might be able to free up a little desk space by wall-mounting the phone but I guess that's out the window now.  Granted, this may not be an issue for many customers but that this was considered an acceptable use case for this product is wild to me.Also, the handset locator button in the back of the base for some odd reason instead of the front, clearly defined and marked, like every other cordless phone I've used in the past 35 years for...reasons?

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Powerful iPhone with a Premium Design
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Apple iPhone 15 Pro Max is a great option for anyone looking for a high-end smartphone without necessarily paying full price for a brand-new model. The Black Titanium finish looks sleek and premium, and the overall design feels modern and durable.The 6.7-inch display is one of the standout features. The screen is bright, sharp, and great for watching videos, browsing the internet, taking photos, and using apps. The ProMotion display also makes scrolling and animations feel smooth and responsive.The camera system is another major highlight. The different camera options make it easy to take detailed photos in a variety of situations, while the video quality is excellent for recording everyday moments. The 5x telephoto camera is especially useful when you want to capture subjects from farther away.The performance is very fast thanks to the A17 Pro chip. Apps open quickly, multitasking feels smooth, and the phone handles demanding games and other tasks well. The 256GB of storage also provides plenty of room for photos, videos, apps, and other files.Since this is a renewed device, the condition can depend on the individual unit, so it is important to check the seller's description and renewal warranty before purchasing. Being unlocked is a major advantage because it gives you more flexibility when choosing a compatible carrier.The battery life is also good for everyday use, although actual battery performance on a renewed phone can vary depending on its battery health and previous use.Overall, the iPhone 15 Pro Max 256GB in Black Titanium is a powerful and premium phone with an excellent display, strong cameras, fast performance, and plenty of storage. For someone who wants a Pro Max experience at a potentially lower price through a renewed model, this is a solid option.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: BE AWARE OF THE RISKS - I spent hours fixing Amazons issueBE AWARE OF THE RISKS - I spent hours fixing Amazons issue
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Updated: since writing the below review, I have received my second 15 pro max renewed premium, set it up, and handled the refund from the first one. Amazon customer support also offered me a generous discount on the new phone for all the hassle (which I somewhat needed to initiate asking for, I doubt they would have offered that to begin with). If I had to do it all over again - I would have still gone this route since apple refurbished hasn’t released this model yet, but moving forward- I will probably order straight from apple refurbished next time or just get a new iPhone. When factoring the discount I got on this one that’s one year old, I paid about 2/3 the cost for this compared to the latest model, so I can’t complain. All that said, in general I am one who much more values my time and ease over saving a quick bucks. Especially if that quick buck saved costs me HOURS of my life in hassle. If you’re like me in that sense - proceed with caution. I trust Amazon will help make it right if you don’t get a great phone as expected, but even if that’s the case, you’re probably in for quite the hoops to jump through in order to make that happen.Here’s my original, unedited review:I ordered the iPhone 15 Pro Max refurbished and it arrived last night. After spending a good 3+ hours setting it up, I realized the lens for the main camera was broken. From the outside, you can’t see any issue. It wasn’t until I opened up the camera app that I actually saw it didn’t work.“Renewed Premium” carries a certain standard with it, and this certainly does not meet that in the slightest. On top of that, upon calling customer support, I was told that I would not be able to do anything unless I deactivated the phone and remove my Apple ID from it. Wouldn’t have been the end of the world if I needed to go back to my other phone for a bit, however, in order to set up this phone with the eSIM, deactivated my previous SIM card. Upon explaining all of that to customer support, I was told there was nothing they could do unless I deactivated this phone (leaving me without a phone until they received this and shipped me a new one)I was then told to call Apple to see what they can do, when honestly, this is their mistake. Either way, I called apple and it was going to be another set of hoops to jump through with scheduling appointments and all that. Plus since I didn’t have apple care, if they needed to repair the camera, I would still be without a phone. So even if Apple was able to help fix this, the issue of me not having a phone would still be there. Had I broken this camera myself - I would certainly except those terms given there’s not much else I could do. However, this was given to me in this condition and for Amazon to leave me with the responsibility of fixing their mistake due to carelessness in inspection and quality control is absurd.So whether I like it or not, I am now STUCK with the responsibility of cleaning this up since my account is connected to this phone now. What at one point could have been a great gift to myself has turned into the biggest hassle I’ve experienced buying/returning anything, probably ever.I’m going to give this one more shot as I’ve now ordered another iPhone from them to be delivered shortly, however, it’s also required me to spend another ~$1000 in having that iPhone sent prior to me getting my refund. This is absolutely ridiculous and unacceptable. Even if this next phone is perfect, I’m likely never going to order from the Amazon refurbished store again. I’ll either go straight to Apple refurbished, or brand new, for any of my future phone/laptop/device purchases.On top of all this hassle, I’ll certainly have to spend another few hours setting up my replacement phone once it arrives.All the time I’ve invested into this so far has NOT been even close worth the “nice discount” on a premium refurbished phone that should have arrived without issue to begin with.Amazon - take note. Change your policies. Making this the customer’s mess to clean up is not acceptable.Potential buyers - BEWARE of the risks.I’ll plan to update this review if anything changes. But like I said, even if the next phone I ordered is perfect, I still give this a 1-star review for all the hassle and lack of responsibility the company took to resolve this.P.s. i’ll also add that I am a quite understanding and peaceful person. The person I spoke with from customer support was doing his absolute best to help me, but this was clearly a bigger issue than he had the power to solve. I requested to have this escalated to upper management and was told the same thing. Whoever is the one making decisions about what can and can’t be done needs to hear about this.

*Disclaimer – Audio quality is dependent on your service provider’s network quality 
A light on the top of the handset flashes when the phone rings, signaling an incoming call. With the ringers muted, this visual indicator can let you know the calls in silence. Also helpful for those who are hearing impaired. 
Audio Assist button instantly increases incoming call's volume and enhances sound frequencies to make speech easier to understand. It is easy to use, just one press on the Audio Assist button on handset. Press again to turn off. 
2" backlit display on handset with high contrast text makes it easy to read incoming caller ID or call history records. Plus, the lighted handset keypad allows for easy dialing in low light conditions. 
With the full-duplex speakerphone on the handset, this phone set not only lets you speak hands-free but also allows both ends to speak and be heard at the same time. Enjoy conversations that are more true to life. 
Stay informed even when you are away from home. All calls are routed to the built-in digital answering machine when necessary, recording key messages for you. 
Screening calls has never been easier. The handset announces the name of the caller, so you don't have to scramble for the handset to see who's calling. 
Experience the best in long-range coverage and clarity, provided by a unique antenna design and advances in noise-filtering technology. 
What's a Smart Call Blocker? 
A simple one-time setup to filter unwanted calls while letting trusted ones through. 
Quick Setup to let the system working for you 
Set Directory - for your family so their calls will go through without the screening. 1. Press MENU on handset. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Directory, then Select. 3. Press Select again to choose Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then Select. 
Set Allow list - so their calls do not get through the screening. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow list, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter telephone number, then Select. 5. Enter name, then Select. 
Set Block List - to prevent their calls from ringing through. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Block list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then press Select. 
Set Star name list for your trusted organizations - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Star name list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the name (up to 15 characters), then press Select. 
Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: With caller ID, call blocking works great
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the AT&T BL102-4 cordless phone set from the Amazon Warehouse (like-new used in original packaging)  when our family switched from a traditional landline setup to a VOIP landline with our local cable provider.  We previously had been using a cordless system from another brand with our phone company's service and the call quality was never good - often lots of crackle on the line, making callers hard to hear.  I wasn't sure if it was the phones, the service, or the cords, so I replaced all of them and started anew.The build quality of this AT&T phone system was a little less substantial than I expected, but the phones do their job and call quality is good.  The handsets and the base feel kind of cheap, but this is an under-one hundred dollar phone system so I guess that's to be expected.  It works well though, and the features are good.The only feature I miss is Bluetooth.  If this system had it  I could pair it with my cell phone, but other than that, it's not missing anything.----------------------------------➡️  SETUP & USE:I put the batteries in the phones and charged them as I went to the included user manual to try and figure out how to set it up.  The manual is a bit overwhelming, but if you read it carefully and go step by step, you can figure it out.Some features on the phone duplicate those offered by my cable company, so I did need to figure out which ones to set up and which ones to leave off on the phone.  For example, my cable provider offers voicemail, and thus using the answering machine feature of this phone system isn't something that I do.Once I set up things like the number of rings before the calls were answered, I started adding numbers into my phone's contacts.  Doing this let these callers come right through, and helped with call blocking.  I set it up so that callers I didn't recognize would have to press the pound button on their phones to get through.  This eliminates robocalls, but real-live telemarketers can still get through.---------------------------------------➡️ CALL BLOCKING FEATURE:Call blocking only works if your phone service provider has caller-ID enabled for your account.It works like this...When a call comes through that you have not put on your call block list already, or that your provider has not filtered, you get an audio announcement of the number and associated caller name.  You can disable the audio announcement if desired.You can then decide if you want to answer or block the call.  If you wish to block it, you press the call block button on the handset which is in the lower right corner.  That stops the call from coming through and the ringing stops on the phone.Call blocking has been a life-changing feature for us.  The combination of our cable provider phone service and this phone has eliminated 98% of our telemarketing calls and all of the robocalls.  We no longer have to unplug our phones to get some sleep, and the calls we do get are nice and clear.------------------------------------------The top 3 reasons I purchased this phone system...1. I got a heck of a deal through the Amazon Warehouse during Prime Day (an additional 20% off the warehouse price), making it under seventy for me.2.  The call blocking feature to eliminate robocalls and telemarketers.3.  The ability to increase the volume easily on the handset, for my hard-of-hearing husband.-----------------------------------------------This phone system works with both traditional phone service providers and VOIP cable company phone services.  It comes with four handsets and has a built-in answering machine along with the call blocking feature that works with the caller ID provided by your phone service provider.The handsets are lightweight, have big numbers that are easy to see along with the LCD display.  The caller ID announce feature is a nice addition and most of the time it's easy to understand.🎯 I think this phone system is a good one for those who want to eliminate robocalls and telemarketing calls from their life.  I also think it's a good choice for those who are impaired visually or have hearing loss.===========================================

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I LUV this phone!!! If your issue is blocking numerous annoying spam callers…
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I give it 5 stars!!  (I don’t know what the “Lock Feature” is, but just gave that feature 5 stars too).  I had a Panasonic cordless that was several years old and still worked perfectly, but it only allowed me to block 30 numbers at a time, which, with the increase in spam callers, caused me to have to constantly have to go into the block list and remove older numbers to make room for the more recent ones.  WELL… this one lets you block 1000 numbers!!!  (Hopefully that will be enough for a while).  Also, my Panasonic cordless would announce “you’ve got a call from…” and then state about the first 5 numbers, so I was still hearing it ring, tho I know from the area code not to pick it up.  With this AT&T cordless, if the spam callers hang up after my greeting starts playing, I never even hear it ring once nor announced.  And if the number is on my block list, it won’t ring thru either.  I check the phone’s caller list daily and if I see new un-blocked spam calls listed I can easily put them on the block list.  It is also much easier to block calls actively coming in or even afterwards than it was on my older Panasonic.  I only have to push a cpl of buttons to put a number on the block list with the AT&T phone, while with my Panasonic, I had to go to the Menu, scroll down to find block list, erase a number to make room for new number, go back to call list to see new spam number, edit it down to 10 digits (minus the “1”), then save it.  It was a LOT of steps. So this AT&T phone makes it much simpler in way fewer steps to block numbers.  I no longer hear spam caller rings / announcements start in the early morning hours because most of them hang up w/o leaving a message. If they do leave a message - which I have not experienced yet since installing new phone about 4 days ago - I would be able to put them on the block list the same as if they hadn’t.  I have observed that spammers roll thru various exchanges to try to get to you by changing 1 digit in the number they are calling from at a time.  I am very diligent in checking every day for those numbers and block them immediately.  This is why the ability to block 1000 numbers is the MOST important new feature of this phone to me.  One thing that is different, which is not as good as the Panasonic, is setting Quiet Hours… those hours between midnight and whatever time in the morning you do not want the phone to ring at all from anyone.  On the Panasonic, there is a setting to enter the specific hours once that you want to be Quiet and it observes those hours day in and day out; however, with the new AT&T phone, you have to set them each night.  It’s an easy setting, but still so easy to forget to do that before bed every night.  So that is the one deficiency of this phone, and I am surprised AT&T didn’t catch that in their development of it.  But so far, I have remembered to set it nightly.  Even if I forget, I still LUV this phone because it blocks spam callers so perfectly, and that is the main reason I bought it!!  So, if you have a problem with lots of spam callers and want to stop them in their tracks, this is the phone for you!!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So I had my S10 forever and finally decided to get an upgrade. I'm someone that /has/ to read the reviews before I buy a large priced item, and luckily for me I saw another commenter going from the same phone as my old one!For anyone else still using an s10 or similar, I would highly recommend this phone. It's hard to tell how it is when you first get it, as it takes about 2 weeks for the 'starting a new technology' headache to go away, but I can safely say this phone is a good match. There is no new issues, and it's not terrible different than my old phone besides where the buttons on the side are placed and the camera. It also has higher storage so you don't need an SD card ( not that you could insert one anyways as there is no place)But nothing is perfect so here is an easy to digest cons list for people just skimming:-if you are switching from an s10, the buttons are all on one side, there is no button on the left side for volume or power.-to take a screen shot you have to press the lower volume button and power button at the same time, which is kinda hard to do in the beginning.(my fingers were confused in how to do it and not just shut my phone off)-the act of the screen actually shotting takes like, a solid second more than my old phone, I'm not sure if I can change that or if I'm just taking screen shots of to many memes that I start to notice it.-I've had this problem of phone calls cutting out when I'm driving in other areas where it was fine with my old phone. I'm not sure if this is the phone or my provider, but my realitive told me to have the wifi off when driving and that seems to help a lot. She said it had something to do with the phone trying to search for a wifi, I don't know. I don't care. It seems fixed now and I live in a rural area so it can't be helped all the time.-this is a pro to me but could be a con to others: this phone is smaller than an s10. It fits in my hand better.-THERE IS NO AUX INPUT. If I had wired headphone there is no where for me to put them. I can't listen to music in my car with the aux cord anymore, and I don't know how to just make the music play from my stereo through Bluetooth so that upsets me greatly. I can actually hear myself sing in the car now and I hate it.-no SD slot but this phone has mote storage so you shouldn't need it.There you have it, please consider any of these if you want. Another pro that I really wanna hype on is the camera! I love space and have been interested in astrophotography for years. With this phone I was actually able to take a good picture of the moon and....get this...the STARS!!!!I will attach photos for ref

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Video review here. Not an "excellent" condition used phoneVideo review here. Not an "excellent" condition used phone
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have had a Samsung S22 for 3 years now,  having gotten it brand new from Verizon, and I'm very happy with its performance. My family member had to buy a new phone when his dog broke his screen, and Verizon gave me an extra SIM card (with 3 yrs free phone number and service) for being a 33 year customer. So I decided to buy another S22, a used one, which is the phone I'm reviewing here.The phone works. It makes calls. It receives calls. The microphone works. The speaker works. It arrived with 10% charge, so I plugged it in with the cord and plug it came with. It charged to 100% as expected. I used the provided Sim card ejection pin to open sim case and install my Verizon Sim card. All of that worked well.Then I picked out the apps that I wanted, and downloaded them without incident. I set up the phone display settings, notifications, and clock, weather and calculator widgets, again without any trouble. I set up the PIN, the pattern, and the fingerprint reader with no problems.Then I looked closely at the cosmetics of the device that I paid a premium price for, because it was described as in "excellent" condition. The front of the phone looks great. The screen glass is pristine. The sides I would say look "very good" with only one small area of deep scuffing. The back of the case has a lot of scratches and burred scuffs, around all four edges as well as around the corner and top edge of the lens assembly.Because of that scratching and scuffing, I would say that this phone is "good" condition rather than "excellent." It's not clean and smooth enough to say the condition is "very good." Function-wise, I will say, with only 20 hours of use to judge by, is very good. And another plus, in my mind, it's that this phone has the 256gig storage, compared with my other S22 that has only 128gigs.So, all in all I'm happy with the phone. I paid probably $50 more to get an "excellent" condition phone than the used phones in good or very good condition; and I don't believe it was graded accurately, and I feel overcharged because it's only a "good" condition phone in my mind.It works so I'm keeping it. Lesson learned as to condition rating system.

description: If you love to get lost in your entertainment, then Galaxy Z Fold8 is for you. This all-new foldable has an all-new shape that really makes your content shine. On the cover screen, enjoy the perfect ratio for scrolling your socials, and then unfold the wide 7.6" display¹⁰ to immerse yourself in your streaming favorites. Rotate your screen to portrait mode and the same space becomes a full-page e-book, making everything you love feel big, clear and more inviting.When you switch from viewing content to capturing content, Galaxy Z Fold8 is ready. With a 50MP dual camera system and an expansive screen, you can see the details before you snap and admire your pic on an immersive display after.This new design also sets a new record as the world’s lightest fold.¹ But don’t let that fool you —inside, you still get a 4,800mAh battery, Super Fast Charging 2.0⁴ and the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chip to power your immersive on-the-go experience.Galaxy Z Fold8 reshapes how you enjoy content, turning every movie night, reading session and social scroll into an experience that perfectly fits your favorites.
features: SHOP NOW: Get an Amazon gift card when you order Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8. You will receive an email once your gift card is available after the product has shipped. Available until 8/23.

CREATED FOR YOUR CONTENT: Any way you turn it, the new Galaxy Z Fold8 gives you a fuller viewing experience. Designed with your content in mind, this foldable phone is the perfect size to make your movies, books and more incredibly immersive.

WORLD’S LIGHTEST FOLD¹: Galaxy Z Fold8 is the newest foldable phone for content on the go. Unfolded, it fits movies and books for an immersive experience. Folded, it delivers comfortable texting and everyday use — all on the world’s lightest fold.¹

THE BRIGHTEST DISPLAY ON A GALAXY PHONE: Our brightest smartphone display² provides you with a comfortable view, whether you’re inside or outside. Watch movies, play games and scroll with ease no matter where you are.

RECORD. REFRAME. READY FOR SOCIAL³: Record content on Galaxy Z Fold8 and then use My FanCam³ to keep your subject center stage. The result is a social-ready video that focuses on the part of the action you really want.

UNTETHER YOUR ENTERTAINMENT: The long-lasting battery of Galaxy Z Fold8 is built to power hours of entertainment. And when you do need to recharge, Super Fast Charging 2.0⁴ gets you back to what you love quickly.

STAY GAMING-READY: Experience what’s possible with our most advanced Galaxy Z Series processor. From immersive gaming and speedy multitasking to the latest Galaxy AI⁵ features, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 keeps for Galaxy everything running seamlessly.
GET LOST IN YOUR SHOTS: With a 50MP dual camera system and an expansive screen, Galaxy Z Fold8 allows you to see the details before you snap and admire your pic on an immersive display after.
LOCK IN TO THE MOMENT: Bring on the bumps, jumps and chaos. Super Steady Video with Horizontal Lock⁶ keeps your footage perfectly upright for smooth, level footage every time.

SWITCHING FROM IPHONE IS NOW EASIER THAN EVER: The excitement of finding your perfect foldable phone can also bring up anxiety about making the switch from iPhone. Bring over photos, contacts, alarms and passwords. Share files and encrypt messages in a way you’re used to.¹³ And do it all on Galaxy Z Fold8.

What are the key features of Galaxy Z Fold8? 
Galaxy Z Fold8 offers a unique foldable design with long-lasting performance, advanced photography and AI features. Designed with an all-new shpae, the cover screen's 10:16 aspect ratio is perfect for scrolling. 
What is the difference between Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra? 
As our product line evolves, our original Z Fold model has advanced to become Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra and the Z Fold8 model has been resdesigned with an all-new shape. 
I’m switching to Galaxy for the first time. How easy is it? 
The excitement of finding your perfect foldable phone can also bring up anxiety about making the switch from iPhone. Bring over photos, contacts and passwords. Share files and encrypt messages in a way you’re used to. And do it all on Galaxy Z Fold8. 
How durable is Galaxy Z Fold8? 
Galaxy Z Fold8 is fortified with materials that strengthen the device for long-lasting durability. The Armor Aluminum frame provides enhanced protection for the device's internal components and exterior edges without adding excessive bulk. 
Does Galaxy Fold8 support S Pen? 
No Galaxy Z Fold8 does not support S Pen.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: No S pen support and Batter is improved significantly from Fold 7.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Disappointing for the Price, No S Pen Support Is a Major Step BackI really wanted to like the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8, but after using it, I decided to return it. For a phone this expensive, I expected much more.My biggest disappointment is the lack of real S Pen support. I am a student and use my phone for serious reading, studying, highlighting, taking notes, and annotating documents. I knew about the S Pen limitation before purchasing, but I thought a good external stylus would be an acceptable alternative. It was not. The external stylus experience is nowhere near the accuracy and natural writing experience of a real S Pen. On such a large foldable screen, proper pen support would have made perfect sense.The battery life also disappointed me. I expected stronger battery performance from such an expensive flagship device, especially considering that the large display encourages multitasking, reading, video watching, and other demanding uses.The Fold8 certainly has strengths. The large folding display is beautiful, multitasking is impressive, and the phone feels premium. But those things do not justify the price for me when a feature as useful as S Pen support has been removed.For students, researchers, professionals, or anyone who reads and annotates documents regularly, I would think carefully before spending this much money on the Fold8. There are less expensive devices that provide proper active-stylus support and may be much more practical.For nearly $2,000, I expected fewer compromises, not more. I returned mine.

From the manufacturer
Effortless, unmatched, reliable with AT&T DL72419 
The AT&T DL72419 4-Handsets DECT 6.0 Expandable Cordless Home Phone features a built-in digital answering machine, smart call blocker, and a large white backlit display. It offers unsurpassed range, is expandable up to 5 handsets, and with the touch of a button, you can enjoy the high-tech benefits your smartphone offers. Connect to Cell lets you pair and connect up to 2 cell phones or one cell phone and one Bluetooth headset for use with landline calls, as well as access Siri, S Voice, and Google Now. 
Key Features Highlights 
Smart Call Blocker - Stores up to 1000 names and numbers on your block list
Handset screen and keypad - Large 1.8” white backlit display on the handset, high contrast text, lighted keypad
Download Cellphone Phonebook - Up to 1000 Name and number
Caller ID / Call waiting – Storing up to 50 call records*
Quiet mode – Silence the ringer to prevent interruptions
ECO Mode - This power conserving technology reduces power consumption for optimal battery performance.
Call Screening - View the caller details in real time to decide whether to answer
Call Intercept - Blocks calls with no valid caller ID before the phone rings
Expandable up to 5 handsets using just one phone jack (using the DL70019 accessory handset)
*Disclaimer - Use of Caller ID features require a subscription from your telephone service provider. 
Connect to Cell 
Be freed from your cell phone at home with Connect to Cell. It removes any cellular signal dead zone by placing the system’s base and your cell phones to where the stronger signal is. 
Pair and connect up to two cell phones or one cell phone and one Bluetooth headset for use with landline calls
Eliminates cellular signal dead zones by placing the system’s base and your cell phones where the signal is strongest
Siri, S Voice and Google Now access
Digital Answering System with Voice Guide 
Stay informed even when you are away from home. All calls are routed to the built-in digital answering machine when necessary, recording key messages for you. 
Up to 22 minutes of recording time for incoming messages
Built-in Simulated Full-Duplex Handset Speakerphone 
Enjoy clear, two-way conversations with the simulated full-duplex speakerphone. The built-in speakerphone allows both parties to speak and be heard simultaneously, ensuring natural, uninterrupted communication. 
Increase participation by allowing both ends to speak and be heard simultaneously
Working From Home Made Easy 
Manage you calls anywhere in your home or home office through both landline and cell-lines with a cordless handset and full-function base station.

Virtual multi-line operation
Conference between an outside line and up to 4 cordless handsets

Table and wall mountable
English/Spanish/French setup menu
What's a Smart Call Blocker? 
A simple one-time setup to filter unwanted calls while letting trusted ones through 
Quick Setup to let the system working for you 
Set Directory - for your family so their calls will go through without the screening. 1. Press MENU on handset. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Directory, then Select. 3. Press Select again to choose Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then Select. 
Set Allow list - so their calls do not get through the screening. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow list, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter telephone number, then Select. 5. Enter name, then Select. 
Set Block List - to prevent their calls from ringing through. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Block list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then press Select. 
Set Star name list for your trusted organizations - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Star name list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the name (up to 15 characters), then press Select. 
Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Even better voice quality than the one it replaced. Removed two stars later due to issues.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Added 6 8 21I have dropped this item from 5 stars to three. The voice quality is still good.I dropped one star as I said I would becasue the date and time have to be re-set every time the power flickers or goes out. It would have taken a small battery or a capacitor that would probably cost less than a dime to have this not happen.I dropped one star because the directions for adding listings to the directory no longer work. They never worked as printed in the handbook, but I had made a note to correct the part that did not work as printed. (On page 37, if you follow the process in item 4, you need to press Menu/Select to store when you finish.) That whole process no longer works.  If I follow the directions, ADD NEW ENTRY never appears. All it offers me now is the option to replace my first listing.  I can add an item to the directory from the Caller ID, but this is not my usual choice.Here is the original reviewOur former AT&T phone system lasted 12 years and died due to a battery swelling up and destroying the system. We had had to go to third-party batteries because AT&T had quit making them.However, this one has a bit more volume and even better voice quality than the EP-5995 it replaced. This was the main feature we needed, and that alone was enough for me to give it 5 stars. I also appreciate that the contacts only have to be entered on one handset. They then populate across the other handsets.The setup is indeed tedious, but we managed it. Some users say that the date and time will have to be re-set every time the power goes out. If this proves to be the case I will come back and take off one star. I will have to dig out the manual to re-do this. It would have taken only a little bit of engineering and a coin battery to make this unnecessary, and I know it will be a big issue for the many people who got this phone and set it up for older relatives.The message waiting light is indeed dim, although other lights on the handset and base are bright. The labeling of the rocker button on the handset and the base is really hard to see, another issue for the older people who will be a large part of the market for this phone. Thankfully, this model moves the handset Call Block button to the bottom of the phone from the middle of the rocker switch, where it would have been much too easy to press while trying to increase the volume (and thus blocking calls from someone the user probably wanted to talk to). This was an even bigger "gotcha" for an elderly person with vision problems. The new location is not great, but it is better.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Title: Excellent Budget Smartphone – Great Value for the Price!I’ve been using the Samsung Galaxy A14 5G for a while now, and I’m honestly very impressed with what it offers for the price. The phone looks modern and feels solid in the hand, with a nice large display that’s perfect for watching videos, browsing social media, and everyday use. The screen is bright and clear, and the size makes everything easier to see without feeling too bulky.Performance has been smooth for my daily tasks like calls, messages, apps, banking, and streaming. It handles multitasking better than I expected for a budget-friendly device. The 5G connectivity is also a big plus—it provides fast internet speeds when I’m out and about, which makes streaming and downloads much quicker.The battery life is one of my favorite features. It easily lasts me a full day (and sometimes more) without needing to recharge, even with regular use. That’s a huge advantage if you’re busy or travel often. Charging time is reasonable, and I like not having to worry about carrying a charger everywhere.The camera does a really good job for the price range. Photos come out sharp in good lighting, and the different camera modes are fun to use. It’s great for casual pictures, social media posts, and video calls.Setup was simple, the phone came unlocked, and it worked perfectly with my carrier. Overall, I think this is an excellent smartphone for anyone looking for reliability, modern features, and 5G capability without spending a fortune. Definitely a great value purchase—I would recommend it to family and friends.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: hardware as well is operating system overdone
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Germans have a wonderful word concoction: "Verschlimmbessern"Meaning to improve something continuously and by that making gradually worse and eventually useless.In our "update mania" world this here is a classic case.The phone has a way to sensitive touchscreen and no matter what you try from the gazillion settings there is only one to increase the sensitivity but not to decrease it! You can search online that issue.Tests I did show that the touchscreen responds when the finger is actually is not touching the screen but is 0.5- 1mm ( 1/52" - 2/52") away from it!This leads of course to an absurd overreaction when you handle the phone, even with the palm protection on, it reacts unintentionally. Often even it responses before you have actually touched anything simply because you moved your finger without touching the screen!Then there is the OS, by now Android 14. Another effort to overload an overdo many functions and poorly organize them. all of course in the eternal other obsession "security". The [settings] interface is not intuitive and straightforward anymore like it used to be in older android OSs.Whereas like in earlier versions you could customize and prioritize which icon functions you wanted where, that no longer seems to be possible.And then of course the confirmation pop-up window mania.Say you want to turn something off or delete a message/email. You have to go on a regular basis through three confirmations! DUH? Say you select an email or SMS and click on delete, then it asks you first if you want to delete it, and then and then again were you wanted deleted to and finally you need to confirm that! Really? Seriously?notwithstanding that the new and improved absolutely outlandish privacy terms and all other terms all of them with their 10,000 links to other terms about terms and privacy etc. blah blah... I really feel being raped on a daily basis.Furthermore for some reason despite larger screen all the fonts are smaller but layout spacing is larger with more wasted space. (yes I tried the font sizing). Total useless another feature is, that you can choose from an endless variety of different fonts...Any app you start needs a gazillion confirmations requesting permission to give access to this and that, here and there etc. etc. Overall straightforward sensible layout of the interface and functionality is gone.Here's a personal comparison and experience.Before I upgraded to this phone I had a Samsung S5 with OS Android 6.01. Everything worked fine I never had an issue SMS and MMS sent out instantaneously and everything else worked. Of course with new apps the phone became, aside from artificial incompatibilities, slower and slower. P part of a marketing ploy probably.Now I have a Samsung A14 5G with Android 14. MMS take much longer and needs two or three confirmations...And when executing a functioning in an app, next time I open the app I have to navigate back as it doesn't go back like previously by default.There's more but that would take up too much space to writeup here.Remember the peaceful relaxed time when we had a Bell telephone and a typewriter?We were able to communicate and even managed to fly two men to the moon and bring them safely back...

description: The Galaxy A06 is a blend of style, functionality, and innovation. A MediaTek G85 processor delivers seamless multitasking, while Samsung Knox Vault keeps your data secure. With up to two OS upgrades and four years of security updates, this device is built to last. Additional features like Digital Wellbeing and integrated Google Meet video calling enhance productivity and wellness. Designed for those who value performance and elegance, the Galaxy A06 truly stands out.

certifiedBy.name: ECOLOGO
certifiedBy.description: ECOLOGO certified products are made with materials that reduce environmental impact at one or more stages of their life cycle, from raw materials to end of life. An ECOLOGO certification indicates that a product has met environmental performance standards, which include criteria in some or all of the following categories: materials, energy, manufacturing and operations, health and environment, product performance and use, and product stewardship and innovation. Products are evaluated on the applicable criteria through testing and auditing. Learn more about this certification

certifiedBy.name: EPEAT
certifiedBy.description: EPEAT certifies electronic products based on sustainability impacts across their life cycle including requirements for energy efficiency and end-of-life management. An EPEAT registered product can also meet optional more ambitious criteria including reduction of fluorinated greenhouse gases (F-GHGs). Products meeting 50% - 74% optional criteria are 'Silver' and those meeting 75% or more are 'Gold'. Learn more about this certification

Galaxy S25+ is packed with the latest AI¹⁰ innovations that intuitively help you make the most out of your day, almost like a real human assistant. From knocking out multiple tasks with one command to personalized daily insights that help you stay a step ahead, S25+ Series helps free up time for the things you love most.¹Compatible with select apps. Requires Google Gemini account. features: MULTIPLE TASKS WITH ONE ASK: Streamline your day with an assistant that gets you. Ask it to Google search for a pet-friendly vegan restaurant nearby and text it to your friend— your Galaxy S25+ handles multiple tasks with a single ask.¹
START THE DAY SMARTER: Stay one step ahead with a phone that gives you the info you need before you even know you need it with Now Brief.²

REDUCE THE NOISE. REVEAL THE MAGIC: AI Camera with Audio Eraser lets you capture vibrant videos in low light and minimize unwanted noises so you can relive your favorite moments with fewer distractions.³

BRING OUT THE BEST IN EVERY FACE: Capture every portrait with clarity and confidence on the Galaxy S25+ Series. The advanced portrait features adjust skin tones and preserve natural textures, giving every shot a polished, professional look.

MORE POWER TO YOU: Reimagine what’s possible with the Galaxy S25+, featuring our most powerful processor yet. Effortlessly translate your calls, slow down a video, or edit your photos without skipping a beat.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great price for a brand new Samsung phone
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted to own a new phone at least once in my life, and took a friend's recommendation and went with a Samsung.  Should it matter, I'm coming over from a brand I love -- LG -- specifically their V60 model.  It took me a little while to get the hang of the new interface, but that didn't take long at all.  Here's a comparison od some points between the old and new phone.  The Samsung fits a higher resolution screen in roughly the same space as the V60 and, in terms of graphical quality and speed, it's a dramatic difference in favor of the Samsung.  One of the cameras on the V60, I think it's the wide angle lens, is better -- but not so much that I notice it.  The battery in the Samsung lasts a bit longer, but charges *dramatically* faster.  Sound seems roughly the same to my best recollection, but I'll do more comparing between the two.  One plus in favor of the Samsung is that it supports WiFi 7 to the LGs WiFi 6.  Big WiFi speed boost if you have the right network.  Another small point is the fingerprint scanner on the Samsung is easily able to read my print without having to be *exactly* on target, and it does it fast, too.  Let's see... I'm getting a bit long winded here.  I'm I had one tiny knock against the Samsung, it's that it doesn't have a jack for wired headphones like the LG.  Of course nobody else does either, so I really can't hold that against them.Overall, it's a great price (I paid $700) on a new, unlocked Samsung phone -- even if it is last year's model.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's NOT an AT&T device and works fine!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Those that are saying it's an AT&T locked phone is NOT correct! It is a renewed mobile phone so until you switch to the new device from your mobile carrier, it will state the previous carrier. Example, I have Metro PCS so to activate the new device, I logged into my Metro PCS account from the old device, selected 'switch to new device' then entered the new IMEI 15-digit number and wa-hoo...success! Powered off the old device, inserted the new SIM card into the new device, allowed it to update and verify my phone number and I was back in action!!!! Just Google your current carrier information to activate a new device or dial *#6# on your new device to retrieve the IMEI 15-digit number.
