A light on the top of the handset flashes when the phone rings, signaling an incoming call. With the ringers muted, this visual indicator can let you know the calls in silence. Also helpful for those who are hearing impaired. 
Audio Assist button instantly increases incoming call's volume and enhances sound frequencies to make speech easier to understand. It is easy to use, just one press on the Audio Assist button on handset. Press again to turn off. 
2" backlit display on handset with high contrast text makes it easy to read incoming caller ID or call history records. Plus, the lighted handset keypad allows for easy dialing in low light conditions. 
With the full-duplex speakerphone on the handset, this phone set not only lets you speak hands-free but also allows both ends to speak and be heard at the same time. Enjoy conversations that are more true to life. 
Stay informed even when you are away from home. All calls are routed to the built-in digital answering machine when necessary, recording key messages for you. 
Screening calls has never been easier. The handset announces the name of the caller, so you don't have to scramble for the handset to see who's calling. 
Experience the best in long-range coverage and clarity, provided by a unique antenna design and advances in noise-filtering technology. 
What's a Smart Call Blocker? 
A simple one-time setup to filter unwanted calls while letting trusted ones through. 
Quick Setup to let the system working for you 
Set Directory - for your family so their calls will go through without the screening. 1. Press MENU on handset. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Directory, then Select. 3. Press Select again to choose Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then Select. 
Set Allow list - so their calls do not get through the screening. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow list, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter telephone number, then Select. 5. Enter name, then Select. 
Set Block List - to prevent their calls from ringing through. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Block list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then press Select. 
Set Star name list for your trusted organizations - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Star name list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the name (up to 15 characters), then press Select. 
Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

modules.title: What's a Smart Call Blocker?
modules.text:
A simple one-time setup to filter unwanted calls while letting trusted ones through. 
Quick Setup to let the system working for you 
Set Directory - for your family so their calls will go through without the screening. 1. Press MENU on handset. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Directory, then Select. 3. Press Select again to choose Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then Select. 
Set Allow list - so their calls do not get through the screening. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow list, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter telephone number, then Select. 5. Enter name, then Select. 
Set Block List - to prevent their calls from ringing through. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Block list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then press Select. 
Set Star name list for your trusted organizations - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Star name list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the name (up to 15 characters), then press Select. 
Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: With caller ID, call blocking works great
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the AT&T BL102-4 cordless phone set from the Amazon Warehouse (like-new used in original packaging)  when our family switched from a traditional landline setup to a VOIP landline with our local cable provider.  We previously had been using a cordless system from another brand with our phone company's service and the call quality was never good - often lots of crackle on the line, making callers hard to hear.  I wasn't sure if it was the phones, the service, or the cords, so I replaced all of them and started anew.The build quality of this AT&T phone system was a little less substantial than I expected, but the phones do their job and call quality is good.  The handsets and the base feel kind of cheap, but this is an under-one hundred dollar phone system so I guess that's to be expected.  It works well though, and the features are good.The only feature I miss is Bluetooth.  If this system had it  I could pair it with my cell phone, but other than that, it's not missing anything.----------------------------------➡️  SETUP & USE:I put the batteries in the phones and charged them as I went to the included user manual to try and figure out how to set it up.  The manual is a bit overwhelming, but if you read it carefully and go step by step, you can figure it out.Some features on the phone duplicate those offered by my cable company, so I did need to figure out which ones to set up and which ones to leave off on the phone.  For example, my cable provider offers voicemail, and thus using the answering machine feature of this phone system isn't something that I do.Once I set up things like the number of rings before the calls were answered, I started adding numbers into my phone's contacts.  Doing this let these callers come right through, and helped with call blocking.  I set it up so that callers I didn't recognize would have to press the pound button on their phones to get through.  This eliminates robocalls, but real-live telemarketers can still get through.---------------------------------------➡️ CALL BLOCKING FEATURE:Call blocking only works if your phone service provider has caller-ID enabled for your account.It works like this...When a call comes through that you have not put on your call block list already, or that your provider has not filtered, you get an audio announcement of the number and associated caller name.  You can disable the audio announcement if desired.You can then decide if you want to answer or block the call.  If you wish to block it, you press the call block button on the handset which is in the lower right corner.  That stops the call from coming through and the ringing stops on the phone.Call blocking has been a life-changing feature for us.  The combination of our cable provider phone service and this phone has eliminated 98% of our telemarketing calls and all of the robocalls.  We no longer have to unplug our phones to get some sleep, and the calls we do get are nice and clear.------------------------------------------The top 3 reasons I purchased this phone system...1. I got a heck of a deal through the Amazon Warehouse during Prime Day (an additional 20% off the warehouse price), making it under seventy for me.2.  The call blocking feature to eliminate robocalls and telemarketers.3.  The ability to increase the volume easily on the handset, for my hard-of-hearing husband.-----------------------------------------------This phone system works with both traditional phone service providers and VOIP cable company phone services.  It comes with four handsets and has a built-in answering machine along with the call blocking feature that works with the caller ID provided by your phone service provider.The handsets are lightweight, have big numbers that are easy to see along with the LCD display.  The caller ID announce feature is a nice addition and most of the time it's easy to understand.🎯 I think this phone system is a good one for those who want to eliminate robocalls and telemarketing calls from their life.  I also think it's a good choice for those who are impaired visually or have hearing loss.===========================================

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this due to what seemed like pretty awesome and aggressive call Blocker features and the large screen.  I've always bought panasonic but this phone was far more "advanced".  I just set it up and I really dislike how complicated this is.  All phones I've had, for decades, had intuitive set up and I chalked my difficulty up to maybe just not being used to.this brand.  I spent 45 minutes scrolling , hitting buttons, not finding a simple "erase" or "space" anywhere to enter numbers then having the phone save stuff I have to go retype and erase.  I didn't use the manual, having zero problem, ever, setting up a phone, and if you lose the manual good luck setting this up or trying to do "a" thing.  I liked the smart call block  which instructs callers that you're screening calls and to say their name  then press pound to be rung thru.  The manual clearly states that this can block calls you want to have and so don't use it.  Which isn't helpful.  Doctors and others call from private cell phones now and many work from home and aren't using caller-ID branded company phones so its also impractical to block everyone but who is in your phone directory  (another option).  If you want to do this, you cant import or choose the numbers you've added to your directory- you have to retype all the names and numbers,  one by one, again, to your " allow list" .  Many i have in my directory still say "unavailable" above the number which isn't helpful if you have the caller ID speak who is calling so you can go pick it up or let it go to voice mail. A few options you can set up, like allowing everyone in your Directory through didn't work.  I also looked for extra batteries, just in case, and in putting the phone name, I find none listed.  I guess you have to look at the 300 batteries being sold to find the compatible ones but ATT ought to make this easier.  While the screen is large, my smaller one had thicker text and I find this readout spidery and not too easy to read.  Perhaps I'll get used to it but I find this overly complicated, the spoken set up instructions pretty much tell you to read the manual, and alas, it has shrill, annoying ringer tones.  The voice announcer is really weird, pronouncing things slowly and with strange inflection..  Wouldn't buy again and would return if I didn't need a phone this second.  Way too complicated, even.for the easy stuff.UPDATE: I have tried my best to adjust to this phone and persevere.  after months and re-re-reading everything and multiple resets and endless tweaking this phone is a nightmare.  if I leave it on " block everyone but people in my directory" then its fine.  but not practical.  i had it on "block unknown calls" which then started giving me spam numbers calling but without any ID to it.  my best friend continually rings thru as "unknown caller" tho she's in my allow list and directory,  yet the talking ID will announce her name.  many, many times I'll answer the phone and it goes to one, constant ring, like an alarm going off.  it won't answer and I can't turn this off! I have to yank the batteries out. the person calling gets dead air.  many times someone will call and hear me but I can't hear them.  I even called ATT who muddled thru the same instruction tome as I have. people in directory show up as "unknown caller" in spite of being allowed. Jerks calling can't be blocked because if you block number you have to enter a name, too, and you cant put in "unavailable " or "out of area" . block doesn't go by name but you cant just block a number, period.  many times phone will ring (when using the screener) and I'll pick.it up to be asked by the phone screen to "press any number and then pound" which is what the CALLER is supposed to get, not me.  if I do this im told by phone voice this is an invalid phone number so my call can't be completed. huh??? the actual caller will tell me the phone rang forever then went dead silent.  my caller ID will show my number called me and as "unknown"  I give up.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I LUV this phone!!! If your issue is blocking numerous annoying spam callers…
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I give it 5 stars!!  (I don’t know what the “Lock Feature” is, but just gave that feature 5 stars too).  I had a Panasonic cordless that was several years old and still worked perfectly, but it only allowed me to block 30 numbers at a time, which, with the increase in spam callers, caused me to have to constantly have to go into the block list and remove older numbers to make room for the more recent ones.  WELL… this one lets you block 1000 numbers!!!  (Hopefully that will be enough for a while).  Also, my Panasonic cordless would announce “you’ve got a call from…” and then state about the first 5 numbers, so I was still hearing it ring, tho I know from the area code not to pick it up.  With this AT&T cordless, if the spam callers hang up after my greeting starts playing, I never even hear it ring once nor announced.  And if the number is on my block list, it won’t ring thru either.  I check the phone’s caller list daily and if I see new un-blocked spam calls listed I can easily put them on the block list.  It is also much easier to block calls actively coming in or even afterwards than it was on my older Panasonic.  I only have to push a cpl of buttons to put a number on the block list with the AT&T phone, while with my Panasonic, I had to go to the Menu, scroll down to find block list, erase a number to make room for new number, go back to call list to see new spam number, edit it down to 10 digits (minus the “1”), then save it.  It was a LOT of steps. So this AT&T phone makes it much simpler in way fewer steps to block numbers.  I no longer hear spam caller rings / announcements start in the early morning hours because most of them hang up w/o leaving a message. If they do leave a message - which I have not experienced yet since installing new phone about 4 days ago - I would be able to put them on the block list the same as if they hadn’t.  I have observed that spammers roll thru various exchanges to try to get to you by changing 1 digit in the number they are calling from at a time.  I am very diligent in checking every day for those numbers and block them immediately.  This is why the ability to block 1000 numbers is the MOST important new feature of this phone to me.  One thing that is different, which is not as good as the Panasonic, is setting Quiet Hours… those hours between midnight and whatever time in the morning you do not want the phone to ring at all from anyone.  On the Panasonic, there is a setting to enter the specific hours once that you want to be Quiet and it observes those hours day in and day out; however, with the new AT&T phone, you have to set them each night.  It’s an easy setting, but still so easy to forget to do that before bed every night.  So that is the one deficiency of this phone, and I am surprised AT&T didn’t catch that in their development of it.  But so far, I have remembered to set it nightly.  Even if I forget, I still LUV this phone because it blocks spam callers so perfectly, and that is the main reason I bought it!!  So, if you have a problem with lots of spam callers and want to stop them in their tracks, this is the phone for you!!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great phone...but compared to what?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Tldr: Good phone for this price, noticeably better than older A13 and I wish more people would include context to their reviews. Glad I bought mine.I'm leaving a long and detailed review because I got tired of reading through reviews that seemed contradictory, or said something was "bad" but without any context. If I made a poor choice buying a phone I'd likely be stuck with it for some years. I'm hoping this helps others like myself who are reading the reviews.Ok, so the most important context is what phone I'm coming from over to the A17 5g. My old phone was Samsung A13 5g. My opinions of the new phone will be largely based on how they compare to the previous phone I used. So it's budget phone to budget phone, with the A17 having approximately 3-4ish years newer tech (or same tech but cheaper.) Both phones are being used on metro PCS (T mobile) network.So I've now had the A17 for exactly one week. I primarily use my phone for android auto, text, checking email, web browser, occasional YouTube and maybe once per week on some games. I don't use it for heavy loads like massive file transfers or rendering video. It's fairly light use overall.So far, the things I've been most pleased with are the screen and software/system layout. The screen has decent color and brightness and is MUCH better than the A13. Both screens claim to run at 90hz but the change from the old 270 PPI (I believe stands for pixel per inch or some equivalent) to 385 PPI feels massive. Much cleaner image from text to images. The change from LCD to AMOLED gives much better contrast with deeper colors. The software and system layout are a bit harder to describe in detail. It's more of a personal/ascetic preference. Things look and feel a lot cleaner. There are added optional features like side slide tabs to house shortcuts for certain apps. Another feature is top down swipe from the right for system shortcuts and from the left for notification, so they are smashed together.Another improvement, though less so than the screen and software changes, is in the speed and responsiveness of the phone. This one also needs to be put in context a bit. I'm sure some would complain about it while coming from a more expensive and technologically superior phone. I have my own bias, as I'm coming from an inferior phone which had over 3 years of use (slowing it down over time.) I also use it for mostly light tasks. That being said, I am pleased that the phone is noticeably more responsive than my old one. Most of the lagging happens on start up (goes away after a few mins while the phone is connecting a bunch of apps and putting out/requesting info like date/time/location.) When I booted it for the first time, that was the worst lag I had. It will also slow down if you have several apps running at the same time.  I feel like that's obvious, but some people genuinely don't know that if you hit the home button to leave an app, you need to bring up multi view and actually swipe the box away to close it fully. If you never close apps and never restart your phone on occasion it WILL slow way down. While using the phone for max 1 or 2 things at time it runs perfectly fine, and is better than the A13.Battery life is good. I went from appx. 5000mAh to 5000mAh phones, so besides the slight degradation in the old phones battery life it should be the same. 5000mAh for my uses feels excellent overall. It can go for a full 2 days without charging. Charging speed itself seems improved, but that's never mattered too much for me so I can't comment much. Seems fine though, roughly 1.5h charge from mostly dead to full. That's using a 25w fast charger block and appropriate USB c cable. I didn't use the cable that came with the phone so I can't comment. It didn't come with a charger block, by design. Your mileage on charge speed will vary based on what you're using to charge the phone with. The phone can't charge at full speed if you're using a 5w charger from 15 years ago.I don't have much to say about the camera. I rarely take photos and when I do it's usually quick snap shots of paper instructions or to share location. I believe (though I'm not sure) the A13 was also 50mp front camera but either the the other 2 lenses have been upgraded or they improved the camera software, because pictures do look a bit cleaner. It's not night and day or anything, but it looks better to my eye. Camera is also faster to adjust light and contrast when first focusing on a object, as compared to the old A13.Build quality seems a little improved. They are both budget phones and how build quality "feels" is inherently subjective but to me it does seem a little better.A quick note on activating this new phone...this may only be an issue I personally had, but in case this helps someone else I'd like to include it. I had a bit of trouble switching my physical SIM card out of my old phone and into the new. The metro app was telling me the phone wouldn't be compatible unless I changed phone plans (which is BS.) I had to call customer service and they opted to use the eSiM feature, rather than swapping the physical Sim. I noticed they also used the new phones 2nd SIM number to activate it, while i had tried using first. If you're having trouble perhaps check the phones info from the settings menu, and then try eSIM activation using the 2nd address. It worked fine for me after this.Samsung has a quick transfer feature if your previous phone was a Samsung. It basically copies over everything from your old phone, including apps, pictures, contacts and even text message history ect. It took 3 or 4 attempts (it didn't want to connect and dropped the connection once at 30% complete.) Luckily if it disconnects part way through, it will pick up where it left off, without needing to restart. Once it finally had a stable connection it took me about 6 minutes, it will vary based on how much stuff you have to move over. You need to download an app to do the transfer, but it will prompt you and take you to it's link.Summery: I find it pretty impressive how nice this phone feels both compared to its older model and for its price point in general. I found it frustrating that people would say this part or that was crap or great, but without giving any context to what they based that opinion off of. In my opinion, based on how cheap this phone is and compared to its older model (A13) this is an awesome phone so far, being one week in. Screen is a big improvement, system software and layout is better (IMO) and they seem to be making incremental improvements to things like the camera and overall build. For this price point I find it really impressive what you actually get. If you're coming from an older mid range phone I expect it will either be inferior or about the same. If you're coming from another phone in the 200 range it should be decent to good. For less than 200 and for what I use it for though, I'm very happy I bought this phone.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this to replace a Samsung A50 that was purchased in October 2019. Yes, 2019! That's before the world changed forever due to a pandemic. And that alone should tell you how infrequently I change phones and what my priorities in life are. I'm a simple woman with simple needs.There wasn't anything really wrong with my old phone but t unfortunately I cracked the screen and it was almost as much to fix it as it was to get a new one. So since it was practically a dinosaur I chose to "upgrade" and decided to take the chance on getting this model after doing a lot of research. I didn't want to spend a lot of money because I mainly use my phone for basic tasks, talking, texting, etc. I don't do any gaming, heavy streaming or lots of downloading. At most I'll watch a YT video or scroll sparingly on SM if time permits.It arrived quickly and came unlocked as described. That's about it for positive feedback. It was really surprising to me that this phone didn't perform nearly as well as it's almost 7 year old predecessor. Let's start with the fact that it took over 4 hours to do a transfer at the mobile store. Then I learned I really didn't have enough storage so a lot of my texts didn't transfer over. The next thing is I keep running out of space and have to keep deleting photos & videos. Now keep in mind these are the same photos from my old A50. I also have almost the same specs on this phone as there is on the A50 so I don't understand why this is happening.Yes, I know things change but I'm not a fan of the new texting features. They're so annoying, especially auto-correct and the "typing" bubble like the iPhone. And I don't find this to be very intuitive so I have trouble changing certain features easily. I have to dig and dig to find what I need.The UI (?) updates are constant and very annoying. Internet pages or tabs will close or switch for no reason and the phone is also laggy as heck. For example, sometimes it takes at least 4-7 seconds to capture a screenshot. Or at times there's a long delay to move from one part of an Internet page to another. What's crazy is I'm not the type of user who requires everything on my phone to move at the speed of light. I can accept a delay here or there but it's a constant waiting game with this phone. And don't get me started on how terrible the camera is. I absolutely despise every picture this camera takes and selfie are the worst! They have everyone looking haggard as heck, no matter what the setting. My A50 camera was 1000x better than this and I could always find a way to take a flattering photo.When I initially read all the negative reviews (and I mean ALL) I incorrectly assumed some of complaints were from folks who were used to swapping out their $2K phones every year. They had high standards and this is a low budget phone so they were disappointed. I get it. It's hard to enjoy beer when you have champagne tastes. But I was quite mistaken. A lot of the complaints are very valid and quite accurate.If you're looking for quality on a budget this ain't it. Trust me. This phone is probably best for a 10-year old child. Take it from someone with super low standards and who kept their own phone for an actual child's formative years. I'll keep it because I don't want to spend more money right now but do yourself a favor and keep your expectations low. If you need a high performance phone look elsewhere. I wish I did.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Features and Value, But Smart Switch Had Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: While the phone setup had a major hiccup, the overall experience has been excellent.The Setup Headache (Data Transfer)Setting up the phone and transferring data from the old device was a bit confusing and frustrating. The transfer app kept insisting on an update, but the download would just sit on "pending" forever and never actually progress. After wasting some time waiting, we finally aborted the automated transfer and did everything manually. If you run into the same issue, saving yourself the headache and going the manual route from the start might be faster.The Good Stuff: Features & PerformanceOnce the manual setup was done, the actual user experience has been fantastic. For the price, this phone is packed with incredible value and high-end features:Built-in AI Assistants: Having both the Gemini app and Microsoft Copilot ready to go right out of the box is incredibly convenient for quick searches, drafting, and productivity.Smart Camera Features: The hand recognition for selfies is a game-changer. You just show your palm to the camera, and it triggers the timer—no more awkward stretching to hit the shutter button.Excellent Value: Despite the initial software download glitch during setup, the phone itself offers a ton of modern functionality that makes it very worth the money.The VerdictThe phone itself is a 5-star device for features and value, but I'm knocking off one star due to the frustrating data transfer glitch. If you don't mind a little manual setup, it is a fantastic, feature-rich phone that won't break the bank!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For starters; the price on these phones is great. Between having the reassurance of Amazon buyer protection, and the benefit of knowing the device has been tested for performance, it’s well worth it.I needed a new phone fast after my cat knocked mine  into the sink ☹️ Rice fixed it for a while, but it was only temporary before it died altogether.I hate buying phones and avoid it whenever possible. 99% of mine belonged to someone in my family first. And i was good with that. Needless to say, my cat didn’t wait for someone in my family to upgrade. I was on my own this time.Okay.... that’s not entirely true. My grandma had an iPhone 7 sitting around so that held me over in the meantime. Going from an iPhone 11 Pro Max to an iPhone 7 was….bad. It was too dam small, in every possible way.  32 gigs of memory!! I needed an upgrade. Fast. My 11 year old was bullying me relentlessly. And that’s on me. They had my old XR (formerly my dad’s)I scoured FB marketplace. I’d decided upgrade a little, so I could feel better about the switch.  I didn’t want to feel backed me into a corner by my cat’s recklessness. I would get a slightly newer model in a fun colour.Marketplace had plenty.  Sending message after message from my iPhone 7, I worried. “This person seems too eager”, “this one has been posted so long”, “I want a purple, but the only purple one listed has less storage space” and “the pretty green one has a small crack”, “this guy lives 2 hours from me” and “Battery life? Errr last time I checked it was like 74%?….no, I can’t take a screenshot of it, it’s turned off”…. “cash only please” Etc.So much pressure. What happens if the thing doesn’t work? That’s $300+ down the drain. I knew I couldn’t afford new. But I hated the idea of buying something used from a stranger on Facebook. I didn’t want to get scammed, and I also didn’t want to settle.That’s when I remembered good ol’ Amazon. Maybe I’d check there. Just for funsies. Probably out of my budget, but it couldn’t hurt.Sure enough, refurbished devices selling “like new!” Mostly same cost or less than what I’d found so far. Surely there was a catch? I read through everything, tested by Amazon, includes all the specs, unlocked, I can pick the colour, the storage size, the condition, etc. AND I could have it delivered to me tomorrow??! With a warranty?!!I recovered from my brief stint of disappointment after learning the 12’s don’t come in yellow. Then fought hard to decide between mint and lavender. The lavender would take an extra day to arrive. Mint it was!!As promised, it arrived the next day. It was in beautiful shape. 128g’s, mint green, not a single scratch, 86% battery life. All for less than I would have paid to some stranger for a 64g with some “small scratches”Once my case and screen protector arrived I excitedly set it up and synced my data.Oh no.The FACE ID DIDNT WORK 😭After becoming used to facial recognition, having that yanked away, and dealing with a 7 for over 2 weeks—  I was desperate for the convenience of Face ID. I had been using my fingerprint. Like a *caveman*.Not to mention I have Blink 182 tickets, and it specifically states facial recognition is required to access the mobile tickets. Idk if that’s true, but I needed Face ID!!I googled, I contacted apple support. Fixing it could be upwards of $300. That’s almost what I paid for the whole phone!!I realllllly didn’t want to be stuck without a phone again. But I also wanted one fully functioning.So I reached out to Amazon support and explained. The rep was incredibly helpful (as most Amazon reps are) and after bts failed, she advised the ship was a 3rd party seller, and she  send a message to them. “If they don’t fix it by (insert date) contact us back and we’ll make this right” she encouraged.I’m ngl. I was nervous. I didn’t have high hopes, having dealt with 3p sellers on Amazon in the past. At least Amazon had my back, ig. The concert wasn’t till July. Even without facial recognition, it was loads better than the  7. I could make do in the meantime.The seller came in clutch though, and my worry was unwarranted. They responded within minutes. They were receptive, apologetic, and more than willing to help.As I’d anticipated, they offered a refund or exchange, as soon as they received the return. I explained my concern with not having a phone for several days or more; and the merchant offered to overnight a replacement as soon as the return was dropped off.I could deal with one day without a phone! I gratefully accepted. That was Saturday night, we made plans to catch up Monday for the return instructions and for them to overnight it.Monday I reached back out; and they were ready to ship, BUT they *had no more green….* 🫢 SHOCK“…do you have purple”No. :( just blue, white, and black.THIS WAS A HUGE BUMMER.It’s silly I know, and the definition of *first world problems “.. but I mean…. My change of heart about this whole phone thing HINGED ON THE FUN COLOUR. Without it, I was just a person…out $350… because my cat was thirsty while I was watching YouTube while washing dishes. I needed a cool colour. Plus,  I’d already gotten the matching case! Clear with mint green borders.It wasn’t even a fun blue… it was a dark, serious, navy blue. It was pretty and classy, but I wanted something fun. I even asked if he had any older models in yellow 😭😭 no luck,They told me they’d be restocking in a day or so. Still, no greens or purples came in.Ugh. Reality was setting in. I was going to have to settle. It was fine, I thought. At least it would be a fully functioning phone.No. I wasn’t ready to let go. They assured me I could take my time to decide, and I asked if we could wait another week in case one came in. If it didn’t, *then* I would choose from the options available.I messaged them Wednesday afternoon, bracing myself for the answer…. THEY GOT IN PURPLE! YAY.They sent a label, I dropped it off, sent a photo, and had my new phone the next morning.they’d said overnight shipping… but wow! I’d dropped off the return around 3pm, and had the replacement by noon the next day. I didn’t even have my new case yet 😅Despite the Barney-Esque colour scheme my mint green case created, the lavender is GORGEOUS and I’m actually sort of glad the green didn’t work out.Don’t get me wrong, the green is also  gorgeous.. but in the end I’m glad I ended up with the lavender. I was overjoyed when I was prompted to set Face ID during setup. Worked brilliantly, as did everything else.Great packaging, no cosmetic flaws, amazing battery life, customer service was great, and best of all… ITS PURPLE!Can’t wait to pair it with the new case. I’m so glad I went this route where I have some peace of mind as a buyer.I’m grateful to the seller for being so helpful and patient with me as insufferable as I must have seemed making such a fuss over colour preferenceIf you’re nervous buying a phone used or refurbished too, hopefully you can take comfort in knowing- this seller is legit. You receive a good quality product, and, speaking from experience, they’ll gladly help resolve any issues you may run into.

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer Camera  Camera  Camera  Camera  Camera  TrueLens Engine 4  Nothing OS  Nothing OS  Nothing OS  Nothing OS  Nothing OS  Nothing OS  Chipset  Performance  Battery  Display
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Design 
It's metal now 
Our engineers used aircraft-grade aluminium to build the unibody on Phone (4a) Pro, bringing a future-forward, metallic flicker into our distinct mechanical design. Cold to the touch, the metal unibody is designed to dissipate heat with remarkable speed. 
Glyph Matrix 
Flagship-grade Glyph Matrix 
Put your screen down and reduce distractions. The Glyph Matrix highlights important alerts at a glance, plus handy tools like a timer, selfie mirror and more. 
Camera 
Pro 3-Camera System 

A pro 3-camera system lets you capture every detail from 0.6x wide-angle to 140x ultra zoom. It's powered by a 50 MP Sony main camera. 
50 MP OIS Sony 1/1.56" main camera / 50 MP OIS periscope camera / 120° Sony ultra-wide camera / 32 MP front camera 
Camera 
140x ultra zoom 

Phone (4a) Pro is equipped with a 50 MP OIS periscope camera with up to 140x ultra zoom, making it the most powerful phone zoom on the market. 
Camera 
Create in 4K video 

Capture ultra-detailed 4K videos and Ultra XDR Full HD footage with exceptional quality in any lighting condition. 
Camera 
Make every shot cinematic 

Fine-tune with 7 camera settings, shoot in RAW for more control or apply ready-made presets created by the Nothing Community. 
Camera 
AI Eraser 

New to the Nothing Gallery app, AI Eraser instantly removes unwanted objects, people and reflections with a single tap.* It runs fully on-device, so your photos never leave your phone. 
*Circle to Erase coming soon. 
TrueLens Engine 4 

Phone (4a) is powered by TrueLens Engine 4, advanced multi-frame RAW processing and 12-layer AI segmentation for Ultra XDR photos, Motion Photos, portraits and lifelike details. 
Nothing OS 
Life runs easier on Nothing OS 

A calmer, personalised and intentional experience with smart tools to keep you focused. Built on Android 16 with 3 years of OS updates and 6 years of security updates. 
Nothing OS 
Essential AI tools 

Essential AI tools help you capture, find, remember, and create by adapting to the way you think and live. 
Nothing OS 
Essential Space 

Essential Space is your second memory. It's a place for you to capture and save what matters. Use the Essential Key to instantly capture an idea, screenshot, photo or voice note. Our powerful AI processing makes sense of it by creating intelligent summaries, extracting key information and to-dos, and even helping you remember upcoming events. You capture. Essential Space takes care of the rest. 
Nothing OS 
Essential Search 

Essential Search is Nothing’s own AI-powered search. Instead of giving you a list of links, it delivers concise, to-the-point answers without wasting your time. Look up news, recipes or get translations instantly. Integrated directly into Nothing OS, Essential Search works without opening any apps. Just swipe up on your home screen and start typing in the search bar. 
Nothing OS 
Essential Memory 

Essential Memory helps you recall important information naturally. Memories are created from what you capture in Essential Space, adding personal context to the answers you get from Essential Search. 
Nothing OS 
Essential Apps 

Essential Apps let you create small, personal tools using simple language. Instead of downloading apps, you shape what you need around your day. These tools live directly on your home screen, stay active, and respond when you need them. They feel less like apps you open and more like tools that are already there, ready to use. 
Chipset 
Class-leading Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 

Class-leading Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 delivers top-tier performance with seamless multitasking, AI processing, and ultra-smooth gaming. 
Performance 
Pro-level gaming 

FPS gameplay for over 60 minutes, with 2,500 Hz instant touch sampling rate for ultra-responsive, longer, and more stable sessions. The X-axis linear motor adds responsive haptic feedback that brings your games to life. 
Battery 
Last longer 

Charge in minutes, last for days with a 5,080 mAh battery. 
20 hours of YouTube. 25 hours of Instagram scrolling. 28 hours of listening to music. 45 hours of voice calls. 
Display 
6.83'' ultra-smooth display 

1.5K high-resolution flexible AMOLED display 
5,000-nit peak brightness 
144 Hz adaptive refresh rate 
10-bit colour / 1.07 billion vivid tones

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very solid phone. I love it so far!!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Where do I start? I recently left the Samsung ecosystem for the Nothing brand and have no regrets. I now have the Phone (4a) Pro, the Ear (3), Headphones (a) and the CMF Watch 3 Pro. First off, the phone looks AMAZING once you've got it in hand. The solid aluminum build is extremely well built, the "techy" looking camera bump is a great aestethic choice as I've gotten many compliments since I bought the phone. I chose the Nothing brand because of the look of their products. No other company is doing what Nothing is doing and I commend them for it. The processor  is snappy and handles mostly anything I throw at it. The shots I've gotten from the camera is on par if not better than my previous Galaxy phones. But the one thing I absolutely love the most is the Glyph Matrix. It's highly customizable and you can even upload simple images to show up when you get certain notifications. For example, I put an image of the letter "W" for WhatsApp notifications, a smiley face for text messages, the letter "a" for Amazon notifications so on and so forth. I mostly have the current time showing on the Glyph Matrix and people always ask me what kind of phone I have. The 5,080mah battery is absolutely solid and I easily get a whole day of battery life with heavy use. It's sad that a lot of people have never heard of the Nothing brand. I've been following Nothing since they came out with the Phone (1) and I've always admired the design choices they've made. Finally they made a Phone that I can get behind and throw my money at =DNO regrets! you will not be disappointed!!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Unfortunately, I have got give the 4a Pro a "mid" review as it is NOT fully unlocked, and not compatible with Verizon.  Unlocked typically means a device works on all carriers.  Its buried in the listing fine print that the 4a Pro is "not recommended with Verizon", but still implies that it works.  This is categorically incorrect as I spent 1 hour with Tier 2 VZW support trying to get the IMEIs for this device recognized on their CDMA network.To be fair, the 4a Pro feels extremely quality, and is very sleek.  I pre-ordered this device weeks ago with high anticipation, and physically the phone didn't let down.  I did not have time to test the full Nothing version of Android (since it wouldn't register on Verizon), but what I did experience was postitive - the screen and OS were both responsive, smooth and fluid.  Speaker quality was great and volume was louder than my old S22 Ultra without distortion.The 4a Pro is potentially a very high value option, considering the price point and what Nothing is trying to do to disrupt the cell phone market.  But do not consider this device if you are a Verizon customer or leveraging a similar CDMA based carrier!

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: To be clear right off the bat, my main phone is a OnePlus 15.I got the Nothing Phone 4a Pro to serve as my work phone, not expecting too much from it...only to be blown away.OxygenOS on the OP15 is the smoothest but NothingOS on the 4aP is shockingly close and it just looks and feels better to me (AOSP but umproved, just like what OxygenOS used to be before they turned it into another iOS wannabe).The photos from the main and telephoto cameras are surprisingly similar in daytime shots(the 4aP only has less saturated shots, but the detail preservation is actually better).The same sadly cannot be same about video recording, that's definitely worse on the 4a Pro (but it's not horrible).And the metal unibody...I missed that so much.All in all, this phone is a pleasant surprise, and Nothing OS is my personal favorite now (in comparison to HyperOS, OxygenOS, PixelUI and OneUI from other flagships I own/owned).To anyone who is considering getting a phone while staying in the 500 € price range and wants a well-rounded device, I can wholeheartedly recommend this one.

bookDescription: Mobile Phones and Tablets Repairs is a complete manual that answers all the basic and professional level questions for entrants into mobile computing devices technical support segment. The book takes the reader one step at a time , combining a strong theoretical knowledge base about mobile devices - how they function, description of their internal components, their internal electronics with tutorial on basic foundation electronics for repairs and merged it with descriptive easily practicable tutorials on both hardware and software related repair procedures for mobile phones and tablets. Information about cell phone hardware and software repair tools is covered with product listings and guides for success. If there is any complete guide-book on computer repairs ever known, then this book is the complete guide-book for mobile phones and tablets repairs! If you are seeking for a way by which you could exchange personal services for money, then this book is for you. It is a complete Do-It-Yourself Guide book. In book stores all over the world, there are hardly complete repair guides for mobile telephones and tablets repairs although you may find many for PCs. This book is for the young people, students, or anyone seeking for a good resource for practical learning towards self reliance. In this century, the age of mobile communication and computing, it is one of the hottest tech repair service segment. Through the pages of this book, a reader would train to become a great mobile phone technician with a brighter and faster earning potential than most PC technicians. What this book teaches is practicable towards becoming also, a good PC technician. The tutorials cover Microelectronic device dis-assembly and re-assembly, troubleshooting, BGA soldering, detailed electronics fundamentals, flash programming and many more. The book ends with a chapter of information on how to set up shop and efficiently manage a mobile repair services support center. Discover the secrets of mobile phone repair with this book!

I'd suggest looking at REWA for their online courses or finding a hands on class somewhere because just about every book of this genre is garbage. This book contains no information on Iphones or Samsung models which are the two most popular phones so why this book is even exists I have no clue. The diagrams are black and white, hard to follow and the only useful information is the things that somebody searching for a "manual" of this type, would already know such as what equipment you'll want to have, etc. The print itself looks like it had been Xeroxed from an old machine sitting in some teenagers dungeon. The whole book has no relevance to the technology being used today i.e. motherboards, smart chips, devices for wiping and rewriting data, etc. I learned what I could on YouTube and other websites. Don't buy this book unless you like wasting money.

In frustration over missing calls  for two weeks  (since we activated the phone), my dad  threw it, smashed it and shattered it to smithereens. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: OverviewThe Samsung Galaxy S22 is a flagship smartphone that represents the cutting edge of mobile technology. As a factory-unlocked device, it offers flexibility for use with various carriers. With a sleek design, impressive hardware, and advanced camera capabilities, the Galaxy S22 is designed to cater to both casual users and tech enthusiasts.Design and Build QualityThe Galaxy S22 boasts a refined and modern design, with a premium glass and metal build. It feels solid in hand, with a sleek and elegant aesthetic that is characteristic of Samsung’s high-end devices. The device is available in various colors, catering to different style preferences.DisplayThe phone features a 6.1-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display with a resolution of 2400 x 1080 pixels. The screen offers vibrant colors, deep blacks, and excellent brightness levels, making it perfect for media consumption and gaming. The 120Hz refresh rate provides smooth scrolling and a responsive touch experience.PerformanceUnder the hood, the Galaxy S22 is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 (or Exynos 2200, depending on the region), paired with 8GB of RAM. This combination ensures top-tier performance, allowing for seamless multitasking, smooth gaming, and efficient handling of demanding applications. The device runs on Samsung’s One UI, based on Android, offering a user-friendly interface with a plethora of customization options.CameraOne of the standout features of the Galaxy S22 is its camera system. The phone is equipped with a triple-camera setup on the back, consisting of a 50MP main sensor, a 12MP ultra-wide sensor, and a 10MP telephoto sensor with 3x optical zoom. The camera performs exceptionally well in various lighting conditions, producing sharp and detailed photos.The 8K video recording capability is a notable highlight, providing incredibly high-resolution videos that are future-proof and offer impressive clarity. The front-facing 10MP camera also delivers high-quality selfies and video calls.StorageWith 128GB of internal storage, the Galaxy S22 offers ample space for apps, photos, videos, and other media. However, it lacks a microSD card slot, so users looking for additional storage will need to rely on cloud services or opt for a higher storage variant if available.Battery LifeThe Galaxy S22 is equipped with a 3700mAh battery, which provides decent battery life. It supports fast charging, wireless charging, and reverse wireless charging. With moderate use, the phone can easily last a full day, but heavy users might need to top up the battery by the evening.ConnectivityAs a factory unlocked device, the Galaxy S22 offers great flexibility for use with different carriers. It supports 5G connectivity, ensuring fast data speeds where available. Other connectivity features include Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.2, NFC, and USB Type-C.Additional FeaturesFingerprint Sensor: An under-display ultrasonic fingerprint sensor provides secure and fast unlocking.IP68 Rating: The device is water and dust resistant.Stereo Speakers: The phone offers a great audio experience with its stereo speaker setup.ConclusionThe Samsung Galaxy S22 is a powerful and versatile smartphone that excels in design, performance, and camera capabilities. Its 8K video recording, premium build quality, and vibrant display make it a standout device in the competitive smartphone market. While the absence of expandable storage might be a downside for some, the 128GB internal storage should suffice for most users. Overall, the Galaxy S22 is a solid choice for anyone looking for a high-end Android smartphone with cutting-edge features.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice A36 phone upgrade from the A35
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a great, unlocked phone. Worked perfectly on our ATT plan (U.S.) so, perfectly compatible.Just popped the sim out of the A35 and into this A36.It worked right off the bat and did not have to call carrier to change IMEI either.Had to change the language to English on initial boot since this is an international phone.Our A35 was bricked after being caught in a two-hour rainstorm on a motorcycle ride, oops. Basically, submerged in water for two hours at 65mph.However, the transfer of photos, contacts and everything else went seamlessly from the shared server (aka "cloud" lol) backup. Windows phone link transferred any (intentional) non-cloud files from the A35's SD to the A36 quickly as well.This phone is slightly bigger than the A35 so, a new case was in order as well. Had no trouble finding a cool one here on Amazon.This A36 is fast, and 256GB so, nice default storage.Now, storage. The only thing I do not like about the A36. There is no SD card allowed with the carriers SIM installed.It has dual SIM yes but, no way to put an SD in the other SIM position.You have to use either an SD or SIM(s). The SD goes into the entire SIM slot after you remove the SIM tray.Well, I don't like that but, the shared servers hold so much data now-a-days it is not too much of an issue.The A36 connected flawlessly with Windows Phone Link (link to phone) so, using the PC for file transfer, messaging, photo management and phone calls is a breeze and SUPER handy.The web browser(s) is/are current and updated unlike i devices which are 4 years behind in processing css, html5 (and other) code which, as a coder is very important to me. I am still forced to write backward compatible and unique code to support these outdated parsers. Hey, i's are great hardware but, lack in the os and policies. As a full time coder for 35 years now, I will digress. I use my phone as a tool, not the other way around.The Android 16 (comes with 15 but updates quickly to 16) is great and allows me to install whatever I want and test the applications I have written with ease.Did not come with any bloatware just the normal stuff which prompts you to allow or disallow on setup (games center whatever). Not forced into installing crap that eats battery in the background or collects data.The 50MP camera is just simply amazing and video is as well.This A36 connected to my wife's Galaxy Watch very quickly and easily.This A36 feels really good in my hand and seems pretty durable.We got the white one but, matters not as it went right into a case.This unlocked A36 is a great workhorse phone for us and WAY cheaper than trendy phones that have less capability.My wife and I are very happy with the A36 but, will toss into the saddlebag next time we ride in a downpour!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Samsung A36 from Cell Universal - two thumbs up!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I decided I needed a new phone and after a reasonable amount of research, decided I wanted to pursue this Samsung A36 because it had what I needed with features just right for me and my needs.  I've always been a Samsung guy which means I also appreciate Android with all its seamless ties to Google and related accounts.  Previous Samsung phones I used included Galaxy S series and most recently, the Z Flip 3 (don't get me started on that model but suffice to say I was on my second screen which had long since started cracking at the crease).I needed an unlocked edition of the A36 and my Amazon search including a few filters led me to the one I ultimately purchased from vendor, "Cell Universal," who currently shows as a 4.7 star vendor based on last 12 months' ratings, and which includes 95% 4- or 5-star ratings.  I had doubts about buying a new unlocked phone online but I found the price very reasonable, so coupled with great vendor ratings I made the order.  Vendor did not disappoint!  :-)Package arrived on time and the day after it arrived I got to work on unboxing it and commencing setup.  Contents appeared complete:  brand new phone in what appeared like original factory wrapping, unsealed, and accompanied by post card that vendor left in the package that contained important "before you start" information.  Vendor also included a 3rd party plug adaptor, allowing charging in the wall outlet with USB C cable.I also had concerns that my US Mobile physical SIM may not work upon start-up.  I removed the chip from my old phone, inserted into new A36, plugged it in and powered up.  The phone immediately recognized the SIM and the related network, and a test call proved that I need not worry anymore.  All good...at least it could make phone calls!  I did need to do some additional data configuration (setup the US Mobile APN) but that had nothing to do with the phone itself and I anticipated the likelihood of needing to perform this step, which insures apps and texting work when not on WiFi.Next issue involved transferring data from old phone to new (photos, apps, contacts, etc.).  My previous Samsung phones handled this stage well enough, and this transfer from Z Flip 3 to A36 also went seamlessly!  I transferred via WiFi (as opposed to using included data cable) and each phone's Android OS operated perfectly...no issues whatsoever, and I expected that some apps' configurations may be lost due to user/pw and thus I would encounter a need to iron out some wrinkles.  But ultimately all pics/videos, contacts, etc. transferred with no significant issues.  I did have to perform my own manual WhatsApp chat backup from old and restore on new phone, but that had nothing to do with the phone itself and everything to do with WhatsApp procedures.I completed all setup in reasonable amount of time, including the biometric fingerprint reader capability that one can use to unlock the phone, as well as facial-rec.  One key difference between fingerprint reader on Z Flip 3 as compared to A36 involved the placement of the reader.  On ZF3 one finds the sensor on side of phone incorporated into a button like feature under the volume keys; on A36, Samsung relocated it on the glass screen, at the bottom, in the middle like where one would find the "home" button on the screen.  I really like this change since I now find it very easy to unlock the phone by simply pressing my finger into the sensor area of the screen.  It's a subtle change, but I like it.Large 6.7" display has great clarity.  A36's processor provides great speed out of the box and after 3 weeks of using the phone I've not experienced any related issues.  At one point the phone flashed a message that occasional restarts will help reset things, and it offered to allow me to configure automatic restarts when phone not in use, which I declined/skipped.  Other than a restart or two after OS software update, I've probably restarted just a couple times with one of those occasions involving a restart after I shut the phone down while flying.  In other words, no noticeable speed issues.The phone has thus far exhibited great battery life and really holds its charge when not in use, or in standby mode.  Watching videos will obviously deplete the battery at a faster rate but it all depends on amount of time one watches or otherwise keeps screen illuminated.  I do tend to keep my phone charging when not in use but when I have not charged it during the day, I don't think the level has gone below 60%-70% and that included frequent use of phone calls, videos, streaming music on Sirius XM app, etc.Phone has ideal weight and I do not find it an issue.  It has not overheated or demonstrated any such phenomena.  I completed outfitting my phone with a "Deerlamn" protective case, also purchased here on Amazon, and with which I'm also quite happy.All things considered, I found a great deal on this phone from "Cell Universal" and received good value for money paid, along with an excellent purchase/delivery experience.  Reader should note that I've written about my experience only and I make no claims that another buyer will necessarily have same experience, though I hope he or she will!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I ordered it on Sept 20th at $339 plus shipping of ~$34 and Morocco VAT of ~$80, so totally I paid $449.Delivery was very good. I saw it was shipped on the 25th. On the 30th, I received an SMS from DHL saying they planned delivery on Oct. 3rd, but on the same day I got an email asking for copy of national ID and content description for clearing customs. I am not a Morocco residents nor citizen, so I sent my foreign passport instead. On the 3rd, Amazon tracking info said clearing custom was delayed as additional documents were needed. So I called DHL, and the rep said it would be delivered on the 4th instead. On the 4th, I saw a newly posted message about delay on Amazon tracking. I called DHL various times but couldn't get to anyone. I then sent an inquiry by email and get a response shortly saying it was being taking care of. Then late afternoon, I got the package.Upon arriving, the seal of the packing had an opening large enough to put in a hand but not for getting the phone out, so I didn't complain.Unpacked, the inner packing of the phone was in excellent condition, very much like the original packing but had no Samsung marking, rather, it had a marking of "amazonrenewed". There was a film covering the screen, like on a new phone. The phone appeared in excellent condition, only had a small scratch at the back when I looked in detail, and a hair of scratch on the screen that is only visible under bright light and in a particular angle. I tried but couldn't turn on the phone - there was no response. The box also included a USB-C cable and a cheap non-Samsung charger made in China. I used my own Samsung Charger to charge the phone. After plugged in, it showed the battery was at 0. So I let it charge to full.After started, it turned out fully unlocked. My Morocco sim card works with 4G. The phone's software looked already reset, but I reset it myself anyhow. Then updated to the latest system with Android 12, and loaded many apps I need. During about the first week, the battery appeared quite poor. With medium usage it lasted about a day. I tried all necessary settings to conserve battery, but it didn't seem to help much. These couple days, it becomes much better, lasting about 45 hours. I read it was likely due to some AI processes either from Android 12 or Samsung doing the learning work at first.  But it's pretty bad the phone doesn't show any info.I would say I am very happy with the phone. And this is after having a terrible experience in the past with Samsung.The last Samsung phone I had was S7 Edge bought in Thailand (I am a traveler), new at a Samsung store for perhaps ~$800. I actually wanted the normal S7 (without the "edge"), but it was out of stock then. I never liked the "edge", it was a silly design in my mind. The phone worked well initially, but in the coming couple of years I had a terrible experience. About 5 months later when I was in Vietnam, the screen started to show shaded bands across. As I was wondering how or if I should return to Thailand to get the phone serviced, the bands disappeared after a month. Then about another 7 months later when I was in Azerbaijan, the phone couldn't start after I did a system update. So I couldn't use the phone for a couple weeks until I reached Tbilisi in Georgia  when I had someone flashed it.  About a year later, it died on me again when I was in Morocco. I had someone re-flashed it, but it was not successful.  About 1 month later I reached the city of Fes where there is a Samsung service center.  After checking, they said there was something wrong with the motherboard. Very shocking!  I've never had such problem in my life with all the phones and computers, cheap or dear, and this was a flagship!  So eventually, I sold it to a local repair shop for $200, for which they said they only needed the screen. That was end of 2017.So I never bought a Samsung again, and would definitely not buy one at the full price. I admit the S series is not worthless.  At least, I like the camera.  But I never had a chance to buy one at a largely reduced price (I won't buy from just any second-hand sellers).So now, the Amazon reviewed phone with some warranty got me interested. Yes, I have some risk, but to me with the past experience, the risk is not much higher than getting a new phone from Samsung, plus, I am putting in a much lower bet now.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A Premium Experience That Comes at a Premium Price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Samsung Galaxy S21 5G stands proud as one of the flagship offerings of the samsung, delivering cutting-edge technology and a sleek design that is sure to turn heads. However, with a price tag that might make even the most devoted tech enthusiasts do a double-take, this smartphone raises the age-old question: is it worth the investment? Here’s my take on this splendid yet pricey marvel.Design and Display: A Visual FeastFrom the moment you lay eyes on the Galaxy S21, it’s evident that Samsung has crafted a device meant for the high-end market. The sleek contours and premium materials give it an unmistakable aura of luxury. The 6.2-inch Dynamic AMOLED display is nothing short of breathtaking, offering vibrant colors, deep blacks, and impressive brightness levels. Whether you are streaming your favorite series or scrolling through social media, every experience is elevated by this stunning showcase of visual brilliance.Performance: Power UnleashedUnderneath the hood, the Galaxy S21 5G is powered by the latest Exynos or Snapdragon chipset (depending on your region), ensuring lightning-fast performance for multitasking and gaming alike. The device handles everything with remarkable ease, and the inclusion of 5G capabilities means you can harness incredibly fast download and upload speeds. With options for up to 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM, you won't find yourself wanting for space or speed.Camera: Capture Life’s MomentsSamsung’s camera system is one of the standout features of the S21. The triple-lens setup, including a 12MP ultra-wide, a 12MP wide, and a 64MP telephoto lens, allows users to capture stunning images in various conditions. The Night Mode is particularly impressive, ensuring that low-light photos are as crisp as those taken in bright daylight. The addition of advanced video features, including 8K recording, cements the Galaxy S21’s status as a powerhouse for mobile photography enthusiasts.Battery Life: Mixed ResultsWhile the battery life is generally sufficient to get through a full day with moderate use, heavy users may find themselves reaching for a charger by late afternoon. The 4000mAh battery powers some serious capabilities, but if you plan on extensively utilizing 5G and the phone's camera, be prepared for a potential drop in endurance. Fast charging and wireless charging options are a plus, but the slightly underwhelming battery performance keeps the S21 from achieving a perfect score.Value for Money:Herein lies the crux of the matter—while the Samsung Galaxy S21 5G dazzles with features, performance, and design, it comes at a steep price. For many, this puts it out of reach, especially considering the current market of other high-quality smartphones that offer comparable features at a lower cost. The premium branding does lend a certain prestige, but that may not be enough to sway budget-conscious consumers.Final Thoughts: A Worthy Investment for SomeIn conclusion, the Samsung Galaxy S21 5G is undeniably a fantastic smartphone that checks nearly all the boxes for performance, photography, and design. It’s perfect for tech enthusiasts who want the best of the best and are willing to pay for it. However, for those looking for value without compromise, exploring other options within the same price range might be a wise choice. With that said, I award the Galaxy S21 a solid 4 stars—it's good, but the expense is certainly something to consider.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I broke my old phone and started shopping around for a used S21 on Marketplace/Kijiji for a replacement. Many phones had defects (scratches, dents) and others were not competitively priced. I was surprised to find Amazon refurbished phones selling at the same price as what was available on these websites (inclusive of sales taxes where I live), while also eliminating most risks associated with buying a used phone by providing a 90-day warranty and a 30-day return option. With the Amazon seller, there's also no risk of the device being blacklisted.I received the phone a couple of days ago and I was very pleased when I first opened up the box. The phone was rated as "excellent" by the seller and it was indeed nearly perfect. You would only notice that it is used if you looked very closely under a bright light and observed micro scratches in a couple of places on the aluminium frame. Looking at it from beyond 10CM away, it's nearly impossible to see any signs that it's a used phone.I ran full diagnostics by dialing *#0*# AND I also used the Samsung Members app diagnostics test. I also checked the battery capacity. Everything appears to be stellar, including the battery life. The phone that I received also came with an original Samsung fast charger which was a pleasant surprise as well, as they advertise that it may come with a third-party unit in the ad.I was originally concerned given some of the reviews, but it's been a great experience for me. Give it a shot, with the return policy, there's really no risk (especially compared to buying a used phone from a random individual...).

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I wish I got the prime day deal but still love the phone.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I upgraded to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold7 512GB after waiting for my Asurion replacement gift card from my previous phone, the OnePlus Open, so unfortunately I missed the Prime Day pricing. Even at the regular price, I don't regret the purchase because this phone has exceeded my expectations. The displays are stunning, the performance is incredibly fast, and multitasking on the larger inner screen is a game changer for both work and entertainment. Samsung has clearly refined the folding experience, and the hinge feels solid and premium. The battery easily gets me through a full day, and the cameras produce excellent photos in just about every situation I've encountered. The Galaxy AI features have also been more useful than I expected, making everyday tasks quicker and more convenient. Coming from the OnePlus Open, I was already familiar with foldable phones, but the Fold7 feels more polished overall. The only feature I truly miss from my OnePlus Open is the built-in IR blaster, which let me use the phone as a remote control for TVs and other electronics. Aside from losing that convenience, the Fold7 has been an upgrade in nearly every category that matters to me. If you're considering making the switch to the Galaxy Z Fold7, I highly recommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent Phone, All the Haters Lied to Us
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve used Samsung’s Ultra and Note series for years, so I’m very familiar with wide, boxy phones and large displays. That’s why, when I first got the Z Fold 7, the cover screen initially felt narrow compared to what I was used to. In height it’s almost the same, but the width seemed smaller. However, this feeling only lasted a few days—once I adjusted, I realized the cover display is more than enough for everyday use. In fact, it’s very similar in size to the S25 Plus, and you can comfortably run any app on it.The magic happens when you unfold it. The internal display is huge, immersive, and makes you forget about missing the wider Ultra screen. You can run two apps side by side, or one above the other, almost like having two phones in one. For example, you can keep your email open on one side while chatting or receiving information on the other—copying, pasting, and multitasking without constantly switching apps. You can also watch a video on one half while replying to emails, chatting on WhatsApp, or doing other tasks on the other half. It’s an unmatched experience that no regular phone can offer.Multitasking and AppsMultitasking on the Fold is incredible. Editing photos, playing games, or browsing is simply more fun on such a large display. Most apps are optimized because Samsung’s software is excellent, and social apps like Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook look fantastic. If you ever prefer a narrower aspect ratio, you can quickly switch any app to “slim mode” through the multitasking options.Addressing the Haters’ ComplaintsUnder-display camera: You can enable a black bar in apps to hide the camera area, so it never gets in the way.S Pen: While there’s no built-in S Pen slot, you can use a capacitive S Pen. By enabling “increased touch sensitivity” (especially if you use a tempered glass screen protector), it works very well for everyday use.Battery life: After weeks of use, I can confirm the battery lasts all day. With adaptive power saving and dark mode, I’ve managed up to 10 hours of screen time on the cover screen, and 7–8 hours with mixed cover and main screen use. Heavy gaming or demanding apps bring it down to 5–6 hours, which is still solid. To preserve long-term battery health, I recommend enabling battery protection (charging to 90–95%) and avoiding letting it drop below 30%.CamerasFor 99% of users, the cameras are more than enough. The biggest advantage is using the high-quality rear cameras for selfies or streaming, which no standard phone—including the Ultra series—can match. Plus, when taking photos of others, they can preview themselves on the cover screen. Photos, selfies, and videos are sharp and vibrant. While professionals may prefer the S25 Ultra for advanced photography, the Fold’s versatility makes it an excellent choice for almost everyone.Final ThoughtsThe Z Fold 7 is an outstanding phone. Even if you’re coming from an Ultra, it only takes a few days to adjust before you realize you don’t miss the wider display. In fact, Ultras feel bulky and brick-like compared to the Fold, which is slimmer, more comfortable to hold, and far more versatile. The cover screen is fully usable for everyday apps, and when you want something larger, unfolding gives you a massive display that no traditional phone can match.I don’t regret switching at all—this is easily one of the best devices I’ve ever used, and I highly recommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A review for MOST users. ( I think)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First let me tell you how I use the z fold 7. And I will compare it to the z fold 4 for those who might want to try a z fold but don't want to spend a lot of money.First I use my z fold to watch videos while I am working out on the treadmill or elliptical, or if I'm waiting at a doctor's office or on in the bathroom.  I respond to emails and texts but I don't use it as a work center.  I play quick games or watch tik tok or other simple apps. I watch videos in bed while my wife is watching home improvement shows on tv..  If you do more or want more this review might not help you.  I dont care if a certain z fold opens an app .33 seconds quicker than another.  I am always by an outlet so I don't care if a certain z fold stays charged MUCH longer than another.  I love the bigger screen that the fold series offer.  Now.  I jumped into the z fold world at z fold 4.  Here are some real problems with the z fold 4 TODAY.  FIRST you are going to get a used zfold.  Battery life will be an issue because it's older.  BUT IF all you want is what I use it for it's a great phone. Yes it's thicker than a zfold 7 yes the screen is smaller BUT it's much less expensive and will give you the same results as a z7 at a much cheaper price.  SO YOURE ASKING WHY DID I BUY A Z7 THEN.  GOOD QUESTION.  I had 2 z4s and what really bothered me is that the hinges will at some point fail and the phone won't open all the way.  A zfold should open 180 degrees a straight line.  I owned 2 z4s and after a while both hinges stopped opening all the way up. More like 175+degrees. My research showed that this was a problem with the z fold 4 5 and 6.  Supposedly they fixed it with the z7 but I still see on line that some ppl are having that problem. I bought this phone refurbished at a MUCH CHEAPER PRICE and so far it's great.  But I have not owned it a full month.  I WILL DO AN UPDATE ON MY REVIEW IF OR WHEN THE HINGE ON THIS PHONE IS A PROBLEM.Right now if you're new to the zfold world  and you are going to use it like I DO I recommend the z4.  Yes it's thicker, the battery won't last all day if you stay on YouTube or tik tok but for the price I think the z4 is great entry point.  I am NEVER GOING BACK TO A NONFOLD PHONE and I'm going to wait till the trifold 3 falls in price to under 2k.  So the z7 was the next best option.Now why I love the z7.  Yes mine is used.  Bigger screen, more bells and whistles, thinner and lighter and hopefully no hinge issues. After 2 z fold 4s I wasn't going to buy a 3rd.  My first zfold4 the hinge was a problem but I got my second because the battery stopped working on the first one.  It would only stay on if it was plugged in.  No one would replace the battery for me so I bought the 2nd zfold4.  My 2nd zfold had hinge issues and the apps started popping up that I couldn't get rid of and the touch screen got glitch. As far as battery life I  Can't say better battery life on the z7  because it's newer. Not a fare comparison But I'm happy with it for now.  If you have had a chance to handle a z series and like it and want to committed definitely the z7.  If you're on the fence and don't or can't drop this kind of money the z4 is a great buy.
