productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Awesome Phone But Missing A Few Features I Wish It Had
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Love the phone especially because it is a flip phone. Great screen size, look and feel.The reason I wanted a flip phone is because I constantly break/crack the screen on the standard phones. It does not matter if I buy the most expensive bulletproof phone case. Those cases only protect the phone/screen if the phone falls on an edge or back side. If the phone lands on an object anywhere on the screen, they automatically crack the screen. Not with a flip phone. Once closed, the screen is protected and if you buy a case for it like I did, now it's truly bulletproof. I've accidentally dropped my phone so many times and no damage to the screen at all. My phone case also protects the small outside screen.I actually like this version with the small screen in the front. Makes it harder to damage it. The larger the screen, the bigger the chances of damaging it like the standard phones.When flipped closed, takes up way less space in my pants pockets compared to a non flip phone. No chance of it slipping out my pocket. The phone case I added does make it bulkier but if you're not using one or a really thin skin type cover, pretty thin sleek phone.The only negatives I really have are:It does not have an external SD card slot for memory. Whatever memory the phone comes with, that's it. This also makes it harder to track, save, and transfer files like pics and videos.It does have wireless charging (I wouldn't have bought it if it didn't) however, it is slow. I believe the wireless charging is rated at 5W max. Wired charging is fast though (30W max). I just prefer wireless charging because all charging ports (on all phones) do wear out over time and eventually fail preventing from charging the phone.The crease in the middle of the screen starts becoming noticeable on the screen after so much use, abuse, and flips. This doesn't bother me and I don't really notice it when watching videos but others are super sensitive to this and want perfect screen clarity always, so keep that in mind. This tradeoff for having a flip phone is worth it to me. This flip phone screen technology is still new so I expect the screens to only get better in the future.Overall, love my phone and don't regret this purchase.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Why do phones have to be so HUGE?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As far as this being as-advertised, it is.  As far as being renewed, it appears to be brand new.  It does have the AT&T OS and bloatware installed.  I popped in my SIM card, and it immediately started working with my PureTalk account.  The phone works great with no issues.  Battery life is, to my mind, a weak point.  It lasts me all day, but won't go two, and I am not a heavy user or game-player.  I don't watch a lot of video.  As for the phone design, I am not a big fan.  When open, it is very long and thin, which makes it very difficult to hang onto.  When folded, it is pretty chunky.  I added a thin case to make it easier to grip, and with the case, it is 13/16" thick when folded - this pushes the limits of "pocket-sized", which is the only reason to purchase a Razr in the first place.  The small outside screen on the 2023 model is a cool feature, but isn't very touch-responsive.  I often have trouble getting it to answer a call or turn off an alarm.  This is unfortunate, because the alternative is to un-fold the phone to get to the main screen, and there is a very finite number of unfolds before the screen will crack.  I have only taken a few photos, but the quality and lighting seems to be pretty decent, but not quite as good as my wife's Pixel4.  So, bottom line, I bought this phone for the single reason that it folds up "small".  I want it to fit easily in my pocket.  This is marginal on that goal, but it is better than any other phone non-folding on the US market.  Why on earth do phones have to ALL be so large?  Please, Samsung or somebody, offer us at least ONE decent 5" Android phone for the US market!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great new-to-me iPhone for an affordable price for basic user!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Although my iPhone 6S Plus still works just as well as when I first bought it, it cannot connect to Airtag 2nd generation in the Find My app, so I wanted to get an updated iPhone to use modern Airtags (2nd gen), the Find My app, and the Apple Podcasts app, which has a fantasic auto-generated transcripts feature.I originally got a Renewed/Refurbished iPhone 12, but the battery life was disappointing when compared to iPhone 6S Plus. I paid a few bucks more and upgraded to the iPhone 13 Renewed Premium. It was really worth it!A renewed premium/refurbished iPhone 13 has everything you need for a modern smartphone in 2026:1. One-year warranty/return period with Amazon. It came with a checklist and a list of all the refurbished/replacements done to the device in the Service History in the About screen on the iPhone. I got 100% battery life since the battery and logic board were replaced.2. It can run iOS 26, which has a lot of cool, quality-of-life features compared to my iPhone 6S Plus: MagSafe wireless charging, StandBy mode to turn it into a desk calendar/clock screen when horizontal and charging with MagSafe, Category grouping in Mail, Face ID unlock is quick and easy to set up and is blazing fast unlocking the iPhone.3. The 6.1-inch screen and power button did have hairline scratches, but they disappear with a screen protector and a case, so I don't mind. The display still looks great for 60 Hz! I do not play games on my smartphones, so I don't care about it.The only negatives:1. iPhone 13 is heavier and thicker than the iPhone 12.2. I don't think the camera focus of either back lens is as sharp as the iPhone 6S Plus. It takes a long time to focus, especially for close-up shots, and boke is not reliable.I am hoping to keep it for another 5 years, as I trust the quality of Apple and its refurbishment partners.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently ordered an iPhone 13 for my son to use for school. I was a little hesitant about ordering a refurbished phone from Amazon, but the price was too good to pass up. It arrived quickly as promised, and so far, I’m mostly pleased with the purchase.However, buyers should be aware that these phones may not truly be in “excellent” condition. They appear to be rebuilt or refurbished using a combination of used and newer replacement parts. Upon inspecting the phone, I noticed visible blemishes on the back glass as well as several chips along the casing.The phone itself seems to work well so far, and considering the price, I’m still satisfied overall. However, describing the cosmetic condition as “excellent” feels misleading. I would consider the phone I received to be closer to “good” condition.If cosmetic appearance is important to you, I’d keep that in mind before purchasing.

Not a scratch that I could see you on the screen anywhere, I checked the left side, the right side, even the back as you can see from the attached photos that I am attaching.It was brand new, or look to be brand new had no problems, I own an iPhone 12 plus Max and I had a Samsung note 9 already, I had them take the note 9 off and add the 16+ Max .I am happy, across the board with everything. It came very well packaged in a box as you can see, I put photo of the box it came in, if you’re on the fence about this don’t be. I’m telling you I could not be happier. I’ll come back here in a couple weeks and update everyone on how it’s working, I can tell you this it is up-to-date technology now is quite different, unlike when I did my iPhone 12 max plus,  I had to get on the phone with my provider and it took about maybe 45-minutes to do everything .when I opened the box and  looked at it. I set it down not thinking next to my iPhone 12 plus, I had no ideal anything would happen till I heard it kind of vibration , when I picked up the phone to look at it it was everything had transferred cause they were only sitting on the table while I went and did something else in the house so, when I come back, I could see the picture of my dog on the front of the new phone and I was like wow what happened if I didn’t know better I would’ve been like it’s gonna take me 45 minutes to an hour and that’s really why it took me three days to open it up, I just did not have time to deal with carrier and Technician for support, and all that drama with cloud and transferring data to one phone from the other.I just did not have the time to get on the phone with the (carrier) and go through all the Rigamarole so to speak .Let me tell you when I saw the dog picture on the new phone. I picked it up and I dialed my husband‘s number and it worked already which was amazing. I still called the carrier and told them and they were like what’s happening is it’s ringing from your iPhone 12+ it automatically because it’s two iPhones everything transfer over and from the note 9 so I didn’t have to do anything, but took me about maybe 10 minutes and that’s cause their system was slow to have them take the phone number off the note 9 and move it to the new iPhone 16+ and then they call me and checked everything and everything was operating fine.I am so happy again if you are on the fence, take a chance you know how great Amazon prime is. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok, I’m a galaxy gal with a S25 Ultra phone.  People tell me try Apple’s iPhone, and I put it off for more than 12 years.  However, I do own 2 Apple Mac Minis, and I like the computers.  Well, I looked up iPhones on Amazon and other sites and came across this iPhone 16 Max Pro with 8 gig ram and 1 terabyte storage for just a little over 900 dollars.  A lot of money for an iPhone that’s a year old I thought.So I took the risk and made the purchase.When I got the package in the mail I hesitated even opening the box and contemplated just returning it back without giving it a chance.  Well, after opening the box and charging it up, I transferred my data over to the iPhone 16 Pro Max and it worked well and fairly easy too.I still wasn’t too impressed with the iPhone just yet, but I gave it a chance.As I began using it and saw the battery life was at 98 % I thought, WOW, nice iPhone with a pretty decent battery too.  I also noticed it still has an Apple warranty until March of 2026.The phone is beautiful and works great thus far, but my niece said I should get the iPhone 17 Pro Max.  So I looked it up and didn’t see why I should go into a 2k debt for an iPhone 17 pro max with a 1 terabyte storage drive.  After all, my iPhone 16 Pro Max still gets another 6 years of updates on the iOS software.I have to say I still have time to return this iPhone, but, right now, this is a well made and solid purchase and I feel very comfortable with it after 2 weeks of use.  I still have my android Galaxy S25 Ultra, and I’m gonna keep it too, but the seller of this iPhone certainly does ship out beautiful and quality iPhones to the buyers.  No scratches or dings and a great battery life too.  The item arrived with great packaging and I am impressed with this seller.Now my niece with the iPhone 17 pro max with 256 gig of storage loves her phone, she’s had it for about a month now, and yes,she paid more than me and I have a 1 terabyte storage drive on mine, and her first complaint about the iPhone 17 is, the aluminum casing gets scratched up easily forcing her to get a cover so she doesn’t have to look at the scratched up case on her new iPhone.The IPhone 16 Pro Max has a titanium frame that is solid, and I do have a case over it to protect it from drops or falls.Would I recommend this iPhone and seller on Amazon.  ABSOLUTELY YES!Alyssa

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I usually don’t put feedback in reviews section, but I think this is important one and so I thought its important to provide a feedback so that customers can get a trustworthy product from Amazon renewed premium category, that really gives the customer the price point of value with money.I ordered my iPhone 16 pro max couple of days back and got it yesterday. I was very excited as I was getting 512GB storage with an amazon backed brand to claim that renewed premium category is like a new. Now as I received my phone, it all looks very nice and I start begin the setup as well as checked everything from the physical perspective if nothing is damaged, I didn’t notice anything major till my son noticed that of the lens on the back side camera have a small chip cut that can easily be observed in day light as well as buy touching it with finger. Anyway I proceed with complete setup, and begin testing the phone, everything looks to be fine, batter at 95% which is good. But then I majorly stuck on side camera button, which was not functional. I did some research on YouTube and google if some setting or config needs to change, and I followed all the steps but nothing works and the conclusion that some sensor or side button is damaged and not functioning properly and this is big red flag if I am spending close to 1000$ on renewed premium product and expecting it to at least work 4 to 5 years. I also want to mention that, amazon send me the lighting cable, instead of usb C cable.Anyway next morning I called customer care to report my feedback and explain all the details, my concern was not that I can’t return it or can’t get the refund. But my biggest concern was of Trust in the branding for renewed premium category of product. Because if Vendor is claiming what they are selling then it supposed to be that way. Because if I have to buy a renewed premium category product I may think twice or more before taking that decision, and I think used premium category is a big market, so seller should focus on quality and maintaining the brand and not to sell the defective product to customer and create so much frustration.But the good thing is at least Renewed premium category is claiming to return and refund upto 365 days that customer support specialist also told me to not worry and return and try order another one, because its rare that such kind of issue come, but anyway I see 11% of customers report bad experience so this matters.Anyway I am retuning this phone today with less than 14 hours of receiving, I am not sure if I will order again, because of all such a big hassle in the whole experience of waiting the product to arrive, setup everything, and test out and its all about experience how much you want to invest in that effort.I am updating my review on May 22 regarding my experience with customer service while following up on my refund. It has now been two days since my return.On May 20, I spoke with an Amazon specialist about a defective product and requested a replacement. I was advised that the best option would be to initiate a return and return at Whole Foods and that I would receive a refund within a week, after which I could place a new order.However, today, when I contacted customer support to check the status of my refund, I had a very disappointing experience. The representative was rude, yelled her voice, and informed me that the refund would take up to 30 days.  So be prepare, if you get a defective product then you stuck with your money and wont be able to buy another unless you get your money back. This is one of the worst experience i had as i cant use the product that i paid for, and the money also stuck for a month, that i cant use to buy another phoneShe also stated that the previous information I received about a 7-day refund was incorrect. She was not willing to listen to my concerns and ended the call abruptly.I have never encountered such poor customer service from Amazon before. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max, US Version, 1TB, Black Titanium - Unlocked
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Premium Powerhouse That Nearly Hits Perfection.After using the Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max (US Version, 1TB, Black Titanium – Unlocked Renewed Premium) for several weeks as my daily driver, I’m ready to share what stands out and where it falls slightly short. This renewed premium model delivers much of the flagship experience at a better price point than new, but there are a few compromises worth noting.Design and Build Quality Apple’s Black Titanium finish feels exquisite and substantially more durable than glossy glass. The weight and heft feel reassuring without being cumbersome for everyday use. The Renewed Premium condition I received was impressive with no noticeable scratches or blemishes, and the device felt indistinguishable from new out of the box. The large display and premium materials maintain Apple’s reputation for class-leading industrial design.Display The Super Retina XDR display on the 16 Pro Max remains one of the best on the market. Colors are vivid, contrast is deep, and brightness is excellent even outdoors. Streaming videos and gaming on this 6.7-inch panel was immersive, and ProMotion made scrolling buttery smooth. For media consumption and productivity, it’s a standout feature that justifies the device’s flagship status.Performance With Apple’s latest silicon under the hood and a massive 1TB storage configuration, this iPhone handles everything I threw at it with ease. Multitasking, editing 4K video on the go, and playing demanding games were all fluid and responsive. The extra storage is a real benefit for power users who shoot lots of video or maintain large app libraries. Performance hasn’t shown any signs of slowing during my time with it.Camera System The triple-lens camera array continues to impress. Daylight shots were sharp, detailed, and true to life. Night mode and computational photography made low-light shots usable and often surprising. Video recording is excellent with stabilization and color accuracy that rivals dedicated cameras. That said, incremental improvements over last year’s model mean that if you already own a 15 Pro Max, the leap might feel modest rather than revolutionary.Battery Life Battery life has been strong, comfortably lasting a full day of heavy use, including navigation, streaming, and photography. Charging speeds are adequate but not industry-leading — still typical of Apple’s measured approach. Wireless charging and MagSafe accessories worked reliably throughout my usage.Software Experience iOS continues to be smooth, intuitive, and well optimized for the hardware. The unlocked status made switching carriers seamless, and everything from setup to daily interaction felt polished. Apple’s long-term software support remains one of the most compelling reasons to choose an iPhone.Renewed Model Considerations As a Renewed Premium unit, this phone represents excellent value compared to buying new. Condition was superb and performance indistinguishable from brand-new units. However, buyers should always be mindful of warranty terms and return policies when purchasing renewed electronics, since coverage can vary by seller.Final Thoughts The iPhone 16 Pro Max in this renewed premium configuration hits the majority of marks you’d want: stunning display, strong performance, long battery life, and a best-in-class camera system. It falls just short of perfection due to incremental updates over previous models and the usual premium price, but when purchased as a Renewed Premium unit, it delivers flagship power and storage at a more accessible price point. I confidently give it four stars.

*Disclaimer – Audio quality is dependent on your service provider’s network quality 
A light on the top of the handset flashes when the phone rings, signaling an incoming call. With the ringers muted, this visual indicator can let you know the calls in silence. Also helpful for those who are hearing impaired. 
Audio Assist button instantly increases incoming call's volume and enhances sound frequencies to make speech easier to understand. It is easy to use, just one press on the Audio Assist button on handset. Press again to turn off. 
2" backlit display on handset with high contrast text makes it easy to read incoming caller ID or call history records. Plus, the lighted handset keypad allows for easy dialing in low light conditions. 
With the full-duplex speakerphone on the handset, this phone set not only lets you speak hands-free but also allows both ends to speak and be heard at the same time. Enjoy conversations that are more true to life. 
Stay informed even when you are away from home. All calls are routed to the built-in digital answering machine when necessary, recording key messages for you. 
Screening calls has never been easier. The handset announces the name of the caller, so you don't have to scramble for the handset to see who's calling. 
Experience the best in long-range coverage and clarity, provided by a unique antenna design and advances in noise-filtering technology. 
What's a Smart Call Blocker? 
A simple one-time setup to filter unwanted calls while letting trusted ones through. 
Quick Setup to let the system working for you 
Set Directory - for your family so their calls will go through without the screening. 1. Press MENU on handset. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Directory, then Select. 3. Press Select again to choose Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then Select. 
Set Allow list - so their calls do not get through the screening. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow list, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter telephone number, then Select. 5. Enter name, then Select. 
Set Block List - to prevent their calls from ringing through. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Block list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then press Select. 
Set Star name list for your trusted organizations - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Star name list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the name (up to 15 characters), then press Select. 
Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

modules.title: What's a Smart Call Blocker?
modules.text:
A simple one-time setup to filter unwanted calls while letting trusted ones through. 
Quick Setup to let the system working for you 
Set Directory - for your family so their calls will go through without the screening. 1. Press MENU on handset. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Directory, then Select. 3. Press Select again to choose Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then Select. 
Set Allow list - so their calls do not get through the screening. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow list, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Add new entry, then Select. 4. Enter telephone number, then Select. 5. Enter name, then Select. 
Set Block List - to prevent their calls from ringing through. 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Block list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the telephone number, then press Select. 
Set Star name list for your trusted organizations - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Star name list, Select. 3. Press Up/Down to Add new entry, Select. 4. Enter the name (up to 15 characters), then press Select. 
Pick one of our Smart Call Block options which suits your preferences: 
Screen and block robocalls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3 Press Up/Down arrow key to Screen robot, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to press the pound key. 
Screen all unknown calls - 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down key to Screen Unknown, then Select. 
The callers will be asked to record their names and press the pound key. After your caller completes the request, the phone rings and announces the caller's name. You then can choose to block or answer the call, or forward the call to the answering system. 
Block calls on the block list only - (This is also the Default settings of the system.) 1. Press CALL BLOCK. 2. Press Up/Down arrow key to Set profile, then Select. 3. Press Up/Down arrow key to Allow unknown, then Select. 
For complete operation instructions, the user's manual can be found from the Product Support section of our company website.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: With caller ID, call blocking works great
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the AT&T BL102-4 cordless phone set from the Amazon Warehouse (like-new used in original packaging)  when our family switched from a traditional landline setup to a VOIP landline with our local cable provider.  We previously had been using a cordless system from another brand with our phone company's service and the call quality was never good - often lots of crackle on the line, making callers hard to hear.  I wasn't sure if it was the phones, the service, or the cords, so I replaced all of them and started anew.The build quality of this AT&T phone system was a little less substantial than I expected, but the phones do their job and call quality is good.  The handsets and the base feel kind of cheap, but this is an under-one hundred dollar phone system so I guess that's to be expected.  It works well though, and the features are good.The only feature I miss is Bluetooth.  If this system had it  I could pair it with my cell phone, but other than that, it's not missing anything.----------------------------------➡️  SETUP & USE:I put the batteries in the phones and charged them as I went to the included user manual to try and figure out how to set it up.  The manual is a bit overwhelming, but if you read it carefully and go step by step, you can figure it out.Some features on the phone duplicate those offered by my cable company, so I did need to figure out which ones to set up and which ones to leave off on the phone.  For example, my cable provider offers voicemail, and thus using the answering machine feature of this phone system isn't something that I do.Once I set up things like the number of rings before the calls were answered, I started adding numbers into my phone's contacts.  Doing this let these callers come right through, and helped with call blocking.  I set it up so that callers I didn't recognize would have to press the pound button on their phones to get through.  This eliminates robocalls, but real-live telemarketers can still get through.---------------------------------------➡️ CALL BLOCKING FEATURE:Call blocking only works if your phone service provider has caller-ID enabled for your account.It works like this...When a call comes through that you have not put on your call block list already, or that your provider has not filtered, you get an audio announcement of the number and associated caller name.  You can disable the audio announcement if desired.You can then decide if you want to answer or block the call.  If you wish to block it, you press the call block button on the handset which is in the lower right corner.  That stops the call from coming through and the ringing stops on the phone.Call blocking has been a life-changing feature for us.  The combination of our cable provider phone service and this phone has eliminated 98% of our telemarketing calls and all of the robocalls.  We no longer have to unplug our phones to get some sleep, and the calls we do get are nice and clear.------------------------------------------The top 3 reasons I purchased this phone system...1. I got a heck of a deal through the Amazon Warehouse during Prime Day (an additional 20% off the warehouse price), making it under seventy for me.2.  The call blocking feature to eliminate robocalls and telemarketers.3.  The ability to increase the volume easily on the handset, for my hard-of-hearing husband.-----------------------------------------------This phone system works with both traditional phone service providers and VOIP cable company phone services.  It comes with four handsets and has a built-in answering machine along with the call blocking feature that works with the caller ID provided by your phone service provider.The handsets are lightweight, have big numbers that are easy to see along with the LCD display.  The caller ID announce feature is a nice addition and most of the time it's easy to understand.🎯 I think this phone system is a good one for those who want to eliminate robocalls and telemarketing calls from their life.  I also think it's a good choice for those who are impaired visually or have hearing loss.===========================================

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this due to what seemed like pretty awesome and aggressive call Blocker features and the large screen.  I've always bought panasonic but this phone was far more "advanced".  I just set it up and I really dislike how complicated this is.  All phones I've had, for decades, had intuitive set up and I chalked my difficulty up to maybe just not being used to.this brand.  I spent 45 minutes scrolling , hitting buttons, not finding a simple "erase" or "space" anywhere to enter numbers then having the phone save stuff I have to go retype and erase.  I didn't use the manual, having zero problem, ever, setting up a phone, and if you lose the manual good luck setting this up or trying to do "a" thing.  I liked the smart call block  which instructs callers that you're screening calls and to say their name  then press pound to be rung thru.  The manual clearly states that this can block calls you want to have and so don't use it.  Which isn't helpful.  Doctors and others call from private cell phones now and many work from home and aren't using caller-ID branded company phones so its also impractical to block everyone but who is in your phone directory  (another option).  If you want to do this, you cant import or choose the numbers you've added to your directory- you have to retype all the names and numbers,  one by one, again, to your " allow list" .  Many i have in my directory still say "unavailable" above the number which isn't helpful if you have the caller ID speak who is calling so you can go pick it up or let it go to voice mail. A few options you can set up, like allowing everyone in your Directory through didn't work.  I also looked for extra batteries, just in case, and in putting the phone name, I find none listed.  I guess you have to look at the 300 batteries being sold to find the compatible ones but ATT ought to make this easier.  While the screen is large, my smaller one had thicker text and I find this readout spidery and not too easy to read.  Perhaps I'll get used to it but I find this overly complicated, the spoken set up instructions pretty much tell you to read the manual, and alas, it has shrill, annoying ringer tones.  The voice announcer is really weird, pronouncing things slowly and with strange inflection..  Wouldn't buy again and would return if I didn't need a phone this second.  Way too complicated, even.for the easy stuff.UPDATE: I have tried my best to adjust to this phone and persevere.  after months and re-re-reading everything and multiple resets and endless tweaking this phone is a nightmare.  if I leave it on " block everyone but people in my directory" then its fine.  but not practical.  i had it on "block unknown calls" which then started giving me spam numbers calling but without any ID to it.  my best friend continually rings thru as "unknown caller" tho she's in my allow list and directory,  yet the talking ID will announce her name.  many, many times I'll answer the phone and it goes to one, constant ring, like an alarm going off.  it won't answer and I can't turn this off! I have to yank the batteries out. the person calling gets dead air.  many times someone will call and hear me but I can't hear them.  I even called ATT who muddled thru the same instruction tome as I have. people in directory show up as "unknown caller" in spite of being allowed. Jerks calling can't be blocked because if you block number you have to enter a name, too, and you cant put in "unavailable " or "out of area" . block doesn't go by name but you cant just block a number, period.  many times phone will ring (when using the screener) and I'll pick.it up to be asked by the phone screen to "press any number and then pound" which is what the CALLER is supposed to get, not me.  if I do this im told by phone voice this is an invalid phone number so my call can't be completed. huh??? the actual caller will tell me the phone rang forever then went dead silent.  my caller ID will show my number called me and as "unknown"  I give up.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I LUV this phone!!! If your issue is blocking numerous annoying spam callers…
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I give it 5 stars!!  (I don’t know what the “Lock Feature” is, but just gave that feature 5 stars too).  I had a Panasonic cordless that was several years old and still worked perfectly, but it only allowed me to block 30 numbers at a time, which, with the increase in spam callers, caused me to have to constantly have to go into the block list and remove older numbers to make room for the more recent ones.  WELL… this one lets you block 1000 numbers!!!  (Hopefully that will be enough for a while).  Also, my Panasonic cordless would announce “you’ve got a call from…” and then state about the first 5 numbers, so I was still hearing it ring, tho I know from the area code not to pick it up.  With this AT&T cordless, if the spam callers hang up after my greeting starts playing, I never even hear it ring once nor announced.  And if the number is on my block list, it won’t ring thru either.  I check the phone’s caller list daily and if I see new un-blocked spam calls listed I can easily put them on the block list.  It is also much easier to block calls actively coming in or even afterwards than it was on my older Panasonic.  I only have to push a cpl of buttons to put a number on the block list with the AT&T phone, while with my Panasonic, I had to go to the Menu, scroll down to find block list, erase a number to make room for new number, go back to call list to see new spam number, edit it down to 10 digits (minus the “1”), then save it.  It was a LOT of steps. So this AT&T phone makes it much simpler in way fewer steps to block numbers.  I no longer hear spam caller rings / announcements start in the early morning hours because most of them hang up w/o leaving a message. If they do leave a message - which I have not experienced yet since installing new phone about 4 days ago - I would be able to put them on the block list the same as if they hadn’t.  I have observed that spammers roll thru various exchanges to try to get to you by changing 1 digit in the number they are calling from at a time.  I am very diligent in checking every day for those numbers and block them immediately.  This is why the ability to block 1000 numbers is the MOST important new feature of this phone to me.  One thing that is different, which is not as good as the Panasonic, is setting Quiet Hours… those hours between midnight and whatever time in the morning you do not want the phone to ring at all from anyone.  On the Panasonic, there is a setting to enter the specific hours once that you want to be Quiet and it observes those hours day in and day out; however, with the new AT&T phone, you have to set them each night.  It’s an easy setting, but still so easy to forget to do that before bed every night.  So that is the one deficiency of this phone, and I am surprised AT&T didn’t catch that in their development of it.  But so far, I have remembered to set it nightly.  Even if I forget, I still LUV this phone because it blocks spam callers so perfectly, and that is the main reason I bought it!!  So, if you have a problem with lots of spam callers and want to stop them in their tracks, this is the phone for you!!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: WARNING: Phone Has a Major, Unfixable Software Update Problem. DO NOT BUY.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this phone expecting a standard, working device. Initially, everything was fine. However, I have discovered a critical software flaw that prevents the phone from receiving any updates. This means the device is already significantly outdated and will become a security risk.​The core issue:​Stuck on Old Software: The phone is running One UI version 6.1 and Android version 14. While others are receiving the new One UI 8.0 update, my phone is completely locked out.​Outdated Security: The device claims it is "up to date," but the actual software information shows a Security patch level of November 1, 2024. This means the phone has not received a security patch in an entire year (as of late 2025) and is vulnerable.​Technical Confirmation of the Problem:​When attempting a manual software update, the system reports the following information, which confirms the update mechanism is broken:​Update information:One UI version: 6.1, Android version: 14Current version: S926USQU4AXK5 / S926UOYN4AXK5 / S926USQU4AXK5Security patch level: November 1, 2024​The retailer's response confirms this is a severe and unfixable flaw:​I contacted my carrier, Amazon, and the manufacturer (if applicable). Amazon's technical support provided a definitive, alarming response:​"FOTA is also not supported in this version. (210) The version of the device is NOT supported. (No delta for the version)"​This technical response indicates that the specific software build on this phone is not recognized by the standard update server and cannot receive the necessary "delta" (the small file needed to transition from the old version to the new one). This confirms the phone is permanently stuck on this outdated and potentially insecure version. strongly regret this purchase and cannot wait to replace this phone with a new one bought elsewhere. Please do not make the same mistake.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great phone, transfer from old phone was a bit tricky
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My son has Type 1 Diabetes and has needed a cell phone since he was diagnosed for tracking his glucose monitor and allowing us to track it. He has always used a Samsung, and he needs to have a fairly current model because the apps the monitoring companies use require certain specifications (like most current system updates). When his S20 wouldn't update anymore we upgraded to this and so far it has worked great. The only complaint I have is that the transfer from the old phone to new phone was not as smooth as other phone brands. I have transferred phone data for myself and my kids a LOT of times and every time, the apps and wallpaper and everything transfers, you don't even hardly know you have a new phone. This one only initially uploaded all the "spam" crappy apps from Samsung that you don't want or need, and with his Google account some of the Google stuff did transfer. However, I had to do a lot of toggling back and forth between his old and new phones to get the rest of his apps and data transferred and it was a pain and took way too much time! We also had to re-log in to many apps which I haven't had to do with other phone transfers so yeah. But the battery life on this is great, the camera is really nice, screen is a bit larger (not a ton) than the past models, and operating system is user friendly.

One huge plus is the natural anti-screen time benefit. The compact hardware cannot support long hours of complex heavy games, which helps limit screen addiction without me having to enforce strict rules every day. This updated version also runs noticeably smoother than the unit I owned for almost a year. Basic functions including calling, messaging, music playback and the camera work reliably. It charges easily with the included USB cable, and battery life works perfectly for kids’ light daily use. It is a basic compact device that works great as a kid’s first phone or simple backup phone, it’s not built for high-demand apps and heavy gaming, which is exactly a helpful feature to control children’s screen time. Wonderful value as a beginner kid phone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: S22 plus, it will never be a top rated Samsung Galaxy, get it if you can't afford an S23.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The phone I ordered was listed as excellent and came with some cosmetic damage around the frame, the front and rear glass was fine and after setting it up and charging it to 100 and running AccuBattery through a full cycle it came in as 85% of the design capacity which exceeds Amazon's criteria of 80%.The battery is almost as bad as my S9 battery for how quickly it discharges and that phone is very old, so I'll be running this phone on locationless power saving mode permanently and using maximum battery protection to keep it from charging over 80%. Honestly Samsung should never have released this line with such a bad battery.The screen is quite a bit larger than my S9 and it not being curved is amazing. Samsung should never have introduced curved screens but... well it happened and I am definitely happy that they went back, although I can't blame misspellings on the poor screen now.Sadly there is no headphone jack or microSD slot as us niche users who adored such technology seemingly don't matter and getting everyone spending money on microtransactions has been the focus for a while now anyway.Tested the camera and it's quite nice, the landscapes of Arrested Development will look like what they actually are, not to mention it's an improvement over the cursed images from the S9 camera I used to use as a "last known photo" generator.Why the resolution of the phone decreased I'll never know but perhaps it's a good thing as the battery can't hold up against a potato.As for using the phone, well I got it working for most things although Duolingo no longer believes I am speaking so there is going to be a bit of faffing about to do.Ideas: The phone functions, it's compatable with something I dunno, the phone does have a brightness slider (weird that was in the ideas list), and the phone weighs about as much as a phone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: S22+ Solid battery, Great performance, Great visuals. Little heavy though.S22+ Solid battery, Great performance, Great visuals. Little heavy though.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'll come back to this review every once in a while as I continue to use the phone.EDIT2: 7/9/2023 Okay the line is not going away after locking and waking the phone like it did before. You can see in the second picture, it's faint, but it's there (ignore the orange glow, that's from my old s7 that can't take pictures of other screens without struggling).The fact that it wouldn't go away makes me think it's getting worse. I had to restart it this time to make it disappear. Went ahead and started the refund process because it seems like it's getting worse. Unfortunate because this was labeled as an excellent condition phone too. I guess it's hit or miss what you get when you buy refurbished. I'm not a phone repairman, so I'm not going to be able to open it up and figure it out. I'm just gonna refund this and get a different phone to avoid the problem happening again.EDIT: Okay, it's been 4 days since the review. Woke this morning and unlocked my phone, typical. Was adjusting notification volume settings then all of a sudden BAM, bright PINK (not green this time) line right through the same spot as usually from top to bottom of the screen. Wanted to take a picture with my old phone but was afraid of leaving the error on the screen for too long (was busy using restroom) so I locked the phone and unlocked it again and the line went away. Man... I might return this thing because this is scaring me.So far the phone has been pretty great. One thing's for sure though, it's crazy the difference (s7 to s22+) 2 oz of weight (including cases) can feel while holding it. This thing feels like I'm holding a brick compared to my old phone lol.All of these things that I am giving it accolades for are, of course, from a biased perspective of somebody who has used the s7 since it's launch, so take it with a grain of salt if you are coming from something like an s20 or later.Great/Solid battery, Great performance, Great visuals. Little heavy though. Those are the main points.Since it is refurbished, the only actual visible damage you can see well is the small scratch at the bottom left corner of the screen (as seen in picture) that is on the glass for a length of about 2mm and then goes off to the side a bit. Not a problem though, it's quite out of the way. Saving around $350 just to have a scratch on the screen is quite the deal. I make my phones last, so this thing is going to be built like a tank by the time I'm done putting protective layers and cases on it.(This is the reason for the 4/5 and not 5/5) So far my only real scare with this phone (purchased as an excellent condition renewed s22+ with 256gb storage from Macalegin Electronics) is, since I've received it as of June 29th, it's now July 3rd, it's had this very thin vertical green line from the top of the screen to the bottom of the screen 3 times upon waking the phone. Seems to really only happen when I wake the phone. If I see it again I'll try to take a picture with my old phone and add it to the review.First time it happened I kinda had a mini freak-out, thinking that this is the end of having this phone and I gotta return it before it's too late and it gets worse.If it does get worse and more frequent, then I will get the refund because that's unacceptable as an excellent condition phone.Some people online say that it is because of a loose connection from the motherboard to the screen panel (I don't know the actual technical lingo), usually caused by the phone being dropped. Well, it's "brand new" to me, so it wasn't me who dropped it.Either way, the phone is great except for that scare. To be honest though, I do miss my more compact and sleek phone designs. I do kinda wish I had gotten the s22 instead, but I wanted to see what it's like having a bigger screen. Well, we'll see as the years go by.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Nice phone autistic 8 yr. Old using and maneuvers it quite well

First off, it took a month to arrive to me from the order date, so I was not impressed with that, HOWEVER, I will look past that and just review the phone. I will try to be detailed as I know I read hundreds of reviews before finally feeling secure with my purchase, so hopefully I can help someone out here.The box it arrived in was old and dirty so I was extremely nervous to open it, but once I did I was very impressed. The phone itself was in phenomenal, like new condition. I was very happy to see everything included in the box (sim key ejector, charging cable, plug in adapter) so that was great since some of the reviews I read said parts were not included or missing, ect.The phone needed to be charged right away, and as soon as I plugged in it, the included wall adapter started making a very high pitched buzzing sound, so I swapped it out with a different adapter I already had on hand (you can get them anywhere so not a big deal) and problem was instantly solved.I am completely unfamiliar with Samsung phones, so I was worried about set up, but once I was easily able to change the language from Spanish to English, it was pretty easy to do.I really liked how crisp and clear the graphics were and the phone has a great screen size for gaming. I will say that in my opinion the phone is pretty laggy in loading, but my 12 year old doesn’t really seem to mind and after pretty much living on it for the past two days, it’s safe to say he loves the phone.It took some doing to familiarize ourselves with it, and found it was not as user friendly as an iPhone, but once you figure out how to actually gets the apps on the Home Screen and change the clock, ect, you’re good to go.Pros: great screen size, clear graphics, amazing battery life, 12 year old approved.Cons: A little laggy, not the most user friendly until you get used to it, weird buzzing adaptor.Note: we have not tried installing a SIM card as of yet, so I can’t attest to that.So far this phone has been great, well worth the purchase price, and my son is extremely happy with it, so for that, I would absolutely recommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Listing says the Renewed Premium phone includes generic charger, but was not included
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I ordered this phone from Amazon to update to a later model, as I have been using an iPhone 12 Pro for several years now.  I received the phone quickly (it was sold by and shipped by Amazon), and it looks quite good.  There was a charging cable in the box, but no charger.  I went to customer service and asked for a call from a customer service agent since my problem was not covered in the automated responses I was offered.  I spent about 15 minutes on the phone since the agent (Mark) told me the phone is shipped with a charging cable but no charger.  I had to tell him multiple times that the listing clearly says that the phone comes with a generic (Mfi certified) charger and cable, but there was no charger in the box.  He said that he would have to wait two days to process a partial refund so that I could purchase a generic charge, since the phone was only delivered today(!).  So, I now have to wait for two days to see if Amazon will actually deliver to me what they promised on their website.  I will update this review when I hear back from Amazon in two days.One other thing that was strange - when I tried to turn the phone on, nothing happened.  I plugged it in using the supplied cable and a charger I had at home, and it started to charge.  I just find it odd that the phone was supposedly "Fully Tested" after being renewed, but the battery was completely dead when it arrived at my home two days after I ordered it.**UPDATE: I did receive a $25 credit to use to purchase a charger for this phone, so Amazon did step up and fix the problem.  Updated rating to 4 stars.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Lamicall Bike Phone Mount – Secure, Durable, and Worth Every Dollar
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using the Lamicall Bike Phone Holder Mount for a while now, and it’s easily one of the most reliable accessories I’ve added to my bike setup. I’ve actually purchased three of these mounts over time for different bikes, which should say a lot about how well they’ve worked for me.Rock-Solid StabilityThe biggest concern with any phone mount is whether it’ll actually hold your phone in place—and this one delivers. Even on rough roads, bumps, and higher speeds, my phone stays firmly locked in without any rattling or shifting. The grip design feels very secure without being overly tight.Easy Installation & AdjustabilitySetup took just a few minutes with no special tools needed. Once installed, the mount is highly adjustable, so you can position your phone at the perfect angle for navigation or tracking apps. It’s easy to switch between portrait and landscape as well.Build Quality You Can TrustThe materials feel sturdy and well-made. It doesn’t feel cheap or flimsy like some other mounts I’ve tried. The clamp holds firmly to the handlebars, and once tightened, it stays put.Real-World Fit (Important if You Have a Large Phone)I use a large Apple iPhone 15 Pro Max with a battery case for extra protection and charging. With that setup, it just barely fits in the mount. It does hold, but it’s definitely at the upper limit of what this mount can handle. If you’re using a bulky or battery case, you may want to switch to a slimmer protective case to get a more comfortable and secure fit.Great for Everyday UseI mainly use this for GPS while riding, and it’s been a game-changer. Having my phone visible and stable makes rides smoother and safer since I’m not fumbling around or stopping to check directions.Popular for a ReasonIt’s also worth noting this is one of the most reviewed bike phone holders out there, with over 67,000 reviews and around a 4.6-star rating. After using it myself, I can see why—it’s consistent, dependable, and does exactly what it promises.Minor Note (Not a Dealbreaker)Aside from the tight fit with larger/bulkier phones, I haven’t run into any real issues.Final ThoughtsIf you’re looking for a dependable bike phone mount that balances security, ease of use, and durability, this is a great choice. It does exactly what it’s supposed to do—and does it well.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This mount is super steady and quite maneuverable.  It came way under the price point I'd expect for something so well engineered--and it was very simple to affix to my bars.  It grips my Galaxy S23 Ultra securely, but I did have to remove my Otterbox Defender case, not because it wouldn't fit--it did, but it was a tight fit and needied some fiddling to remove it, defeating the one handed operation. I took a minor spill (okay I lost my balance) yet  the mount withmy phone remained rock solid and was cushioned  at all four corners against impact well. I'm glad I purchased this piece of kit, until I purchase a dedicated bike computer, and encourage the reader of this review to do the same.

certifiedBy.description: Recycled Claim Standard (RCS Blended) certified products contain recycled content (>50%) that has been independently verified at each stage of the supply chain, from the source to the final product. features: Compatibility: Engineered exclusively for Samsung Galaxy A17 / A16 5g with precision cutouts that give full access to ports, speakers, and buttons without interfering with wireless charging. Our 24/7 dedicated support team resolves any model or quality concerns instantly.

Military-Grade Dual-Layer Protection: A shock-absorbing TPU interior with reinforced corner airbags and a heat-dissipating honeycomb core is wrapped in a hard polycarbonate outer shell. Certified 14ft drop protection guards your phone against high-impact falls onto concrete warehouse floors and rocky hiking terrain.

360 Screen Defense with Tempered Glass: Each case includes a separate HD tempered glass protector that delivers full edge-to-edge coverage while preserving original touch sensitivity and clarity. It shields against pocket-key scratches and face-down drops on gym tiles or concrete floors.

Practical Design for Secure Grip: Textured side panels and a non-slip matte back provide a confident hold during sweaty gym workouts, one-handed texting, and fast-paced daily commutes. The fingerprint-resistant finish stays clean, and soft-touch buttons deliver crisp, responsive feedback.

All-Scenario Versatility: The minimalist, low-profile matte design blends effortlessly into any environment, from business commutes to weekend hikes. It pairs rugged durability with everyday pocketability for heavy-duty protection without the bulk.

Eco-Conscious Durability: Crafted with over 50% certified recycled materials, this case offers robust protection while supporting sustainable design. Made with safer chemicals under ethical manufacturing conditions, it delivers a long-lasting shield that cares for your device and worker well-being.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Simple, protective case that holds up well
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've used this case on my iPhone 14 Pro Max and have been really happy with it. It fits the phone snugly without adding a ton of extra bulk, which is important with an already large phone.The case has held up well to everyday use and provides a good amount of protection around the edges and camera area. I also like that the back works with magnetic accessories/charging without having to remove the case.It's a fairly simple case, but that's actually what I like about it. It protects the phone, doesn't make it unnecessarily bulky, and has held up well. Good option if you want something functional without spending a lot on a case.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I don't know about "military-level" protection but it certainly feels durable and provides a solid level of protection. The dual-layer design feels sturdy, while still fitting the phone easily. Installation is straightforward, and once on, the case has a snug fit.The textured back provides a good grip and helps reduce the chance of accidental drops. It feels like a practical choice for everyday protection and situations where extra durability is preferred, such as going outdoors and using the camera a lot.Like other cases, it is NOT waterproof, so it should not be relied on for protection against water exposure. Also, when used in dusty or dirty environments, some dirt can collect along the edges and seams of the case. This is not a major issue, as it cleans easily with a microfiber cloth, and a cotton swab works well for reaching the smaller gaps.It is clear but you can put stickers and other decorative designs on the back of your phone to personalize it if you so wish, which makes it convenient.I would say that it is a durable and well-fitting protective case that provides good everyday protection. The main considerations are that it is not waterproof and may require occasional cleaning if used in harsher environments.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a mount that could move between my car and my truck, and this 3-in-1 set is one of the most stable I’ve used. Most budget mounts trade off quality for features, but this one feels surprisingly rugged.The suction cup is the real winner here. It uses a sticky gel that actually stays put on a textured dashboard, even in the summer heat. If it starts to lose its grip, you just rinse it with water and it's sticky again. When I move it to the air vent, the hook design is much more secure than the standard "clip" style that usually slides off during sharp turns.It fits my iPhone with a relatively thick case without any issues. The one-touch release button on the back is smooth and doesn't stick, making it easy to grab my phone and go. The telescoping arm is also a nice touch—it lets me pull the phone closer so I’m not leaning forward to see the GPS.Pros:3-in-1 Flexibility: Works on the windshield, dash, or vent.Superior Suction: The gel base handles heat and textured surfaces well.Long Reach: Telescoping arm extends up to 8 inches.Case Friendly: Holds thick cases (up to 14mm) easily.Cons:Airflow: Like all vent mounts, it will block some AC/Heat when used on the vent.Bulk: It’s a bit larger than minimalist magnetic mounts.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Can almost pass for a flagship phone
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My old Galaxy, which I managed to keep alive for 6+ years, finally got to the point where it could no longer be upgraded and was becoming incompatible with the apps that I use every day.  It's been a great phone-- durable, very reliable, and just enough phone for someone like me.My needs are pretty modest.  I don't game, film videos, or do anything very processor-intensive so I don't need a flagship phone.  The only things I didn't like about my Galaxy was the modest amount of internal memory (only 64Gb), and the amount of Samsung bloatware that I couldn't shut off or get rid of.I didn't want to spend $800 on a phone, but I wanted to keep a lot of the features of my old Galaxy.  Probably most important to me was an IP68 rating, because I've managed to dunk a few phones in my past and I still remember the days when that was a death sentence for them.  I also wanted an SD card slot because I have a large collection of audiobooks and prefer to keep them on external storage.  Aside from that, I wanted more internal storage than the measly 64Gb that my old Galaxy had.  I use a lot of different apps, and I was always bumping up against the storage limit of my old phone.Finally, I really, REALLY wanted a 3.5mm audio jack.  I have Bluetooth earbuds but I greatly prefer my $8 wired earbuds.  They're inexpensive, they never need to be recharged, I won't lose a night of sleep if I lose or damage them, they fit my ears better than the wireless earbuds, and they're inexpensive enough that I can keep a spare pair in my bag in case I forget my daily-use set.A few phones fit the bill but the Moto line of phones had the best reviews, a very reasonable price, and up-to-date hardware and software.  I settled on the Moto G Stylus as it had the best combination of features for my needs.Now that almost all our information is stored in the cloud (for better or for worse), switching to a new phone is very easy.  After I switched my SIM card over, I was instructed to scan a QR code with my old phone.  This initiated a transfer of all my info-- call logs, text history, etc.  The process took a few minutes but was absolutely seamless.Over the next few days, I continued to set my phone up-- logging into apps, playing with different settings, etc.  Just a few days into my ownership, I was prompted to upgrade to Android 16, which I did.  The process went off without a hitch.  From what I've read, I can expect longer battery life, something that I will evaluate in the next few days.Aside from that, the phone has been excellent so far.  The screen is nicer than my ancient Galaxy, it runs all the apps that I use flawlessly, and it hasn't lagged or slowed down at all for me once I got everything set up and updated.  I'm not exactly a power user, but I do use my phone a lot for many different tasks and so far everything is working well.Some people have complained about the camera quality.  I've only snapped a few pics (and no video) but the quality has been pretty good, at least to my eye.  I've examined the images on a computer screen and they are crisp and the colors are vibrant.  The image quality is better on this phone than on some other more expensive phones that I've looked at in the past.I'm still trying to decide if I'll use the stylus or not.  I don't take a lot of hand-written notes but that may change if the apps are intuitive and easy to use.  Time will tell on that one.The phone has some included apps that I will probably never use, but nowhere near the bloat that Samsung was cramming into its phones even 6 years ago.  I am NOT sorry to see the Bixby button and app gone for good.  For those that have never owned a Samsung phone, Bixby is the name of the virtual assistant that is/was loaded onto each phone.  On my old Galaxy, you'd summon Bixby using an extra button on the side of the phone.  I never once used it but I'd accidentally hit that cursed button all the time, which would open up the Bixby screen while I was trying to do something else.  Motorola doesn't do that so good riddance to Bixby.I was dreading the day I'd have to get a new phone because I'd have to start all over again with something that might not be as good as my old Samsung.  That thing was an absolute soldier and worked well for a long time so the bar was pretty high.  While the verdict is out on the Moto G until I put some more miles on it, it's off to a great start.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best Phone I've Had (and I've owned a lot of Moto's) -- Definitely the Current Bargain!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been a rather loyal Motorola phone user. First of all, my first cellular phone (way back in the day) was Motorola, but I've also owned Moto/Motorola branded smartphones since the Nexus 6 (which was branded Google but was actually made by Motorola). After that phone's internal storage failed on me ( watch -- this will become a pattern), I bought a Moto G5S Plus. Then after 2 years when it's internal storage failed on me (told you -- pattern!), I bought first model Moto G Stylus. Then my first Stylus started showing the now familiar signs of failing internal storage (again after 2 years), I bought the Moto G Stylus 5G 2022.  I admit that I probably could've continued using the original Moto G Stylus for a while longer (maybe?), but I also really wanted 5G capability, so when the original Stylus first started slowing down, I just went ahead and bought the then current 5G Stylus model. That was 3 years ago, and just recently (much to my surprise), my Moto G Stylus 5G 2022 started showing signs of a failing battery. Yes, I could've just replaced the battery, but the phone was already 3 years old and I had been watching it carefully for the past year for any sign of the familiar internal storage failure. I just didn't think it was worth the time/trouble to replace the battery only for the internal storage to likely fail sometime soon. So, I decided to move on to the Moto G Stylus 2025.The Positives:And...WOW. Very significant, obvious upgrade! I think everything on the phone is a big improvement over the Stylus 2022 model. The phone is much faster with the newer higher end processor, the cameras are much better quality (as is the improved Moto Camera app, which...sorry...has previously just been useless), the stylus features/apps are much nicer, love the fingerprint sensor being in the screen rather than on the power button, the screen seems much brighter with better refresh (even though I think its technically the same), love the faster wifi with Wifi6, love the newer Bluetooth, and I really like that Moto has kept the headphone jack and expandable storage. The rest of the improvements are mostly due to the OS upgrade, but you can't really disregard those when the older Stylus isn't receiving anymore OS upgrades.The new cameras are just superb in comparison to the Stylus 2022, and I really liked the Stylus 2022 cameras. I've always used GCam ports (specifically BSG MGC) with my Stylus 2022, which is why I always got the great photos that I did. The Moto Camera 3 app was actually just lousy. It used to take a decent enough photo, but then the post processing would pixelize and blotch up the image. The new Moto Camera 5 app actually works a lot like the Google Camera (GCam) and actually enhances the photo in post processing rather than ruining it. I still installed GCam port and sometimes use it, but for most photos I just use the Moto Camera 5 app.So far the battery life has been great, but so was all my Moto cameras, so there's no real surprise there.I was a little disappointed in the lack of color choices of the Moto G Stylus 2025, and I especially miss the seafoam green of my Moto G Stylus 5G 2022 (which I wasn't tired of at all), but I've actually really come to like the purple-ish blue color of "Surf the Net" (whatever that's supposed to mean), and I've put it in a clear case like I did my Stylus 2022 to show off the color.More a matter of market timing than anything else, but it's also nice that this time around I actually found that 1TB microSD cards are now reasonably priced, about as much as the 512GB ones were back when I bought the Stylus 2022. So, now I have a phone with 1,256GB of storage for around $460 total. You're definitely not going to be able to find a Samsung or Apple phone model with that much storage (and all these features) for that low of a price. Moto is definitely the best thing going in bargains.The Negatives:Most of these aren't true negatives, and are actually more like situational issues for me, personally.  First of all, I don't like the new Gemini AI. I was able to easily avoid it when Google offered it as a software upgrade in my last phone, but it's built-in to this one's ROM. It took several tries, but I think I've finally turned it off in most areas of my phone and I'm almost entirely back on the good ol' reliable Google Assistant. I'm sure eventually I will only be offered Gemini.Another personal negative is that apparently this phone is now entirely 64-bit so I ended up losing several of my favorite 32-bit apps. One of them is PicSay Pro photo editor, which is hands-down the best Android photo editor available even though it hasn't had an update or even supported for over a decade. It was removed from Chromebook when it was finally removed from the Google Play Store as unsupported, but it wasn't removed from my phone until I tried to upgrade to this phone and migrate all data and apps. Even so, I tried the backup/restore method to move an old app and it didn't work, citing that the app is not compatible with my phone. The problem is that there is no other photo editor that even comes close to this decade old unsupported app, which is truly pathetic. Fortunately, the latest version of Google Photos that came with the new OS on this new phone, at least has most of PicSay Pro's features, but still not all of them. And no, Snapseed doesn't have it all either. Oh, well.There are other little issues, too, like for whatever reason Moto decided to copy Apple and have the usual power button changed into a multi-function button that does everything except power on/off the phone. That's pretty annoying considering the main reason I'm sticking with Moto is because it's not typically going the way of Apple, Samsung, and Google.Summary:Definitely the best phone I've ever owned, and even though I've liked all my Moto phones, I thought that was never going to happen again after the Nexus 6.  The positives far outweigh any negatives (if there are any legit negatives that would matter to anyone except me), and Moto has definitely brought the Stylus way into the realm of a flagship more than a mid-class phone.  With how Samsung and Google went completely Apple-esque with having no expandable memory, no headphone jack, and a ridiculous high pricetag, the market for me has now ceased to be a question of Android vs. iOS, and it's now Moto vs everything else.  For now, I'm very happy sticking with Moto.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this recently to replace an aging Moto G7 Power (circa 2018?).  I needed this to be my go-to main device to do most things on.  I didn't want a top-of-the-line flagship phone, because they usually have gimmicks that are of limited use to me (like folding screens).  But I still needed a fairly decent spec'd phone to handle everything that I wanted.Having had Motorola and Samsung phones before, I knew that the Motorola would likely closer to pure Android, since Samsung likes to push its One UI on top of everything.  There is still some pre-installed 'bloatware' that Motorola packages with it, but it's really straightforward to remove/uninstall the majority.  A few Moto apps could only be disable, but that's just as good.The main specs for me is that it needed to have storage capacity (my old Moto had long hit its limit), needed to be 5G, needed to be unlocked, and needed good battery life.My past experience with Moto has been that their batteries tend to be better than average life.  This one is no exception - I went 3 days without a charge and light use, and on a day of heavy use I still had ~60% at the end of the day.Back to the storage capacity, the 256GB is plenty of room for apps.  AND, Motorola still includes a microSD slot to add up to 1TB.  That built-in storage has the option to enhance memory performance too by allowing up 8GB to be used as RAM.  That's adjustable too in 2GB increments.One real nice to have is that Motorola finally came around to including NFC and wireless charging in its devices.  That was the final kicker for me that pushed me to get this.  Part of the problem with my old phone is that the charging port was worn and wouldn't always charge unless positioned a certain way.  So, wireless charging is a nicer, more durable feature for me.It's running the latest Android 14 and immediately asked to update to the latest patch after initializing.As for that initializing, Google has really gotten Android to be nearly seamless when migrating devices.  When it came up the first time, it told me what to do with the old phone - basically just turn on bluetooth and scan a QR code.  It asked a few questions of what I wanted to carry over, then it took it all from there.  When it was done and up and running, it had my wallpapers and ringtones and a bunch of other settings that came from my old phone.  It made adjusting to a new device pretty easy.  The only thing I did have to do is remove the unwanted apps that are included, like I mentioned before.  It's now a smoother, more capable version of what my old phone no longer was.The display is nice, clear, and bright.  It's actually really good resolution, I had to get a magnifying glass just to see what is the pixel size.  It's bright enough to still see in the sun, and goes dim enough for at night.The camera is good for a phone camera.  I'm still a dedicated DSLR guy for high quality images.  But this does a fairly good job for the usual everyday photos.  The one rear camera is rated at 50MP, but there is is small caveat to that.  It uses all those pixels in groups to generate a combined 'better' pixel.  This comes out to an effective resolution of around 13MP, which is still more than enough for most needs.  And with that pixel arrangement, the image processing can do things like better digital zoom, and image stabilization.  There is optical image stabilization too.  All-in-all, this does make for fewer blurry picture.  The camera app itself covers all the bases for different needs, include night and action shots.  A nice-to-have in the app is the option to go full manual control, which the photog in me really appreciates.  It's not a full standalone camera, but I can get it to do what I want rather easily.Lastly, there is one thing about this particular phone that I would categorize as a slight gimmick, and that's the stylus.  Don't get me wrong, it is nicely integrated into the body so it's out of the way.  I just have never had the need for a stylus on a phone.  For someone needing the finer point of a stylus, I can see it having a purpose for them.  Who knows, I'll give it a try now and then, and see if I pick up to it.Overall, I am extremely happy with this.  I does what I need, and then some.  It's not a flagship phone, but it's definitely on the higher side of the mid-level category.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This Is One of the Best Kept Secrets
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I can't say enough great things about this phone.  I had always used Samsung Note phones before.  I loved my Samsung Note 9 and never thought I'd replace it, till my new security system said I couldn't install their app because the Note 9 was too old.  And I wanted a stylus.  Had to have a stylus.  Not wanting to spend a fortune on the latest and greatest Samsung Galaxy, I looked at the Motorola Moto G Stylus.The more I looked, the more I liked.  Price was obvious...it's about a third of the price of the Samsung.  But what am I getting?  First off, it had the stylus.  My hands shake and the stylus helps with that.  Then I noticed it was both waterproof and MIL-spec rated for drops and the other abuse I could give it.  That was a plus.  And it had the latest software, so it wouldn't be obsolete soon like my Note 9 was.The more I've used it, the more I like it.  I don't need a bulky case because the outside is textured great for holding it.  And the MIL-spec rating for durability means the case is unneeded.  The screen is incredible.  Bright.  Clear.  Easy to read.  Processing power is notably faster than my Note 9...which was no slouch.  And battery life is also phenomenal.  I can use the phone all day long with a number of apps and still have 70% battery life at the end of the day.  The AI in the phone manages the apps so if they aren't being used, it cuts down on the power to them.  They're still there, and if you want to use them, they are back instantaneously.  But they aren't consuming power in the background.  Good engineering.The only quirk I've found is with the stylus.  For some reason, the width when I'm writing on the screen, is not consistent.  If you're just writing, it is no big deal.  If I was trying to draw something it might be...but then I'd probably use something more appropriate than a small screen device.Oh...and this is a big deal.  This phone comes with a slot to add a SD card.  Most phones like the Samsung phones, don't.  What you initially purchase for memory can't be changed.  You can expand your memory a very little cost with the Motorola.I didn't want to change phones initially.  Since I've purchased this Motorola Moto G, I've never looked back.  I highly recommend this phone to anyone.
