productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Poor camera 😭, GREAT PHONE. Rich feature list, big battery, nimble UI, So close to perfectPoor camera 😭, GREAT PHONE. Rich feature list, big battery, nimble UI, So close to perfect
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve had this a month or so now and have been using it every day and I absolutely love this phone. The operating system isn’t bloated-down, it’s got tons of features and personalization… gestures are very handy, and this phone hasn’t skipped a beat. I swapped my e-sim over from USMobile and once I disabled it in my old phone I was fully going. It’s got plenty of battery to run all day at moderate screen brightness and I’m only charging to 80% to save the battery long term. Even then, it’s usually at 30-40% at the end of the day if I’m using it all day, Bluetooth etc is the only thing that uses much power aside from the screen.Cons- Weak camera system. I really wanted the new/25 model but the price bump, nearly double I think, made it not worth it *to me*, as someone on a budget. Still, it’s a weaker camera than I expected-50mp is a lie, thats including “digital processing” or something, it’s really 12mp I believe. This results in sub-par photos without much depth of detail unless you’re in specific photo modes. The telephoto works pretty well but your every day photos will be kinda low in definition. The photo processing helps but it will occasionally do strange things with the lighting, at least in one particular photo for me.-If you drop it, your pen *will* pop out. It pops right back in but you’d expect a stronger retention system.Pros-Great screen, great/unbloated UI that’s actually useful instead of being just pure bloat, responsive and stable jumping between apps all day, lots of customization options and useful features, the most utility I could find in a phone— stylus, SD card storage, fast charging, fairly large battery, a built-in FM radio…. And since it takes a microSD card, you can buy the 128gb and save some money and roll your large files onto an SD card, I have a highspeed Sandisk in there.Only reason I'm can’t give it a 5 star is because of the weak main camera. It takes roughly equal pics to my old phone, a 22 model iPhone SE (small single camera phone). It’s my only regret as the camera is actually a fairly to highly important feature depending on the user. For someone who’s constantly posting selfies and stuff, it’s bad enough to be a deal breaker. For a casual user like myself? I deal with it, and ask a coworker with an iPhone to take product photos for me.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This phone came with a few small scratches which I was not thrilled about but it was not a make or break for me. I also noticed that this phone had a lot of scratches on the case and even a big dent on the side. The phone I use to have was a Samsung Galaxy S10E. It was such a better phone than this one and half the price. I noticed that my S10E had a far superior camera than this phone as well. The pictures were very blurry and had terrible lighting, not to mention the video had terrible stability. I ended up sending this phone back. It just didn't feel worth the price. One of the good points of this phone was the set up and SD card insert. I had no problems with putting in my mint mobile card. I would not recommend this seller because it was not packed well and came with no charger or cord. I decided to buy a Samsung Galaxy S21 5G instead and couldn't be happier.

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Home and Business Smart 
Smart, reliable 2-line business, home/home office system designed to make calling, voice messaging and conferencing easy and convenient for everyone. Expandable to 12 cordless handsets. 
Features 
Secure, Long-Range Signal 
Designed with DECT 6.0 Plus, the KX-TG9582B system ensures clear sound, added reliability and long-range signal security throughout the home or office. Its enhanced signal strength won't interfere or conflict with routers, wireless keyboards, microwaves and other devices. 
2-Line Advantage 
With the convenience and control of two lines plus a corded and corded handset, it's easy to manage calls and voice messaging. Use both lines to manage business needs or keep work and home separate with a dedicated line and separate greetings and voice message recording for each. 
Sync Four Smartphones 
With Link2Cell you can sync up to four cell/smartphones via Class 1 Bluetooth (range up to 330 ft.) to make and receive mobile calls using any cordless handset, everywhere you have one. Cell calls are automatically routed to your handsets, and you can assign distinctive ringtones to the handsets to distinguish mobile calls from other calls. 
Easy Call Block 
With Call Block you can avoid calls from up to 250 telemarketers, robocallers and other bothersome, unwanted caller numbers. 
3-Way Conferencing 
Conduct conversations simultaneously from your phone and two other phones. Conference hands-free with high-quality speakers in the base unit and handsets, and use enhanced noise reduction to suppress surrounding noise when conferencing-in calls from noisy locations. 
Call with Outlook 
Connect your phone to your business or home office PC via USB to make outgoing calls to your Outlook contacts, plus receive incoming calls with a single click. 
To make a call just highlight the person's name on your contact list, activate the speakerphone function on the base unit or cordless handset, and click. No need to dial. To answer calls, click the incoming caller pop-up window on your display to talk hands-free on your speakerphone while you're working. 
Power When the Power Goes Out 
When the lights go out, a powerful battery back-up system keeps you connected for up to 75 minutes during outages with two long-lasting rechargeable Ni-MH AAA-size batteries (included) in the base unit. You will also have power for up to 15 hours talk time and seven days standby for calls using other cordless handsets in the house. 
Text and Caller ID 
Get instant alerts on your handsets when texts are received on your synced cell/smartphones. And when the phone rings on one side of the room and you're on the other, Talking Caller ID uses advanced text to speech technology to tell you who's calling. 
Bright, Quick-Read LCDs 
Clearly see numbers and calling info in any light conditions on a large, adjustable 3.4-inch white backlit LCD on the base unit and handset LCDs. 
Additional Conveniences 
Phonebook and Speed Dials 
Transfer and update up to 3,000 names and numbers via Bluetooth from your cell/smartphones to the high-capacity, built-in directory, plus dialing time with 20 speed dials. 
Battery Power Backup 
When the lights go out, a powerful battery back-up system keeps you connected for up to 75 minutes during outages with two long-lasting Ni-MH rechargeable AAA-size batteries (included) in the base unit. 
*Global #1 Brand Cordless Phones

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best cordless phone system I have used
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a great phone system!  One of the best features, that I wasn't even aware of until they arrived, is that the phones don't use the typical battery packs that are impossible to find or too expensive to replace.  These phones use normal, NiMH rechargeable AAA!  I buy new cordless phone systems every 3 years because the phones won't hold a good charge anymore and the replacement battery packs cost more than new phones (if you can even find them).  The fact that these phones use normal, easily replaceable batteries is a huge deal for me.  That one feature alone makes up for the slightly higher cost of entry because I'll make up for it in a 3 years, but these phones also have great features and work very well that also make the price worth it.  With all of the features that these phones come with, I don't foresee the need to replace the phone system for a very, very long time.Adding new handsets to the system is incredibly simple.  There are some features that are more complicated to use that you will have to reference the manual for, but that's only because it can do so much.  Basic functions are easy and intuitive.  Call quality is good.  The Link2Cell feature was a requirement for me, and it works well.  The cordless range is very good, even without the optional extender.If you have a wired headset plugged into the headset jack, then you cannot use the speakerphone.  I was hoping to leave a headset hooked up to the phone for longer calls, but use the speakerphone for shorter calls, and that doesn't work well.The speakerphone quality is okay.  The microphone picks up people on the other side of the room, which is good for me, but could be bad for others.  I haven't actually been on the other side of a speakerphone call, but my wife tells me it echoes a bit, but that could be because I have it mounted on the wall.Overall, I am very pleased with this phone system and very glad I purchased it.  I fully expect to use it for 10 years or more.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very Happy With This Phone System
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a great phone system.  I have two phone lines (yes I still want a landline in my house) one I use for my personal use and the other for business.  I have purchased other brands of phone systems similar to this in the past and they were terrible.  The issues with the others systems were too many to count.  I took a long time researching a new phone system and I very happy I picked this one.Here is what I love about this phone:1.  It works as it should2.  No crazy bright blue light on it showing it's charging.  My previous phones systems all had this and I didn't like it.  This has a display on the face and when I pick up the hand set is the only time it lights up.3.  You can hear people on the other end. Both on the main base and on the cordless handsets.4.  Re-playing a message is easy.  So is deleting a message.5.  CID is easy6.  Editing a number from CID is easy7.  It has a cool feature that after 2 or 3 rings it will announce who is calling.  When I'm not right near a phone it helps me determine if I wan to run to pick up the call.8.  The batteries seem to last a long time.Cons:1.  Challenging to set up your outgoing VM message.2.  Ok not a big a thing but I did purchase a head set to plug into my cordless phone and the rubber thing on the side where you plug the head set into is difficult to move.  I sometimes have to use a butterknife to unplug the rubber piece.  The jack doesn't seem to work too well.  I did purchase the headset that was recommended to go with it.Overall I recommend this phone to anyone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Simple to set up the basic setup card.  After that good luck with the most complicated instruction booklet we have ever seen!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: We use Comcast Business internet and its phone service starting in June.  Our old AT&T phone system was not working well.Comcast Business phones does not allow us to block spam/crank calls in spite of supposedly having a system.  Nor does it allow us to use NoMoreRobo calls as plain Comcast did.So we were swapped with spam/crank calls.This unit can block a lot of calls (it "ain't" that easy), more on that later.The setup using the fast set up system card was easy and worked well for the base phone and the remote.The quality of the phone calls is excellent,  and the remote works in our home and outside.However, that was the last easy thing with this phone.As noted by many other users, the instruction booklet is over whelming and complicated.I did programming in the 1960's for business and the Navy.  We were among the first to have a home pc.We have used Android Phones since they came on the market. The same with Android or Amazon Fire tables, Ace Chromebooks and a Win 10 laptop.  So we are not  virgins re tech stuff.Again, the instruction booklet is terrible to deal with.  One of our grandsons is the IT guy for his family, neighbors, friends, classmates and his old grandparents when we need help.  He carries a portable Mac, I phone and an Apple tablet to his classes at a private school and uses them everyday for classwork, homework and to communicate with friends everywhere.After a frustrating hour with the instruction booklet, he gave up.We finally are able to block spam/crank calls but you have to go through a fairly complex protocol for each number, versus just pushing a button on the main phone or remote to block the calls.There are a ton of supposed options to use with the phones, again the instructions are too complex.In summary, the phones were easy to set up and are reliable and come back on if there has been a power failure or a break in the Internet.We would probably prefer being mugged than dealing with the Instruction Booklet.A humorous thing is when someone calls, a voice on the set in not that great of English tries to tell us who is calling in a flat SE Asian nasal tone with miss pronounced words.  We and guests laugh at this butchering of English.  The funnest is when a friend who is named Christopher calls.  The phone announcer with that funny accent/tone tells us that Christ is calling.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Move along, folks... nothing to recommend here...
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I thought I hated our existing VTech system.  This Panasonic system is FAR worse.  The lowlights?- Fragile-feeling, chintzy handsets.- The sound quality is terrible.- Every available ringtone is nerve-grating.- Putting someone on hold requires opening a menu and scrolling to the "Hold" option.  Who thought that was a good idea?!On the bright side, the range is amazing as long as you stay in the same room as the base.  Put more than one wall betwixt you and the base phone, and you can forget about it.  The handset might ring, but it won't answer.  No, endless adjusting of the various settings did not improve any of these drawbacks noticeably.  The glaring "hold" design flaw certainly can't be overcome.I've always been a fan of Panasonic equipment, but this cordless system is a staggering failure front to back.  The base phone itself is quite nice other than the dreadful ringtones; unfortunately they don't appear to offer the base separately.  So this whole system is being returned... it's actually unlivable in a fast-paced environment with lots of movement between rooms.I've ordered replacement handsets for my aging VTech system instead.  I've got a whole new appreciation for it after this.

Speaker phone on the base unit could stand to be a lil louder but that's just my preference maybe... but I can hear ok as long as I stay focused on listening to the other person and not try to multitask too much with my mind. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased this Galaxy renewed S23 5G for my husband because his phone was junk and and the battery barely held a charge anymore. It's unlocked so you can use it with any carrier (we use T-Mobile and it was a breeze to take it in and transfer everything from his old phone over to this new one. Because it's 5G , Internet speeds and app downloads are fast.  The screen is in impeccable condition, no scratches or dents. The entire phone is in immaculate condition.  The only reason I'm deducting 1 ⭐, is because the battery isn't what we were hoping for.  It drains fast, doesn't hold a charge all day.  With that being said, I have to be completely transparent and acknowledge the fact that my husband never puts his phone down.  He's on this phone more than not. And he does a lot of gaming on it and watches a lot of social media videos, so that very well could be contributing to the battery draining faster. I'm going to have to try to pry it away from him while he's sleeping and check his settings because he's technically challenged and has been known to keep location on 24/7 and use other options or settings that can cause the battery to drain quicker.  But aside from the battery, the phone is like new, and takes beautiful pictures and videos.  I think it was a good value for what you get.Update:  So my husband has had this phone for a few weeks and he's complaining about the battery draining quickly.  I thought I had ordered Amazon Renewed Premium, and realized that I only ordered renewed.  This is where the difference is with regards to the battery. title: Phone-Free Evenings: A 21-day plan for parents of school-age kids to park the phones after dinner and get bedtime back
author: The Phone Bowl Press
breadCrumbs: Kindle Store > Kindle eBooks > Self-Help > Stress Management
bookDescription:
A 21-day plan for parents of school-age kids to park the phones after dinner and get bedtime back.
Evenings are a scroll pile: dinner, homework, and bedtime keep losing to phones, including yours. This is not a culture manifesto and not an adult digital-detox memoir. It is an evening install for the hours after 5pm.
Short paragraphs. Scripts you can say once. Cards you can tape by a bowl. Composite school-night houses, not portraits. A bowl is a bowl. No gadget brand as a cure.
What you actually get:• Night-one forty minutes: bowl, station, one clock, three promises you will not make• If you only have tonight: four moves and stop• The 21-day shape from audit to a one-page house rule• A 48-hour map of where every phone goes, including the parent phones• A visible bowl after dinner and charging in a hall or kitchen, not a bedroom• Parents first: the sequence the kids can see• Dinner without a screen as the centerpiece, plus photo and work-ping scripts• Homework hour with a lid-down time and no YouTube as the open tutor• Park time as a clock, and a house definition of "off"• Bedtime with the charger already out of the room• Pushback lines for guests, carpool, two homes, and the kid who bargains• Named exceptions so every night is not a hearing• Day 21 closeout page, calendar, copy-ready scripts, two-home card
This is not medical advice, therapy, or a treatment for insomnia, anxiety, ADHD, or "addiction." It will not tell you to ignore a court order, a custody agreement, or a school's required device. It does not promise grades, mental health, or a closer family in 21 days. It will not coach hidden tracking apps or sell a branded dock as the plan. If a child is in crisis, get local professional help. A stricter bowl is not a crisis plan.
Put a bowl where you rinse plates. Put your phone in first. Set a number. The rest of the book is how not to turn the next twenty nights into a debate series.
Forthcoming tools from THE PHONE BOWL PRESS: a homework-lid card, and a two-home evening card.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Not really unlocked and it can't read physical SIM card
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Even though the phone looked great and was advertised as unlocked, I could never get it to work.  It would not read the SIM or ESIM provided by either company that I tried, and it took weeks and weeks and paying for phone plans through two different phone carriers for a month each paid up front to realize that the phone itself had some kind of flaw.  Both companies spent hours with me on the phone, trying repeatedly to get the phone I bought to talk to their system, as it was showing as compatible, but the phone itself kept saying to insert a SIM card, even though I tried three different physical SIM cards, , plus downloaded ESims from each company, and it just kept saying insert a SiM card.  Hundreds of dollars down the drain, plus an extra hundred in useless phone plans, and no way of finding out that it is actually a bad phone until it is too late to make a complaint, because it takes so long to get a SIM card from a phone company each time.  One of the techs said that it may be a cloned phone or from another country, or locked to a carrier, but sold as unlocked, but that they really had no idea what was wrong with it, just that they could find no way to get it to connect and talk to their system. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: All round a decent mid-range phone. Currently daily driving it. And I'll say for 350 bucks this is definitely worth it. Battery is decent, not amazing but notable. Speakers are nice and can get pretty loud if needed. The phone itself is sleek and smooth. HyperOS (the operating system) itself is well made and it'd very iOS-esque, but is bloated to all hell. Recommend looking up "Canta" or getting familiar with ADB to debloat. It comes with a simple case and screen protector which surprised me. Also comes with a USB-A to USB-C charger. For gaming, it runs Zenless Zone Zero at medium settings at a tolerable level and at low settings it's smooth (it's a demanding game, or maybe just poorly optimized). But if you want to do gaming I'd recommend getting the 512GB + 12GB RAM variant for 50 dollars more. 8GB is kind of tight. But if you aren't doing considerable gaming then this suffices. Finally, it worked flawlessly with T-Mobile, I didn't have to do any extra steps. It was just plug and go with my sim card.FOR POWER USERS:Xiaomi is very strict with rooting. This was my first Xiaomi phone and I learned there's a mandatory 30 day account age requirement plus a ~7 day wait before you can unlock the bootloader in order to root.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: HMD needs to make a U.S. version of this phone STATHMD needs to make a U.S. version of this phone STAT
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The phone itself is actually really nice, has a lot of features and comes with 3 full games plus cloud phone apps. It is the perfect dumb phone.I HAVE to give it a 1 star though because it doesn’t work correctly in the U.S. even if you’re using it on the recommended GSM networks. It’s lacking specific bands that allow full service in the U.S. I even added the correct APN for Tello and it did nothing. The service stayed at G instead of LTE and whenever it did switch to LTE it was only for a few seconds. Couldn’t send or receive MMS. It could only send texts, not receive texts, and if it did receive texts they would come an hour later after sending. The only thing that worked well were phone calls (sending & receiving is fine) and the radio, so if that’s all you need, by all means purchase this phone. If anything though, get a U.S. specific Nokia phone, cause this one; although cute and nostalgic, is NOT it. I wanted to like it so bad but it’s a waste of money for Americans. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I made the switch to this phone as a way to get away from constantly getting sucked into my smartphone. It has been doing the job fairly well; Snake is fun, YouTube is a nice addition (Shorts are functional and it has YouTube Music as well), other apps like a basic web browser, a weather app, caluculators/converters, flashlight etc. prove useful. The audio quality honestly astounded me. I have ~700 songs on an SD card and it plays louder through the aux than my Galaxy A14 did, and the speaker is pretty nice. The camera is okay. It exists, but nothing much to speak about it. The operating system has a sleek modern design that I found to be visually appealing, with some personalization options. The text messaging system has had a couple of glitches, but nothing too terrible, like some messages disappearing on phone restart and I had an issue where I had a message notification but didn't see any unread message. I am in the Southeastern United States, and coverage has been well with my Metro SIM Card (except in my office, the only spot I haven't got coverage :/ ) . For people in the US wondering if it works: yes, it should on the T-Mobile network. The manual states that it supports LTE bands 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12, 13 (w/o NS07), 17, 28, 40, and 66. I feel like this is not well-documented online so seeing that in the manual was a relief. Wi-Fi support would've been a nice addition. The battery lasts well enough for a day or two, I haven't had it die on me yet as long as I stay mindful of plugging it in occasionally. Overall, I'd say this a cool little device for people looking to stay connected in a basic way, or for techies wanting to revisit the past in a modern skin.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent phone with big improvements over the Pixel 6.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This phone is by far the best one I've owned thus far. I upgraded from a Pixel 6 and have been using this one for about two months now. Its battery life is excellent, and unlike the 6, it gets excellent 5G reception even in our semi-rural neighborhood where the signal is very weak. It's free of service provider bloatware, the Google-installed utilities are largely unobtrusive, and its touch screen accuracy is much better than my previous phones, including the 6.Phone call quality is great in most cases, the onboard speakers sound excellent, the fingerprint reader is much improved and very fast, it supports Qi and Qi2 wireless charging, and the camera is very high quality. (Note that the 10 does not have a macro lens like the 10 Pro.)Very happy with this phone so far.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Love this phone, but the battery thinks '24hr/full day' is a suggestion
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great phone overall. The screen display is amazing, build quality feels solid, and the camera is fantastic. My only real concern is the battery — it's not the best. I'll wake up in the morning to find it's dropped 7-10% overnight, even with power saving mode on. I did figure out a fix though: after a full charge, just restart the device and it won't drain like that. Honestly, I've had budget phones hold a charge better than this.The color is nice, but it doesn't really matter since you'll end up slapping a case on it anyway. Big plus that it came fully unlocked.My one wish: Google should go with a Snapdragon CPU, because the Tensor G5 is terrible for gaming — it heats up fast. But for daily use it's great.Would still recommend, just go in knowing the battery quirks — it CANNOT last a full day with heavy usage. That's why it's a solid 4 stars and not 5.One last thing: it was listed as "Used - Good," but this was honestly a new phone. Charging cycles were around 20, no scratches, original packaging, and the cable hadn't even been used.

features: 2-in-1 Mounting for 99% Vehicles: This phone holder for car offers both dashboard and vent mounting options, giving first-time wireless car charger buyers more ways to find the right fit for their vehicle. The military-grade 3M dashboard base uses a dual-support structure and is tested through 4 environmental reliability tests from -40°F to 194°F, while the reinforced vent hook is extended by 60% to fit more air vents. Its compact charging head helps reduce windshield obstruction and avoids blocking airflow, making installation easier and lowering the risk of choosing the wrong mount.

15W Wireless Charging for Nonstop Driving: This LISEN MagSafe car mount charger combines a magnetic phone holder and 15W wireless car charger in one compact design, helping keep your phone powered throughout the trip. Just place your phone on the mount when you get in, and charging starts automatically; when you arrive, simply lift it off and go. Built for GPS, calls and music on long drives, it is especially useful for Uber, Lyft and delivery drivers who need steady power on the road.

Strong Magnetic Hold, No Button Blocking: Built with 24 N52 magnets and up to 3800gf magnetic force, this car phone holder is tested to hold the weight of 8 phones at once for a more stable hold on bumpy roads and sharp turns. Its clamp-free magnetic design keeps side buttons accessible, so you can place your phone with one hand and use GPS, calls or music without extra adjustment.

Ice Blue LED Glow for Interior Style: This magnetic car accessories mount charger features an ice blue LED light ring that adds a modern accent to your car interior at night. The soft glow helps you quickly locate the mount in low-light driving conditions, while the magnetic one-hand snap-on design makes phone placement easier during night drives, parking, commuting and GPS use.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Good-----------------------+ Really strong magnet+ Multiple mounting options (vent or adhesive)+ Adhesive mount is very flexible in its design that would allow it to fit in a much wider array of places compared to others+ 15W fast charging+ Ring light on charger can be useful for finding it in low light settingsThe Bad------------------------ Haven't found any yetThe Nitpicky-----------------------= Took me a little bit to figure out that you have to rotate the base to extend the hook for the vent mount, instructions are mostly just a QR code for a videoThoughts-----------------------I previously had an ESR magsafe charger for my car, but the plastic bit that connects the base to the mount broke and there's no fixing that. Not too broken up about it because the ESR charger was always hit or miss whether it would actually charge my phone or not. Sometimes I could be driving for 30-45 minutes and it would only charge my phone 1-2% when it wasn't even doing anything (no GPS, no CarPlay, nothing). I tried different cigarette port adapters, cables, with and without a case, even more than one ESR charging base and every time the same thing. Even across multiple phones when I upgraded my iPhone 12 to a 15.So this time I went in search of something different and settled on this. Only had a chance to use it on a single trip as of time of writing, but after I figured out you need to twist the base to extend/retract the hook for the vent mount, things went pretty smoothly. The magnet is pretty strong, so it won't be going anywhere during normal driving. Unlike the ESR I had before, this time even on a relatively short trip of maybe 10 minutes to the grocery store, it had already charged the phone by around 1-2%. As long this behavior is consistent, I'll be happy. I also prefer this vent mount to the old ESR one. The ESR was like a clothespin that you just "clipped" onto the vent flap, while this one hooks around the back and then you tighten things up so that it's pressing against other parts of the vent to provide additional stability. The adhesive mount is also interesting how it can be made to fit a much broader array of surfaces compared to most mounts. Suppose the drawback would be in finding replacement adhesive pads if you ever need them.Edit 2/8/25: Still so far so good. Unlike the ESR charger, where charging was hit or miss, this one is working consistently. I've noticed that, unlike with the ESR, I get the charging screen with the circular graph of battery charge every time I attach my phone to this charger.Edit: 2/23/25: Probably the last update as the device is still working well and I have no new issues with it. I don't usually like to drive at night if I can help it, but the light around the charger can be useful for letting me know where I need to put my phone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Charging repeatedly turns on and off without end
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update #2: I received an e-mail from Lisen in response to my inquiry. The rep said to make sure the charger that plugs into the cigarette lighter has a minimum 20W output. In review of the Samsung "Adaptive Fast Charger" I was using, nowhere on it does it state the output wattage. So I borrowed an Ainope 36W charger and tried it. This completely resolved the problem. With the 36W Ainope charger, the phone now charges on the Lisen magnet Qi mount with no issues. I see that the instructions supplied with the Lisen Qi mount charger do state that the output charger needs to be a minimum of 18W. Conclusion: The Samsung charger I was using has an output wattage of less than 18, causing it to be incompatible with the Lisen magnetic Qi charging mount. I suspect that many of the other reviewers who experienced this same problem were also trying to use output chargers that have less than 18W. I have updated my rating to 4 stars. Minus one star because at the time of my original review, Lisen's hyperlinks to both their "support" page and to their "contact us" page took me to their product sales page, which was a bit frustrating. Otherwise the response and service from Lisen was great. As both a phone car mount and a Qi charger, this product is highly recommended with the use of a compatible output charger. Many older vehicles have lower output USB ports that won't work, and many older cigarette lighter chargers do not have enough output wattage to work. Back when I purchased my previous phone, a Samsung S9 Plus that came with the cigarette lighter charger I was trying to use, 10W was considered to be a "Fast Charger," but that is not enough juice to support this Lisen Qi charger.Update #1: I see that other reviewers have had the identical problem I am having. I used the Lisen product support link on Amazon, which takes me to the Lisen website *product sales* page (not to a support page). While on the Lisen website, I found and clicked on the "support" hyperlink. It also takes me to the sales page, not to a support page. Then I clicked the "contact us" link, which also takes me to the same product sales page... not to a contact page. I found a support e-mail address on the product box and sent an e-mail describing the problem. In reference to my original post, the Lisen phone number I called is the one posted on Amazon. I got an answering machine and left a message with my phone number and requested a return call. We shall see how this plays out.While my phone is mounted to the Lisen wireless phone charger Model 2E778, which is connected to a Samsung Fast Charger plugged into my car cigarette lighter, the charging starts, goes into turbo charging mode, then the charging stops a second or two later, then this cycle repeats over and over again never ending. The Mount attaches securely to my car vent. The magnetic mount is strong. If I can get the charging function to work, this would be a good product. I am using a newly purchased Motorola Edge + 2023 with the circular magnet applied to the outside of a Poetic case. The Poetic case has only a thin clear piece of plastic film on the backside and the circle magnet is attached to the plastic film. There is no thick plastic case that the charging has to penetrate through. Troubleshooting steps taken: I used the Lisen supplied USB cable plugged directly into my phone and the car charger. Charging worked normally with no issues. I placed the phone (in the Poetic case with magnet installed) on two different non-magnetic Qi chargers in my home. Charging worked great on both without interruption. I slid the backside of the phone around on the Listen charger to make sure I have correctly located the circular magnet and confirmed the magnet is correctly positioned and installed. If the phone is moved up, down, right, or left, there is no charging connection. On the sweet spot where the magnet is installed, charging starts, but then cycles on and off repeatedly. I called the manufacturer and left a recorded message explaining the problem and requested a call back. I will update this review if the problem is resolved.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought these to replace a set that was over ten years old. I chose a Panasonic to replace a set because that set was incredible (and lasted over ten years.).Pro: Back-lit buttons are nice, the display is fine, definitely better than those phones that are amber black-lit. Plenty of room in your Phone Book and blocked numbers list. Quality construction, I dropped one a couple of times on hard surfaces, no damage. You can set up the phones as a baby monitor. Big reason I bought these is the call block button - block calls immediately anytime whether you’ve answered it or not. Display a previous call and block the number. With the old set I’d have to go thru multiple menu settings to block one call.Con: Battery life isn’t that great, don’t leave them off the hook overnight, but that may improve once the batteries are go through some charging cycles. Reception range is average, definitely less than our old set.This set is really fine, except for some disappointing operation.  The reception is not as strong as my previous set. The sound quality of the speaker phone is poor, distorted. My old set lit up if you had a voice mail message or a missed call. This one only lights up for messages. I miss that feature.  The buttons are too sensitive, many times when the phone rings, if I pick it up it would answer the call before it could display the caller ID.Despite all of the above I would still recommend this set, although battery life and reception may be downers. And it’s Panasonic.

Key Features: 
Simple, corded operation 
Reliable, corded operation eliminates the search for a misplaced cordless handset, while sturdy construction ensures long-lasting performance. Clean design makes it an easy fit on any counter or wall. 
Caller ID/call waiting 
Allows you to view the name, number, time and date of incoming calls at a glance, even those on call waiting. 
Audio Assist 
With the touch of a button, Audio Assist temporarily increases overall volume and enhances sound frequencies that make speech easier to understand. 
Extra-large tilt display for easy viewing 
Extra-large, easy-to-read LCD on the base tilts for best viewing angle. This feature provides a clear view of the incoming Caller ID or call history. 
Extra-large buttons

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Just What I Was Looking For......
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My old cordless phone with a built in answerer had finally given up the ghost. Even though it still worked, you couldn't tell what the display was showing anymore and it was beginning to lost connections when away from the base. The main reason was the display as you couldn't tell what you were dialing anymore. At any rate, I really wanted a cord type phone as the cordless was not of any use if a power outage took place. I needed a phone with answerer and number memory so I wouldn't have to keep up with the numbers as I'm really bad keeping up with things like this without keeping notes, etc. I checked this phone out for a replacement for the old one. It seems to have all the features I needed and a few I didn't need. After reading the reviews and looking over the features, I decided it was the one for me. Got it in yesterday and unpacked and looked it over. Liked it's look and styling. I noted it could be wall mounted and as I had once had a wall mounted cord phone that I liked this was great. I got a 25 foot headset cord to go with it and had no trouble installing it. After the usually drilling holes, placing of screws and getting the phone mounted, I had it set up and checked it out. First thing I noted was the answerer's message is very bland and I changed that right off the bat. This was very easy to do and that sort of surprised me as my old one had been a bit of a pain to change. I noted that this phone has easy to read prompts to help and also voice cues to help you. The display was large and easy to read, but the angle on my wall was such that I had to up the contrast to be able to see it OK. This was very easy to do. Changing any settings were very easy to do and the manual that came with it was very helpful in this. Entering numbers in the phone's memory was likewise very easy to do. I did note one thing in the manual however that was a bit confusing. The manual states the phone has 10 speed dial locations and it does, but what it doesn't point out is that these locations are taken from the phone's total memory for phone numbers which is 25 total. So if you store 10 speed dial items, then you only have 15 slots left in the directory slots. In the manual, it seems to say that you have 10 speed dial and 25 phone directory locations when you only have 25 slots total. That said, that's a very minor thing for me. I really liked the ability to turn off the ringer and the call monitoring feature if you wanted to. The display stays off until a call is received or you use the phone. It then comes on and if the call monitor and ringing are off, it stays silent when dealing with the call. My old phone would sometimes wake me up when it received a call and you couldn't turn this off on it. This was a real pleasure for me. It also has volume controls and a type of "tone" adjustment that I set to natural as that sounded good to me. On the power outage front, I noted that if you lose power the basic phone functions are still there as they run off the phone company's line voltage. (My old one would just go dead until the power came back up.) Overall, this phone is just what the doctor ordered for me and I'm very happy with it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good Quality, Excellent Sound, Easy to use, Functions Well, No EMF
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted a corded answering machine to avoid EMF from cordless phones and cell phones, and after buying several different stand-alone answering machines that had crappy sound quality and features, I bought this corded phone answering machine. I have been very pleased with the quality and features. The large display is easy to read, the function buttons operate and are laid out logically, sound quality of call recordings, the greeting, and on the handset is excellent, and plenty loud, even for those who are hard of hearing. There is a large easy to use volume control button on the phone face, so it's easy to adjust the ringer, recording, handset, or speaker phone volume on the fly.Initial setup is intuitive enough that I didn't need the manual to set it up. The screen has amber colored backlighting when a call comes in or when you press any button on the phone. It's easy to read even from a few feet away, but not sure if color blind people may have a problem with the amber backlighting. The power button is a large red lighted button when on, and the message indicator is a large red flashing button that is easy to see from a distance.The phone does NOT require batteries, and since I have it connected to a hard-wired landline, it uses the land line's phantom power to keep settings when we have frequent power outages/blips, so I don't have to reset anything after a power outage. I don't know if it will do this on a VOIP line. You can make calls during a power outage, at least with a hard land line, but the display won't work, unless you have the phone's power supply connected to a UPS.You can record your own custom greeting or use an auto announcement.One caveat, if you pick up a call from an extension, the phone shows it as a missed call on its screen, which I couldn't care less about since I only care about messages, but you can easily scroll through the call log on screen to see any missed calls.Also annoying, if a call comes in and the answering machine picks up and then you pick up on the phone or an extension, the recorder will not shut off, and broadcast your call through the speaker. The only way to stop this is to unplug the power supply.You can wall mount the phone. I see in other reviews references to the instructions being only in Spanish, this was not the case with my phone.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this phone for my mother, who isn't very good with technology, is a bit hard of hearing, and doesn't see very well.I specifically bought the phone for the large LCD display with the orange background, because of its high contrast, and the hearing assist feature.The ringer can be turned up nice and loud, and the hearing assist feature amplifies the caller enough that mom can easily hear the person on the other end. She can also read the caller ID display, so this phone has met my expectations.It's also pretty easy to use. When viewing the caller ID list, if she wants to call someone back, all she needs to do is pick up the handset and the phone will dial the number. So she can use this phone even though she's not very technologically savvy.There are a few things that I don't like about the phone.- Limited Directory listings. You can only store 25 numbers into memory. These days when you may have a home phone, plus two or three mobile numbers for a family member, 25 numbers just isn't adequate. Especially if you need to take into account: Children (and spouses) grandchildren, friends, etc... 50 would be a better limitation, while 100 numbers would probably be ideal.- Directory isn't alphabetical! I can't figure this one out, as it would seem that alphabetizing your phone list would be basic functionality. However, this phone doesn't seem to think so. What this means, is that it makes it difficult to find individual phone numbers using the directory. The directory has a feature (most phones do this) that you can enter the directory, then press one of the number keys to go directly to a letter of the alphabet. In theory, this makes it easy to locate a number. Calling a name starting with a "J"? Press the 5 button and start scrolling through the "J's". With this phone though, the numbers are in the directory in the order you've added them... So, you can press the 5 button to get to the J's, but scrolling down may go J, S, B, etc... This just doesn't make any sense to me... The manual says the entries will be sorted alphabetically if you go to a letter and scroll down, but this isn't the case. No matter how I try to scroll through the directory, it isn't sorted properly.- Abridged manual. For some reason, the manual included with this phone is the abridged version. If you want the full manual, you'll need to download the .PDF from AT&T's support site.The abridged manual doesn't describe some functionality that I would consider necessary information. For example, the abridged manual tells you how to add your home area code, as well as four alternate local area codes. What it doesn't explain is what this area code is used for. In my area, the area code is required on local calls, so the phone should display 10 numbers. Thinking that adding the area code would enable this functionality, I added it as my home area code. Then I was trying to figure out why the caller ID was only showing 7 numbers. So if you tried to call a number back using the caller ID information, the call wouldn't go through because it won't dial the area code first.After trying to figure out what was going on, I noticed that the manual said it was the abridged version... What? So I went to AT&T's website and downloaded the full manual. The full manual describes that the function of adding the area code is the opposite of what I would expect. Adding your home area code to the phone will cause the caller ID data to NOT show the area code! If you need the area code to make local calls, don't add your area code... The full manual also explains how to change this data on the fly using the pound key. If a number comes through as showing only 7 digits and you need 10, you can press the pound key to add the area code to the number. Why isn't this in the abridged manual?- Audio assist is per call. You can't tell the phone to always use audio assist. You must press the audio assist button each time you are on a call. I can see how this would make sense if multiple users are going to be using the phone, but if only a single person will be using it and they are hard of hearing, it would be nice to have a way to always enable the audio assist.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm completely pleased with this phone.  I was a bit worried coming from my Pixel 8, considering all I've had are Pixel devices for years now - but I wanted something I could fold up and make smaller, throw in my bag or pocket without issues and I've heard good things about the Razr.  I'm always switching up phones, it's my vice I guess but so far I will say I'm really loving this one.  Compared to the Pixel 8, the speed of the device, the battery life, its all very comparable.  I don't have any issues with lagging, which I thought might happen, but no issues there.  The extra features it adds with the ability to flip open the phone are nice, though I don't use them a ton.  I do like the fact that for a number of apps I don't even have to open the phone, I can use them right from my front screen on the device - that's a huge plus for me.  Not all of them work perfectly as not all of them are designed for that type of use, but to my surprise many of them work just fine!  The hinge/folding part of the screen can be a little noticeable but I expected that, and it doesn't bother me at all while using the phone, scrolling, viewing, etc.  The sound on the device is good, clear, I don't see much of a difference vs. my prior Pixel.Now, the one thing you can't compare is the camera.  While its acceptable for me on this device, the Pixel blows it away.  If that's important to you, take note.  The camera is not bad at all honestly - I can just tell the difference, especially when taking pictures in bright light - now maybe that is on me and I need to make adjustments but compared to the Pixel its just not as good.Also, I found it odd that it has preinstalled factory made screen covers - there are multiple warnings stating not to remove them or you void your warranty, etc.  So yeah, DON'T remove them.  I hope they're strong enough - I worry about what you do when they crack...but I've saved that thought for another day.Overall, I'd say if you're on the fence and you want a folding device like this one, it's a great choice especially for the price.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have been using my RAZR for 2+ weeks.  Have been (and still keeping as a backup) Pixel 7.  Bottom line: this has surpassed my expectations.  My primarily reason for wanting a razr is because of size and compactness, it's so much easier to carry and there are no small phones any more (I'd jump at something like iPhone 4 size).  Vs the Pixel, I give up Pixels unique phone filtering setup for intercepting callers, it's superb voice mail intercept and transcription.  Also photo editing capability can't match pixel.  And while the speed is plenty good enough for me, I can sense slight lag in opening launching some apps, not a big deal.  Some people complain about the crease... It's basically unnoticeable for me.  Open, it feels real smooth like a large slab.  I'm not a rough user but I sense the close mechanism is really well designed, satisfying to open and close.  After years of slippery phones,  the 2024 faux leather texture is just a pleasure and beautiful to look at.  I have a couple of cases and they're pretty good, but often to minimize size in the pocket I don't see a case... In which case it feels much more safe than a regular slab phone with big glass area.  Day to day it's been a real pleasure to use.  My original intent was to swap SIM onto Pixel when I need the latter's functionality.  But I've found I use the RAzr 100 percent of time now.  I didn't go for 2025 Razr since only apparent plus was supposedly more secure fringe.... But the draw back is that the 2025 has a more slippery back.  Also came with Android 14 but easily upgraded to Android 15.  Couldn't be happier with this Mot!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was absolutely delighted when I first bought this phone; the color was exactly to my liking, and its compact, portable design meant I could slip it into my pocket—unlike other bulky phones—making it feel incredibly convenient. Because I really love this phone, I’ve taken very good care of it. However, less than a year and a half after purchasing it, the screen failed. During that period, I spent ten months abroad, which means I barely even used the phone at all; I never expected the build quality to be so poor. I’ve since consulted a repair technician, and I was told that the cost of replacing the screen is equivalent to buying a brand-new phone. I’d like to offer a word of advice to anyone considering this model: think twice before you buy. Furthermore—since this is a foldable phone—constantly opening and closing it places stress on the screen; eventually, you may find that cracks begin to appear. Honestly, I never never so disappointed to a phone

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: ALTSON 60 LED Portable 2500K-6500K Rechargeable Clip-On for Laptop, Makeup & VloggingALTSON 60 LED Portable 2500K-6500K Rechargeable Clip-On for Laptop, Makeup & Vlogging
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Stop Looking Underexposed on CameraIf your video calls look drab, your selfies are grainy, or your makeup tutorials lack true color, your cheap lighting solution isn't cutting it. This is the ultimate upgrade. The ALTSON 60 LED Portable Light is the pocket-sized powerhouse that gives you professional studio quality lighting without the huge price tag or complicated setup.Ease of Use: The Plug-and-Play Check-OffThe biggest win for this light is how fast and easy it is to deploy. You don't need a huge tripod or complex wiring; it's genuinely plug-and-play:Ease of Use CHECKED (Instant Setup): The multi-function clip instantly attaches to your phone, tablet, laptop webcam, or desktop monitor. It’s reliable and requires virtually no setup time, making it the perfect tool for streaming or professional calls where time is money.This light is specifically designed for serious content creators and professionals who need perfect lighting, fast. It seamlessly clips onto your phone, laptop, or camera, delivering the clarity and color accuracy that cheap lighting simply can't touch.The real secret to this light's power is the technical specification: CRI 97+ (Color Rendering Index). Most consumer lights fall short, making skin tones look drab and desaturated.Color Functionality Checked: A CRI of 97+ means this light provides Excellent color reproduction, colors appear as they would under natural daylight. This is a total game-changer for makeup application and photography, guaranteeing true-to-life skin tones and vibrant visuals, which is essential for beauty content where color matching is critical.Pro Lighting Functionality Checked: With 60 powerful LEDs, this unit is far brighter and more effective than smaller ring lights. It’s perfect for professional video conferencing, ensuring you look polished and bright during important Zoom meetings.The Control: Modes, Brightness, and TemperatureMaximum conversion comes from maximum control. The ALTSON light gives you nine lighting modes to perfectly tailor your look to any environment:Versatility Functionality Checked: You get 3 Light Modes (White, Natural, Warm) with a color temperature range adjustable from a cozy 2500K up to a crisp 6500K daylight. This lets you match warm indoor lighting or simulate bright outdoor sun.Precision Functionality Checked: With 10 levels of adjustable brightness, you can fine-tune your light output from a subtle glow to a powerful key light, making it suitable for everything from reading in bed to high-impact live streaming.Portability & Build Quality (The Creator's Must-Have)The best light is the one you actually use. This unit is built for the creator on the move:Mounting Functionality Checked: The multi-function design includes a heavy-duty clip that attaches to your phone, tablet, or laptop webcam, and a 1/4-inch thread adapter with a hot shoe mount for use with a tripod or camera. The 160° rotation means you can precisely position the light wherever you need it.Battery Functionality Checked: Equipped with a 2200mAh rechargeable battery, this light lasts about 4 hours at 50% brightness (and up to 15 hours at 10% brightness). No more being tethered to a wall socket! It's compact (weighing just 95g) and perfectly fits in a pocket or pouch.For creators, vloggers, or anyone who takes video calls seriously, the ALTSON 60 LED is the perfect blend of professional technical specs (CRI 97+, 2500K-6500K) and ultimate portability. It outperforms basic clip-on lights and is the essential tool for boosting your digital presence.Upgrade your lighting and elevate your content instantly.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Phenomenal design and quality for the price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The price point of this case and the sleek quality feel of the case is phenomenal it's not bulky cumbersome or intrusive in any way it's just a really sleek design very minimalist but still provides a decent level of protection.  if it came with the case alone it would be worth the asking price but it actually comes with a really nice glass screen protector as well or whatever it's made of it's very nice it was actually easy to install it so nice.I don't have any pictures of the case because it's currently on my phone but I ordered the Black version of the case. It's got a really soft to touch feel and again it feels very quality and very minimalist it's not intrusive in your pocket it doesn't weigh it down and make your phone which is already heavy enough even heavier it's got a very strong magsafe magnet on it which I use for a mag safe popsocket and it works quite well. It will protect your phone from average bumps bangs drops and falls I wouldn't test it any other thing over 3 ft though however for the price and for what you're ordering you know it's not going to be something that from three or four feet in the air it's going to protect your phone perfectly.I actually left my phone on top of my car the other day it's a fairly small CUV crossover about 5 ft tall of course I drove off and the phone with banging off the car it looks like there was significant damage done from the fall even on the corresponding corner of the case there was damage but I believe it was subsequently run over as it was waiting more demolished than it should have been however the case was still usable for the most part however the magsafe magnet did fall out that was kind of disappointing considering that I don't believe the case itself got run over I believe it was just the phone so I'm kind of surprised that it broke the bag safe magnet and popped it out but it is I guess I understandable it did get run over but my point is is that it's not the most solid durable case you're ever going to get your hands on but it also is less than a Happy meal at McDonald's and under normal circumstances in normal day to day use and abuse I believe it will handle just about anything you throw at it in a normal day. And that brings me to the screen protector that also comes with it at that super low price point it's such a nice little screen protector then it was actually easy to install I've installed about 20 screen protectors now and every time they're hard to get the bubbles out different things like that I've literally had them crack in my hand while I was try to squeeze the bubbles out but this thing just went on perfectly the first time and so far I'm I'm perfectly happy with it.If you're looking for a sleek minimalistic case to cover your phone and give you a little bit of protection so you can rest a little easier that is not going to hurt your pocket that is bag safe and will work with all bagsafe items and wireless charging magsafe stands all kinds of stuff look no further because this little bugger was a great buy

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Perfect for watching phone video on the plane
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I ordered this product specifically because I wanted a stand that was stable, robust, and could adjust to any reasonable viewing angle. It folds flat for putting in handbag etc. and opens up via two hinges to form a compact stand which allows any viewing angle from 0 -90 degrees from the horizontal. It also has enough clearance at the bottom to allow charging and/or headphone cable to be connected at the same time (which my previous one didn't) It came as a pack of two, and I only really needed one, but at under £10.00 the pair, I'm more than happy to have one as a spare/for office use. A much better product than I expected, and would happily recommend.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Between commuting during the week and taking my family on weekend road trips, I easily drive well over 600 miles every month. Over the years I've gone through more car phone mounts than I can count—cheap ones, expensive ones, windshield mounts, vent mounts—you name it. Unfortunately, they all seemed to have the same problems. The suction cup would eventually let go in the summer heat, the arms would loosen after a few weeks, or the vent clip would scratch my air vents. After enough disappointments, I wasn't expecting much from the VICSEED 3-in-1 Car Phone Holder. I figured if it could simply survive one hot summer without falling off, I'd be happy.After using it every day for almost one year, I can honestly say it has exceeded my expectations.The first thing I noticed was the overall build quality. The packaging is simple and practical, and inside the box everything is neatly organized. You get the main phone holder, an additional suction mounting base, a vent clip base, and a black dash-mount disk. Nothing feels cheap. The plastic has a premium texture, the joints feel sturdy, and the whole mount has a reassuring weight to it. Every adjustment point has just the right amount of resistance—not too stiff, but tight enough that it stays exactly where you position it.The biggest selling point is definitely the 3-in-1 mounting system. At first I thought it sounded more like marketing than something I'd actually use, but it turned out to be genuinely useful.I initially installed it on my windshield using the upgraded suction cup. The vacuum locking mechanism is extremely easy to use—just press it down and lock it in place. Once installed, it felt incredibly secure. I actually tried pulling it off by hand and it barely moved. Later I switched it to my dashboard, and it was just as solid.Most of the time, though, I use the vent mount because I like having cool air blow across my phone while running navigation during the summer. The vent clip is much better designed than the typical spring clips I've used before. Instead of simply pinching the vent, it uses a hook-style locking mechanism that grabs the vent blade securely. The silicone padding prevents scratches, and even after several weeks I haven't noticed any marks on my vents.I even tested it with a few hard stops and rough roads. My phone didn't shift at all. That honestly surprised me because my previous mount actually launched my phone onto the passenger seat after hitting a speed bump.Daily performance has been excellent.Part of my commute includes a stretch of road that's full of potholes and construction. With previous phone holders, my phone would shake so much that reading Google Maps became difficult. This one keeps the phone remarkably stable and never affects visibility.My biggest concern was how the suction cup would handle high temperatures. Summers where I live get extremely hot, and I've had several mounts fail simply because the adhesive softened under the heat. After nearly a year of daily use, including multiple hot afternoons parked outside, the suction cup hasn't budged once. Whether mounted on the windshield or dashboard, it has stayed exactly where I installed it.The quick-release button deserves special mention. One-handed operation is effortless. A simple press releases the phone, making it incredibly convenient when stopping for gas, grabbing coffee, or making a quick store run. Putting the phone back is just as easy, Press side arms and securely grip the phone without any fiddling.The adjustable ball joint is another feature I appreciate. Switching between portrait and landscape takes only a second, and once tightened, it actually stays in place. Unlike some cheaper mounts I've owned, it doesn't slowly droop while driving.Compatibility has also been excellent. I use a fairly large smartphone with a protective case, and it fits comfortably with room to spare. The clamp opens wide enough that I don't see most modern smartphones having any issues, even larger devices. The soft silicone pads on both the arms and back plate protect the phone from scratches while also eliminating annoying rattles over rough roads.Overall, I'm genuinely impressed with this phone mount. It delivers where it matters most: incredibly strong suction, outstanding stability, easy one-handed operation, and enough mounting options to work in almost any vehicle. More importantly, it gives me confidence that my phone will stay exactly where it belongs, whether I'm driving across town or taking my family on a long road trip.If you're tired of replacing flimsy car phone holders every few months and just want something dependable, this one is absolutely worth considering.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Functional but not without its flaws
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Purchased this for Colorado's hands-free law update regarding cell phones when driving.  Most of the time the suction cup portion of the mount will stay affixed to the windshield however with even minor to moderate temperature variations of 15° or more the suction cup will come loose, and it will happen even when you're driving which can of course be a potential hazard.It also comes with a vent mount clip if you prefer that instead and in my experience that might be great for summer months when you've got air conditioner blowing on your phone to be able to keep it cold so the battery won't overheat but in winter months when you're actually using your heater... That's just going to make your phone overheat that much faster especially with hard plastic or durable rubber cases like OtterBoxes which are already black and absorb a lot of heat...Also worth noting that the vent clip even when fully secured and tightened down the phone tilts significantly and depending on your vehicle layout there might not be a way to mount it safely on a vent that doesn't require you to take your eyes off the road to look at the screen which of course completely defeats the point.It gets the job done but it's not without its issues.Surprisingly it is quite durable considering how many times it's fallen off my windshield while driving with my phone in it and the plastic still has not broken thankfully.As far as compatibility goes I initially purchased it back when I had a Galaxy s22 Ultra in an OtterBox defender and it would hold the phone just fine and now I've got an S25 Ultra in an OtterBox defender and it still fits just fine.Regardless of the setup you choose it's relatively easy to mount either way, you just have to figure out what works for you.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve never had one of these before and if you’re new like I am, install it when you have actual time and not when you’re waiting in line at the drive thru. Since I wasn’t focused, it didn’t occur to me that it HAD to go on the bottom vent to be properly installed and remain stable. Obviously I figured it out the next time I tried, undistracted! When you get it right, it’s very easy to install and stays put. No big deal, I’d rather do than that have to remove it every single time just to use the holder.The ball joint does tend to come loose, it came loose and flopped around a little by the second or third use but maybe I just didn’t tighten it enough. I just tightened it again so we’ll see how long it lasts. Not the end of the world if it does continue to loosen from the weight/use since I can still get it at an angle that works but it would probably get annoying if you need the GPS for like Uber or roadtrips.Overall, it’s a great product, easy to install, easy to use, just some small flaws. Considering getting this brand but a different type for my husband (who does not have MagSafe) but I need to figure out what type would work best in his car.

Overall, this holder is reliable, well-made, and does exactly what I need it to do. And the price point is a fraction of the other ones I tried, which makes it even better.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good Spare Phone for the Price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The good, the bad and the ugly about the MIRO 4G phone. Note that I bought this phone to use strictly as a backup phone for traveling. I am not using this for my primary cell. So the good: lightweight (very important for me), USB-C, dual SIM, easy access to the SIMs, Micro SD card and battery as the back pops off, like the old days.  Also it does work in Europe (at least for my network) with a local EU SIM... Lastly the display is bright enough. The bad: it seems to be a bit slow. Not that I expected great performance, but it's an adjustment from a higher end cell. Also battery life doesn't seem great. Time will tell as it's still new and I can tweak the settings. Note that there is no NFC. If you like paying with your phone at a register and not pulling out cards, it doesn't have this feature. The ugly: The Amazon web description says there is fingerprint recognition under Add'l Details, there isn't. Under Device Unlock there is Screen Lock (ex: PIN, Password) and Face Detection but I didn't activate that. Perhaps it was an entry error. So it's a 4G phone with limitations, good as a 'get home phone' should something happen to my main phone and for the price, I don't have regrets.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My husband was very happy with this Kyocera flip phone because it reminded him of the old flip phones he used many years ago. It was easy for him to use and worked well at first. Unfortunately, after only about two weeks, the phone stopped working completely. We tried removing and reinserting the battery, charging it, resetting it, and performing several troubleshooting steps, but nothing helped. Sadly, we had to return the phone. It was a great concept for someone who prefers a simple flip phone, but the reliability was disappointing.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 30, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Kyocera DuraXA, Excellent flip phone! Rugged, great sound and good battery life.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This Kyocera DuraXA Unlocked flip phone is everything that Kyocera claims. It's tough, it has great volume (and yes, we haven't given it a dust or water bath) but it is supposed to be dust resistant and water-proof. It's battery lasts well and it's from a company that's known to make good, high-end products. My wife won't adjust to smart phones and does have a tendency to drop things, so this has good odds of lasting as long as 5G is the standard.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 21, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This phone is incredible!  It got soaked over night in a pants pocket, then washed the next day. Unbelievably this happened twice in two months. I thought it was dead. I left it in my hot car for two days thinking I’d remember to take it to a repair place. It dried out and started working again like it never happened!  Again, this happened twice. I bought an extra one as a backup, but will probably not have to use it. This phone truly lives up to its description!  BTW, it has also been dropped numerous times on concrete.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on September 12, 2025
